```py
class AttemptNotStarted(Exception):
    """The queen denied a reservation; no subprocess has been started."""
    def __init__(self, code="run_stopped", message=None):
        self.code = code
        super().__init__(message or code)


class AttemptHooks:
    def __call__(self, kind):
        raise NotImplementedError

    def finished(self, attempt_id, result):
        raise NotImplementedError


def parse_output(text):
    """Accept a JSON instance or one whole json fence. Never extract or repair."""
    text = text.strip()
    fence = re.fullmatch(r"```json\s*\n(.*?)\n```", text, re.DOTALL)
    if fence:
        text = fence[1]
    def pairs(items):
        result = {}
        for key, value in items:
            if key in result:
                raise ValueError("duplicate JSON key")
            result[key] = value
        return result
    def invalid_constant(value):
        raise ValueError("non-finite JSON number")
    value = json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=pairs, parse_constant=invalid_constant)
    if isinstance(value, dict) and ("$schema" in value or
            value.get("type") == "object" and "properties" in value):
        raise ValueError("schema wrapper instead of a JSON instance")
    return value


def matches_schema(value, schema):
    """Validate the shared Hive schema vocabulary, failing closed on unknown assertions."""
    if isinstance(schema, bool):
        return schema
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        return False
    supported = {"type", "properties", "required", "additionalProperties", "items", "enum", "const",
                 "anyOf", "oneOf", "allOf", "minimum", "maximum", "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum",
                 "minItems", "maxItems", "uniqueItems", "minLength", "maxLength", "pattern",
                 "minProperties", "maxProperties", "$schema", "title", "description", "default", "examples"}
    if set(schema) - supported:
        return False
    if "anyOf" in schema and not any(matches_schema(value, s) for s in schema["anyOf"]):
        return False
    if "oneOf" in schema and sum(matches_schema(value, s) for s in schema["oneOf"]) != 1:
        return False
    if "allOf" in schema and not all(matches_schema(value, s) for s in schema["allOf"]):
        return False
    if "enum" in schema and not any(type(value) is type(v) and value == v for v in schema["enum"]):
        return False
    if "const" in schema and (type(value) is not type(schema["const"]) or value != schema["const"]):
        return False
    types = schema.get("type", [])
    types = [types] if isinstance(types, str) else types
    kinds = {"object": isinstance(value, dict), "array": isinstance(value, list),
             "string": isinstance(value, str), "integer": type(value) is int,
             "number": type(value) is int or type(value) is float and math.isfinite(value),
             "boolean": type(value) is bool, "null": value is None}
    if types and not any(kinds.get(t, False) for t in types):
        return False
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        properties = schema.get("properties", {})
        if not set(schema.get("required", [])).issubset(value):
            return False
        extra = schema.get("additionalProperties", True)
        for key, child in value.items():
            if key in properties:
                if not matches_schema(child, properties[key]):
                    return False
            elif extra is False or isinstance(extra, dict) and not matches_schema(child, extra):
                return False
        if len(value) < schema.get("minProperties", 0) or len(value) > schema.get("maxProperties", float("inf")):
            return False
    if isinstance(value, list):
        if not all(matches_schema(v, schema.get("items", True)) for v in value):
            return False
        if len(value) < schema.get("minItems", 0) or len(value) > schema.get("maxItems", float("inf")):
            return False
        if schema.get("uniqueItems") and len({json.dumps(v, sort_keys=True) for v in value}) != len(value):
            return False
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if len(value) < schema.get("minLength", 0) or len(value) > schema.get("maxLength", float("inf")):
            return False
        if "pattern" in schema and re.search(schema["pattern"], value) is None:
            return False
    if type(value) in (int, float):
        if type(value) is float and not math.isfinite(value):
            return False
        if value < schema.get("minimum", -float("inf")) or value > schema.get("maximum", float("inf")):
            return False
        if "exclusiveMinimum" in schema and value <= schema["exclusiveMinimum"]:
            return False
        if "exclusiveMaximum" in schema and value >= schema["exclusiveMaximum"]:
            return False
    return True


def _prose(text):
    # Code, Markdown quotes and quoted examples are evidence, not a provider statement.
    text = re.sub(r"```.*?```", "", str(text or ""), flags=re.DOTALL)
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*>.*$", "", text)
    text = re.sub(r'"[^"\n]*"|“[^”\n]*”|`[^`\n]*`', "", text)
    return text


def is_refusal(*texts):
    for text in texts:
        if not isinstance(text, str):
            continue
        for line in _prose(text).splitlines():
            line = re.sub(r"(?i)\b(?:no|without|not a|not any)\s+(?:\w+\s+){0,3}(?:usage policy(?: violation)?|policy violation|content filter)\b", "", line)
            line = re.sub(r"(?i)\bnot refused by the model\b", "", line)
            if REFUSAL.search(line):
                return True
    return False


def _text_outcome(text):
    if str(text).lower() in ("refusal", "content_policy_violation", "safety_refusal", "content_filter", "usage_policy_violation"):
        return "provider_refusal"
    if is_refusal(text):
        return "provider_refusal"
    if re.search(r"(?i)invalid[_ -](?:schema|json)|structured_output_retries|json_schema_error", text or ""):
        return "invalid_schema"
    if re.search(r"(?i)\b(?:429|rate[_ -]?limit(?:ed|[_ -](?:exceeded|error))?|(?:insufficient[_ -])?quota(?:[_ -](?:exceeded|exhausted))?|too many requests)\b", text or ""):
        return "rate_limit"
    if re.search(r"(?i)context[_ -]?(?:(?:length|window)[_ -]?)?(?:limit|exceeded)|maximum context|too many (?:input )?tokens|prompt (?:is )?too long", text or ""):
        return "context_limit"
    return None


def terminal_signals(data):
    """Only explicit native status/code fields; messages are classified separately."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return []
    result = []
    for key in ("code", "status_code", "http_status", "stop_reason", "finish_reason", "codex_error_info"):
        signal = _text_outcome(str(data.get(key) or ""))
        if signal:
            result.append(signal)
    error = data.get("error")
    if isinstance(error, dict):
        result.extend(terminal_signals(error))
        signal = _text_outcome(str(error.get("type") or ""))
        if signal:
            result.append(signal)
    elif isinstance(error, str):
        signal = _text_outcome(error)
        if signal:
            result.append(signal)
    return result


def redact(text):
    text = str(text or "")
    key = r"(?:(?:[A-Za-z0-9]+_)*(?:api[_-]?key|auth[_-]?token|access[_-]?token|refresh[_-]?token|token|password|client[_-]?secret)|authorization|proxy-authorization|x-api-key)"
    text = re.sub(r"[\"']?(" + key + r")[\"']?\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']*[\"']", r'\1: "[REDACTED]"', text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    text = re.sub(r"(?i)(\b" + key + r"\s*[:=]\s*)(?:Bearer\s+)?[^\s,;\"}]+", r"\1[REDACTED]", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?i)\bBearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/-]+=*", "Bearer [REDACTED]", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?i)(--(?:api-key|token|password)\s+)\S+", r"\1[REDACTED]", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\b(?:sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}|gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\b", "[REDACTED]", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(https?://)[^/\s:@]+:[^/\s@]+@", r"\1[REDACTED]@", text)
    return text


def classify_result(*, terminal, assistant_text="", diagnostic="", output=None, schema):
    """Classify trusted terminal signals before diagnostics, prose and schema validation.

    terminal is normalized by each CLI: completed, timed_out, returncode, signals
    (outcome strings), error and optional code. Tool text never enters diagnostic.
    """
    terminal = terminal or {}
    wrapper = isinstance(output, dict) and ("$schema" in output or output.get("type") == "object" and "properties" in output)
    valid = isinstance(output, dict) and not wrapper and matches_schema(output, schema)
    signals = set(terminal.get("signals", [])) - {None}
    message = str(terminal.get("error") or diagnostic or "")
    code = terminal.get("code")
    if terminal.get("timed_out"):
        outcome, code = "timeout", "process_timeout"
    elif len(signals) > 1 or terminal.get("inconsistent"):
        outcome, code = "failure", "inconsistent_terminal"
    elif signals:
        outcome = next(iter(signals))
    elif _text_outcome(diagnostic):
        outcome = _text_outcome(diagnostic)
    elif not valid and _text_outcome(_prose(assistant_text)):
        outcome, message = _text_outcome(_prose(assistant_text)), assistant_text
    elif terminal.get("returncode", 0) or terminal.get("error"):
        outcome = "failure"
    elif not valid or not terminal.get("completed"):
        outcome, code = "invalid_schema", "invalid_output" if not valid else "incomplete_turn"
    else:
        outcome, code = "ok", None
    if outcome == "provider_refusal":
        # Preserve a refusal near the start even when a huge diagnostic follows it.
        source = message or assistant_text
        match = REFUSAL.search(source)
        if match:
            message = source[max(0, match.start() - 60):match.end() + 220]
    if outcome != "ok" and not message:
        message = assistant_text or ("answer does not match the bee's output schema" if not valid else "turn did not complete")
    native = redact(diagnostic)
    return {"schema": "hive.bee-result/1", "ok": outcome == "ok", "outcome": outcome,
            "output": output if outcome == "ok" else None,
            "error": None if outcome == "ok" else redact(message).strip()[:300],
            "seconds": 0, "refused": outcome == "provider_refusal", "code": code,
            "provenance": {}, "tool_rejections": None,
            "diagnostic": {"text": native[:4096], "truncated": len(native) > 4096,
                           "characters": len(native), "limit": 4096}}


def provenance(runner, role, name, attempt_id=None):
    env = runner.env or {}
    server = getattr(runner, "server", None) or env.get("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL")
    server_kind = "cloud"
    if server:
        host = urllib.parse.urlsplit(server).hostname
        try:
            loopback = ipaddress.ip_address(host).is_loopback
        except ValueError:
            loopback = host == "localhost"
        server_kind = "local" if loopback else "remote"
    return {"attempt_id": attempt_id, "logical_id": name, "kind": "bee", "role": role, "bee": name,
            "client": "codex" if hasattr(runner, "codex") else "claude",
            "server_kind": server_kind, "server": server,
            "requested_model": runner.model, "observed_model": None, "model_digest": None,
            "context_id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "origin": getattr(runner, "origin", "primary")}


def run_attempt(runner, role, name, operation, before_start=None, *, kind="bee"):
    # A denied hook propagates without a finished event or a subprocess.
    attempt_id = before_start(kind) if before_start is not None else None
    started = time.monotonic()
    metadata = provenance(runner, role, name, attempt_id)
    metadata["kind"] = kind
    try:
        result = operation()
    except AttemptNotStarted:
        raise
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        result = classify_result(terminal={"timed_out": True, "error": f"no answer within {runner.timeout} s"},
                                 diagnostic=str(error.stderr or ""), schema={})
        result["tool_rejections"] = getattr(error, "tool_rejections", None)
    except Exception as error:
        result = classify_result(terminal={"error": str(error), "returncode": 1},
                                 diagnostic=str(error), schema={})
    result["seconds"] = runner.timeout if result["outcome"] == "timeout" else round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
    result["provenance"] = metadata
    if before_start is not None:
        before_start.finished(attempt_id, result)
    return result


def json_events(stdout):
    try:
        value = json.loads(stdout or "")
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            return [value]
    except ValueError:
        pass
    events = []
    for line in (stdout or "").splitlines():
        try:
            value = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            events.append(value)
    return events


class ToolRejectionMonitor:
    """Read native MCP results; prose and other tools cannot change the streak."""
    def __init__(self, client, limit=None):
        self.client, self.limit = client, limit
        self.observed, self.total, self.consecutive = False, 0, 0
        self.names, self.seen, self.stop = {}, set(), None

    @staticmethod
    def schema_error(error):
        if isinstance(error, dict) and error.get("code") == -32602:
            return True
        return bool(re.search(r"(?i)invalid (?:arguments|params|parameters)|arguments must match.{0,80}schema"
                              r"|(?:input|argument|parameter) (?:schema|validation)|validation error"
                              r"|does not match.{0,80}schema", str(error)))

    def result(self, identity, name, rejected):
        self.observed = True
        if identity is not None:
            if identity in self.seen:
                return
            self.seen.add(identity)
        self.total += int(rejected)
        self.consecutive = self.consecutive + 1 if rejected else 0
        if self.limit is not None and self.consecutive >= self.limit and self.stop is None:
            self.stop = {"tool_name": name or None, "consecutive_tool_rejections": self.consecutive}

    def feed(self, event):
        if self.client == "claude":
            if event.get("type") not in ("assistant", "user"):
                return
            for block in event.get("message", {}).get("content", []):
                if not isinstance(block, dict):
                    continue
                if block.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    self.names[block.get("id")] = block.get("name", "")
                name = self.names.get(block.get("tool_use_id"), "")
                if block.get("type") == "tool_result" and name.startswith("mcp__"):
                    self.result(block.get("tool_use_id"), name,
                                bool(block.get("is_error") and self.schema_error(block.get("content", ""))))
        elif event.get("type", "").startswith("item."):
            item = event.get("item", {})
            if item.get("type") == "mcp_tool_call":
                if event.get("type") == "item.completed":
                    self.result(item.get("id"), item.get("tool") or item.get("name"),
                                bool(item.get("error") and self.schema_error(item["error"])))


def tool_rejections(events, *, client):
    """Count observed MCP argument/schema errors, never infer missing tool traces."""
    monitor = ToolRejectionMonitor(client)
    for event in events:
        monitor.feed(event)
    return monitor.total if monitor.observed else None


def run_cli(argv, *, input, cwd, env, capture_output, text, timeout, check,
            client, max_tool_rejections):
    """Capture both pipes live and stop only the POSIX session created for this CLI.

    No shell or preexec_fn: concurrent bees each own a distinct process group.
    Keep the leader unreaped until group signalling finishes, preventing PID reuse.
    """
    if os.name != "posix":
        raise OSError("live tool monitoring requires POSIX process groups")
    if not capture_output or not text or check:
        raise ValueError("run_cli requires text capture and check=False")
    monitor = ToolRejectionMonitor(client, max_tool_rejections)
    captured = {"stdout": bytearray(), "stderr": bytearray()}
    pending, payload, sent = bytearray(), input.encode("utf-8"), 0
    process = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                               stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True)
    deadline, stopped, timed_out = time.monotonic() + timeout, False, False
    drain_deadline = float("inf")

    def stop_group():
        # Reaping only happens below, after both signals target our original group.
        for signum in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGKILL):
            try:
                os.killpg(process.pid, signum)
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass
            except PermissionError:
                # Darwin reports EPERM for a group containing only zombies.
                # Accept it only with an unreaped, exited leader.
                if os.waitid(
                        os.P_PID, process.pid, os.WEXITED | os.WNOHANG | os.WNOWAIT) is None:
                    raise
            if signum == signal.SIGTERM:
                time.sleep(0.1)

    def events(data):
        for event in json_events(data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")):
            monitor.feed(event)

    try:
        with selectors.DefaultSelector() as selector:
            for pipe, name, mode in ((process.stdin, "stdin", selectors.EVENT_WRITE),
                                      (process.stdout, "stdout", selectors.EVENT_READ),
                                      (process.stderr, "stderr", selectors.EVENT_READ)):
                os.set_blocking(pipe.fileno(), False)
                selector.register(pipe, mode, name)
            while selector.get_map() and time.monotonic() < drain_deadline:
                if not stopped and (monitor.stop is not None or time.monotonic() >= deadline):
                    timed_out = monitor.stop is None
                    stop_group()
                    stopped = True
                    # Other sessions may retain inherited pipe writers. Bound
                    # our drain and close our read ends without signalling them.
                    drain_deadline = time.monotonic() + .25
                for key, _ in selector.select(min(.05, max(0, drain_deadline - time.monotonic()))):
                    pipe, name = key.fileobj, key.data
                    if name == "stdin":
                        try:
                            sent += os.write(pipe.fileno(), payload[sent:sent + 65536]) if sent < len(payload) else 0
                        except BrokenPipeError:
                            sent = len(payload)
                        if sent == len(payload):
                            selector.unregister(pipe)
                            pipe.close()
                        continue
                    data = os.read(pipe.fileno(), 65536)
                    if data:
                        captured[name].extend(data)
                        if name == "stdout":
                            pending.extend(data)
                            while b"\n" in pending:
                                line, _, rest = pending.partition(b"\n")
                                pending[:] = rest
                                events(line)
                                if monitor.stop is not None:
                                    break
                    else:
                        if name == "stdout" and pending:
                            events(pending)
                            pending.clear()
                        selector.unregister(pipe)
                        pipe.close()
                if monitor.stop is not None and not stopped:
                    stop_group()
                    stopped = True
                    drain_deadline = time.monotonic() + .25
            # A CLI may close its pipes before exiting. The deadline still applies.
            if not stopped:
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    timed_out = True
                    stop_group()
            process.wait()
    except BaseException:
        if process.returncode is None:
            stop_group()
            process.wait()
        raise
    finally:
        for pipe in (process.stdin, process.stdout, process.stderr):
            pipe.close()
    stdout, stderr = (captured[key].decode("utf-8", errors="replace") for key in ("stdout", "stderr"))
    if timed_out:
        error = subprocess.TimeoutExpired(argv, timeout, output=stdout, stderr=stderr)
        error.tool_rejections = tool_rejections(json_events(stdout), client=client)
        raise error
    result = subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)
    result.tool_schema_stop = monitor.stop
    return result


def tool_schema_result(completed):
    """Only the live controller can issue this outcome, never assistant prose."""
    stop = getattr(completed, "tool_schema_stop", None)
    if not isinstance(stop, dict):
        return None
    name = stop["tool_name"] or "unknown MCP tool"
    result = classify_result(terminal={"signals": ["tool_schema_failure"], "code": "tool_schema_failure",
                                      "error": f"Stopped after {stop['consecutive_tool_rejections']} consecutive "
                                               f"MCP argument/schema rejections ({name})"}, schema={})
    result.update(stop)
    return result


def capability_roundtrip(events, client, nonce):
    """Native tool evidence for check_model; no generated tool claims count."""
    pending = set()
    for event in events:
        if client == "claude":
            for block in event.get("message", {}).get("content", []):
                if not isinstance(block, dict):
                    continue
                if (event.get("type") == "assistant" and block.get("type") == "tool_use"
                        and block.get("name") == "Read"
                        and Path(str(block.get("input", {}).get("file_path", ""))).name == "capability-input.json"):
                    pending.add(block.get("id"))
                if (event.get("type") == "user" and block.get("type") == "tool_result"
                        and block.get("tool_use_id") in pending and not block.get("is_error")
                        and nonce in str(block.get("content", ""))):
                    return True
        elif event.get("type") == "item.completed":
            item = event.get("item", {})
            if item.get("type") != "command_execution" or item.get("exit_code") != 0:
                continue
            try:
                argv = shlex.split(item.get("command", ""))
                if len(argv) == 3 and Path(argv[0]).name in ("sh", "bash", "zsh") and argv[1] in ("-c", "-lc"):
                    argv = shlex.split(argv[2])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if (len(argv) == 2 and Path(argv[0]).name == "cat" and Path(argv[1]).name == "capability-input.json"
                    and nonce in str(item.get("aggregated_output", ""))):
                return True
    return False


def brief(role, task):
    """The shared role-card prefix first (identical across sibling bees), the task last."""
    common = (ROLES / COMMON).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    card = (ROLES / f"{role if role != 'repair' else 'worker'}.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    return f"{common}\n\n{card}\n\n# Your task\n\n{task}\n"


class ClaudeBees:
    """Run each bee as `claude -p` in its own folder with its own ReverseAI MCP server."""

    def __init__(self, *, engine, inputs, enabled=("ghidra",), claude="claude", model=None, effort=None,
                 timeout=2400, python=sys.executable, config_dir, env=None, max_tool_rejections=8):
        if type(max_tool_rejections) is not int or max_tool_rejections < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_tool_rejections must be a positive integer")
        self.max_tool_rejections = max_tool_rejections
        self.engine, self.inputs, self.enabled = str(engine), str(inputs), tuple(enabled)
        self.claude, self.model, self.effort, self.timeout, self.python = claude, model, effort, timeout, python
        self.config_dir = Path(config_dir)
        self.env = env  # None inherits this process's environment; hive.selfhost sets a self-hosted one

    def _mcp_config(self, name):
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", name):
            raise ValueError("invalid bee name")
        self.config_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path = self.config_dir / f"{name}.json"
        env = {"PYTHONPATH": self.engine, "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"}
        args = ["-B", "-m", "reverseai", "mcp", "--inputs", self.inputs, *("--with-" + t for t in self.enabled)]
        path.write_text(json.dumps({"mcpServers": {"reverseai": {
            "type": "stdio", "command": self.python, "args": args, "env": env}}}, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def argv(self, role, name, *, schema=None):
        tools = TOOLSETS[role]
        argv = [self.claude, "-p", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--json-schema", json.dumps(SCHEMAS[role] if schema is None else schema),
                "--mcp-config", str(self._mcp_config(name)), "--strict-mcp-config",
                "--tools", ",".join(tools), "--permission-mode", "dontAsk", "--no-session-persistence",
                "--allowedTools", "mcp__reverseai__*", *(f"{tool}(./**)" for tool in tools)]
        if self.model:
            argv[2:2] = ["--model", self.model]
        if self.effort:
            argv[2:2] = ["--effort", self.effort]
        return argv

    def __call__(self, role, name, task, folder, *, schema=None, before_start=None):
        expected = SCHEMAS[role] if schema is None else schema
        def execute():
            completed = run_cli(self.argv(role, name, schema=schema), input=brief(role, task),
                                       cwd=folder, env=self.env, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                       timeout=self.timeout, check=False, client="claude",
                                       max_tool_rejections=self.max_tool_rejections)
            events = json_events(completed.stdout)
            finals = [e for e in events if e.get("type") == "result"]
            # Retain compatibility with a captured --output-format json result.
            if not finals and len(events) == 1 and any(k in events[0] for k in ("structured_output", "result", "is_error")):
                finals = events
            data = finals[-1] if finals else {}
            assistant_errors = [str(e["error"]) for e in events if e.get("type") == "assistant" and e.get("error")]
            has_error = bool(data.get("is_error") or data.get("error") or assistant_errors
                             or str(data.get("subtype", "")).startswith("error_"))
            assistant = str(data.get("result") or "")
            if not assistant:
                assistant = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for e in events if e.get("type") == "assistant"
                                      for b in e.get("message", {}).get("content", []) if b.get("type") == "text")
            output = data.get("structured_output")
            if output is None:
                try:
                    output = parse_output(assistant)
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    pass
            signals = []
            for e in events:
                if e.get("type") in ("assistant", "result"):
                    signals.extend(terminal_signals(e))
                    message = e.get("message", {}) if e.get("type") == "assistant" else e
                    signals.extend(terminal_signals(message))
                    if any(isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "refusal" for b in message.get("content", [])):
                        signals.append("provider_refusal")
                if e.get("type") == "result" and e.get("is_error"):
                    signal = _text_outcome(str(e.get("subtype") or ""))
                    if signal:
                        signals.append(signal)
            native = "\n".join(filter(None, [completed.stderr, str(data.get("subtype") or "") if has_error else "",
                                               assistant if has_error else "", str(data.get("error") or ""), *assistant_errors]))
            terminal = {"completed": bool(finals) and not has_error, "signals": signals,
                        "returncode": completed.returncode}
            if has_error:
                terminal["error"] = assistant or str(data.get("error") or data.get("subtype") or "agent failed")
            result = classify_result(terminal=terminal, assistant_text=assistant,
                                     diagnostic=native, output=output, schema=expected)
            result = tool_schema_result(completed) or result
            result.update(turns=data.get("num_turns"), cost_usd=data.get("total_cost_usd"),
                          tool_rejections=tool_rejections(events, client="claude"))
            if hasattr(self, "_capability_nonce"):
                result["capability_tool_roundtrip"] = capability_roundtrip(events, "claude", self._capability_nonce)
            if hasattr(self, "_capability_mcp"):
                from hive import selfhost
                result["capability_mcp_tool"] = selfhost.mcp_tool_accepted(events, "claude", self._capability_mcp)
            return result
        return run_attempt(self, role, name, execute, before_start)


def environment_ok(claude="claude"):
    """True when the agent CLI can be found; the run itself proves the login."""
    return any((Path(p) / claude).is_file() for p in os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep)) or Path(claude).is_file()
```

`hive/codex_bees.py`:

```py
"""Codex bees and mixed Claude/Codex councils.

Codex bees have a shell, can read the disk and can execute programs. On macOS,
codex-cli 0.165.0 allowed network access through `codex exec` in both sandbox modes,
despite network_access=false; `codex sandbox` blocked the same command. A preliminary
probe decides whether each sandbox mode may run bees; an inconclusive probe refuses
them. This reachability check is not a guarantee of isolation against every destination.
An explicit --codex-allow-network opt-out warns on every result. Use Codex bees only
for software the operator would run anyway, never for malware.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import re
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path
from hive import bees as bees_module

from hive.bees import (REFUSAL, SCHEMAS, brief, is_refusal, AttemptNotStarted, classify_result,
                       matches_schema, parse_output, json_events, tool_rejections, run_attempt,
                       provenance, _text_outcome, capability_roundtrip, terminal_signals)

NETWORK_REFUSAL = "Codex sandbox allowed network access; Codex bees refused"
NETWORK_WARNING = "Codex bees ran without network isolation"
NETWORK_COMMAND = "curl --max-time 5 --silent --show-error --output /dev/null https://example.com"
NETWORK_SCHEMA = {"type": "object", "properties": {"exit_code": {"type": "integer"}},
                  "required": ["exit_code"], "additionalProperties": False}
NETWORK_TASK = ("Network isolation probe. Run exactly this shell command once, with no extra commands, "
                "wrappers, redirections or file reads:\n" + NETWORK_COMMAND
                + "\nReport its actual exit code. Never invent a result or substitute another command. "
                "If execution is unavailable, report -1.")


def strict_schema(schema):
    """Require every object property, allowing null for originally optional fields."""
    if isinstance(schema, list):
        return [strict_schema(item) for item in schema]
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        return schema
    result = {key: strict_schema(value) for key, value in schema.items()}
    if schema.get("type") == "object" or isinstance(schema.get("type"), list) and "object" in schema["type"]:
        required = schema.get("required", [])
        result["properties"] = {
            key: value if key in required else {"anyOf": [value, {"type": "null"}]}
            for key, value in result.get("properties", {}).items()
        }
        result["required"] = list(result["properties"])
        result["additionalProperties"] = False
    return result


def drop_nulls(value):
    """Restore omitted optional object fields without changing array positions."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: drop_nulls(item) for key, item in value.items() if item is not None}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [drop_nulls(item) for item in value]
    return value


def _matches(value, schema):
    return matches_schema(value, schema)


def restore_optionals(value, schema):
    """Remove only null placeholders introduced for optional fields in the wire schema."""
    for keyword in ("anyOf", "oneOf"):
        if keyword in schema:
            branch = next((s for s in schema[keyword] if matches_schema(value, strict_schema(s))), None)
            if branch is not None:
                return restore_optionals(value, branch)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        properties, required = schema.get("properties", {}), schema.get("required", [])
        return {key: restore_optionals(item, properties.get(key, {})) for key, item in value.items()
                if item is not None or key in required}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [restore_optionals(item, schema.get("items", {})) for item in value]
    return value


class BeeExecutionError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, result):
        self.result = result
        super().__init__(result["error"])


class ProviderRefusal(ValueError):
    """Codex ended because the model provider refused the request."""


def failure_messages(stdout):
    """Messages of the error events in `codex exec --json` output; tool output never counts."""
    messages = []
    for line in (stdout or "").splitlines():
        try:
            event = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if not isinstance(event, dict):
            continue
        if event.get("type") == "error":
            messages.append(str(event.get("message", "")))
        elif event.get("type") == "turn.failed":
            error = event.get("error")
            messages.append(str(error.get("message", "") if isinstance(error, dict) else error))
    return messages


def refusal_excerpt(*texts):
    """The text around the first provider refusal in any of the texts, or an empty string."""
    for text in texts:
        match = REFUSAL.search(text) if isinstance(text, str) else None
        if match:
            return " ".join(text[max(0, match.start() - 120):match.end() + 120].split())
    return ""


class CodexBees:
    """One non-interactive Codex process and ReverseAI MCP server per named bee."""

    def __init__(self, *, engine, inputs, enabled=("ghidra",), codex="codex", model=None, effort=None,
                 timeout=2400, python=sys.executable, config_dir, allow_network=False, env=None, max_tool_rejections=8):
        if type(max_tool_rejections) is not int or max_tool_rejections < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_tool_rejections must be a positive integer")
        self.max_tool_rejections = max_tool_rejections
        self.env = env  # None inherits this process's environment; hive.selfhost sets a self-hosted one
        self.engine, self.inputs = str(Path(engine).resolve()), str(Path(inputs).resolve())
        self.enabled, self.codex, self.model = tuple(enabled), codex, model
        self.effort, self.timeout, self.python = effort, timeout, str(python)
        self.config_dir = Path(config_dir).resolve()
        self.allow_network = allow_network
        self._network_checks = {}
        self._network_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._network_local = threading.local()

    def _paths(self, name):
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", name):
            raise ValueError("invalid bee name")
        return self.config_dir / f"{name}.schema.json", self.config_dir / f"{name}.output.json"

    def argv(self, role, name, folder, *, schema=None):
        schema_path, output_path = self._paths(name)
        self.config_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        schema_path.write_text(json.dumps(strict_schema(SCHEMAS[role]) if schema is None else schema),
                               encoding="utf-8")
        output_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)  # A failed retry must not reuse an earlier answer.
        mcp_args = ["-B", "-m", "reverseai", "mcp", "--inputs", self.inputs,
                    *("--with-" + tool for tool in self.enabled)]
        mcp = ("mcp_servers={reverseai={command=" + json.dumps(self.python)
               + ",args=" + json.dumps(mcp_args) + ",env={PYTHONPATH=" + json.dumps(self.engine)
               + ',PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1"}}}')
        argv = [self.codex, "exec", "--ignore-user-config", "--skip-git-repo-check", "--ephemeral", "--json",
                "-C", str(Path(folder).resolve()), "--sandbox",
                "read-only" if role == "councillor" else "workspace-write",
                "-c", 'approval_policy="never"', "-c", "sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=false",
                "-c", "sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=[]",
                "-c", "sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_tmpdir_env_var=true",
                "-c", "sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_slash_tmp=true", "-c", 'web_search="disabled"',
                "-c", mcp, "--output-schema", str(schema_path), "-o", str(output_path)]
        if self.model:
            argv += ["-m", self.model]
        if self.effort:
            argv += ["-c", "model_reasoning_effort=" + json.dumps(self.effort)]
        return [*argv, "-"]

    def _execute(self, role, name, task, folder, *, schema=None):
        expected = SCHEMAS[role] if schema is None else schema
        wire_schema = strict_schema(expected) if schema is None else schema
        completed = bees_module.run_cli(self.argv(role, name, folder, schema=wire_schema), input=task, cwd=folder,
                                       env=self.env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=self.timeout, check=False,
                                       client="codex", max_tool_rejections=self.max_tool_rejections)
        events = json_events(completed.stdout)
        errors = failure_messages(completed.stdout)
        signals = []
        for event in events:
            if event.get("type") in ("error", "turn.failed"):
                signals.extend(terminal_signals(event))
                error = event.get("error", event)
                if isinstance(error, dict):
                    native_code = str(error.get("code") or error.get("type") or "")
                    signal = _text_outcome(native_code)
                    if signal:
                        signals.append(signal)
        finished = any(e.get("type") == "turn.completed" for e in events)
        failed = any(e.get("type") == "turn.failed" for e in events)
        terminal = {"completed": finished and not errors, "returncode": completed.returncode,
                    "signals": signals, "inconsistent": finished and failed}
        native = "\n".join(filter(None, [completed.stderr, *errors]))
        if errors or completed.returncode:
            terminal["error"] = f"exit {completed.returncode}: {native or 'agent failed'}" if completed.returncode else native
        assistant = "\n".join(str(e.get("item", {}).get("text", "")) for e in events
                              if e.get("type") == "item.completed" and e.get("item", {}).get("type") == "agent_message")
        _, output_path = self._paths(name)
        output = None
        try:
            output = parse_output(output_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
        result = classify_result(terminal=terminal, assistant_text=assistant, diagnostic=native,
                                 output=output, schema=wire_schema)
        result = bees_module.tool_schema_result(completed) or result
        result["tool_rejections"] = tool_rejections(events, client="codex")
        if hasattr(self, "_capability_nonce"):
            result["capability_tool_roundtrip"] = capability_roundtrip(events, "codex", self._capability_nonce)
        if hasattr(self, "_capability_mcp"):
            from hive import selfhost
            result["capability_mcp_tool"] = selfhost.mcp_tool_accepted(events, "codex", self._capability_mcp)
        if not result["ok"]:
            raise BeeExecutionError(result)
        completed.bee_result = result
        return completed, output

    def probe_key(self, role):
        mode = "read-only" if role == "councillor" else "workspace-write"
        payload = {"client": "codex", "server": getattr(self, "server", None), "model": self.model,
                   "executable": self.codex, "mode": mode, "network_access": False,
                   "writable_roots": [], "exclude_tmpdir_env_var": True, "exclude_slash_tmp": True,
                   "web_search": "disabled", "effort": self.effort}
        return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()

    def _network_ok(self, role, folder, *, before_start=None):
        key = self.probe_key(role)
        mode = "read-only" if role == "councillor" else "workspace-write"
        with self._network_lock:
            self._network_local.result = None
            if key not in self._network_checks:
                def probe():
                    try:
                        completed, output = self._execute(role, f"network-probe-{mode}", NETWORK_TASK,
                                                          folder, schema=NETWORK_SCHEMA)
                    except BeeExecutionError as error:
                        return error.result
                    events = json_events(completed.stdout)
                    commands = [event["item"] for event in events if event.get("type") == "item.completed"
                                and event.get("item", {}).get("type") == "command_execution"]
                    isolated = False
                    if len(commands) == 1:
                        command = commands[0]
                        argv = shlex.split(command["command"])
                        if (len(argv) == 3 and Path(argv[0]).name in ("sh", "bash", "zsh")
                                and argv[1] in ("-c", "-lc")):
                            argv = shlex.split(argv[2])
                        isolated = (argv == shlex.split(NETWORK_COMMAND)
                                    and type(command.get("exit_code")) is int and command["exit_code"] in (6, 7)
                                    and output["exit_code"] == command["exit_code"]
                                    and any(event.get("type") == "turn.completed" for event in events))
                    if not isolated:
                        return classify_result(terminal={"signals": ["failure"], "code": "network_isolation",
                                                        "error": NETWORK_REFUSAL}, schema={})
                    return getattr(completed, "bee_result", classify_result(
                        terminal={"completed": True}, output=output, schema=NETWORK_SCHEMA))
                result = run_attempt(self, role, f"network-probe-{mode}", probe, before_start, kind="network_probe")
                self._network_local.result = result
                self._network_checks[key] = result["ok"]
            return self._network_checks[key]

    def __call__(self, role, name, task, folder, *, schema=None, before_start=None):
        try:
            self._paths(name)
            if role not in SCHEMAS:
                raise ValueError(f"unknown bee role: {role}")
        except ValueError as error:
            result = classify_result(terminal={"error": str(error), "code": "configuration", "returncode": 1}, schema={})
            result["provenance"] = provenance(self, role, name)
            return result
        if not self.allow_network:
            # Keep the isolated adapter's historical two-argument probe seam.
            allowed = (self._network_ok(role, folder) if before_start is None else
                       self._network_ok(role, folder, before_start=before_start))
            if not allowed:
                result = classify_result(terminal={"signals": ["failure"], "code": "network_isolation",
                                                   "error": NETWORK_REFUSAL}, schema={})
                probe = getattr(self._network_local, "result", None)
                if probe is not None:
                    result["provenance"] = dict(probe["provenance"])
                    result["probe_outcome"] = probe["outcome"]
                    result["seconds"] = probe["seconds"]
                    for field in ("tool_rejections", "tool_name", "consecutive_tool_rejections"):
                        if field in probe:
                            result[field] = probe[field]
                else:
                    result["provenance"] = provenance(self, role, name)
                    result["provenance"]["context_id"] = None
                return result
        def execute():
            try:
                kwargs = {} if schema is None else {"schema": schema}
                completed, output = self._execute(role, name, brief(role, task), folder, **kwargs)
                result = getattr(completed, "bee_result", classify_result(
                    terminal={"completed": True}, output=output,
                    schema=strict_schema(SCHEMAS[role]) if schema is None else schema))
                if result["ok"] and schema is None:
                    result["output"] = restore_optionals(output, SCHEMAS[role])
            except BeeExecutionError as error:
                result = error.result
            except ProviderRefusal as error:
                result = classify_result(terminal={"signals": ["provider_refusal"], "error": str(error)}, schema={})
            if self.allow_network:
                result["warning"] = NETWORK_WARNING
            return result
        result = run_attempt(self, role, name, execute, before_start)
        if self.allow_network:
            result["warning"] = NETWORK_WARNING
        return result


class MixedBees:
    """Alternate module builders and give the other model two of three council seats."""

    def __init__(self, claude, codex, policy="mixed"):
        if policy not in ("claude", "codex", "mixed"):
            raise ValueError("bee policy must be claude, codex or mixed")
        self.claude, self.codex, self.policy = claude, codex, policy

    def runner(self, role, name):
        if self.policy != "mixed":
            runner = self.claude if self.policy == "claude" else self.codex
        elif role in ("planner", "tester") or (role == "repair" and re.fullmatch(r"behaviour-fix-\d+", name)):
            runner = self.claude
        else:
            pattern = (r"m(\d+)-council-r\d+-(control|io|data)" if role == "councillor" else
                       r"m(\d+)-build" if role == "worker" else
                       r"m(\d+)-repair-[bcl]\d+" if role == "repair" else "")
            match = re.fullmatch(pattern, name) if pattern else None
            if not match or int(match[1]) < 1:
                raise ValueError("cannot route bee role/name in mixed policy")
            use_claude = int(match[1]) % 2 == 1
            if role == "councillor" and match[2] in ("control", "io"):
                use_claude = not use_claude
            runner = self.claude if use_claude else self.codex
        return runner

    def __call__(self, role, name, task, folder, *, schema=None, before_start=None):
        try:
            runner = self.runner(role, name)
        except ValueError as error:
            return classify_result(terminal={"error": str(error), "returncode": 1}, schema={})
        kwargs = {}
        if schema is not None:
            kwargs["schema"] = schema
        if before_start is not None:
            kwargs["before_start"] = before_start
        return runner(role, name, task, folder, **kwargs)


def add_arguments(parser):
    parser.add_argument("--bee-policy", choices=("claude", "codex", "mixed"), default="claude",
                        help="Bee models: Claude only, Codex only, or alternating builders and mixed councils")
    parser.add_argument("--codex", default="codex", help="Codex CLI executable")
    parser.add_argument("--codex-model", help="Model for Codex bees (default: Codex CLI's default)")
    parser.add_argument("--codex-effort", help="Reasoning effort for Codex bees")
    parser.add_argument("--codex-allow-network", action="store_true",
                        help="Accept Codex network access: skip the isolation probe and warn on every bee result")
    from hive import selfhost
    selfhost.add_arguments(parser)


def build(args, claude_runner, **runner_kwargs):
    """Build from CLI options; kwargs are CodexBees' shared engine/input/config settings."""
    from hive import selfhost
    runner, extra = selfhost.apply(args, claude_runner)
    if args.bee_policy == "claude":
        return claude_runner
    codex = runner(**dict(runner_kwargs, codex=args.codex, model=args.codex_model, effort=args.codex_effort,
                          allow_network=args.codex_allow_network), **extra)
    return codex if args.bee_policy == "codex" else MixedBees(claude_runner, codex, args.bee_policy)


def build_router(args, claude_runner, **runner_kwargs):
    """Configure routing only. The queen owns fallback activation and attempts."""
    from hive.selfhost import BeeRouter
    return BeeRouter(args, claude_runner, runner_kwargs)
```

`hive/fuzz.py`:

```py
"""Deterministic file mutations and reports; execution stays in queen.run_cases."""

import base64
import copy
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random
import re

MAX_MUTANTS = 500
ATTEMPTS_PER_MUTANT = 20
MUTATORS = ("bitflip", "insert", "delete", "truncate", "boundary", "splice")
BOUNDARIES = (0x00, 0xff, 0x7f, 0x80)


def count(value):
    """Validate both the command-line count and the Python keyword."""
    if isinstance(value, str) and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", value):
        value = int(value)
    if type(value) is not int or not 0 <= value <= MAX_MUTANTS:
        raise ValueError(f"fuzz count must be between 0 and {MAX_MUTANTS}")
    return value


def mutate(data, operation, rng, max_file_size, other=b""):
    """Apply one bounded byte operation; arguments and filenames are never involved."""
    data = data[:max_file_size]
    if operation == "bitflip":
        if not data:
            result = bytes([1 << rng.randrange(8)])
        else:
            at = rng.randrange(len(data))
            result = data[:at] + bytes([data[at] ^ (1 << rng.randrange(8))]) + data[at + 1:]
    elif operation == "insert":
        at = rng.randrange(len(data) + 1)
        result = data[:at] + bytes([rng.randrange(256)]) + data[at:]
    elif operation == "delete":
        at = rng.randrange(len(data)) if data else 0
        result = data[:at] + data[at + 1:]
    elif operation == "truncate":
        result = data[:rng.randrange(len(data))] if data else b""
    elif operation == "boundary":
        at = rng.randrange(len(data)) if data else 0
        choices = [value for value in BOUNDARIES if not data or value != data[at]]
        result = data[:at] + bytes([rng.choice(choices)]) + data[at + 1:]
    elif operation == "splice":
        other = other[:max_file_size]
        result = data[:rng.randrange(len(data) + 1)] + other[rng.randrange(len(other) + 1):]
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown fuzz mutator: {operation}")
    return result[:max_file_size]


def _written_name(name):
    """A file's relative destination in the fresh case folder, or None when run_cases skips it."""
    path = Path(name)
    if path.is_absolute() or path.drive:
        return None
    parts = []
    for part in path.parts:
        if part == "..":
            if not parts:
                return None
            parts.pop()
        elif part != ".":
            parts.append(part)
    return str(Path(*parts)) if parts else None


def _input_key(case):
    # Later entries for the same destination overwrite earlier ones before any step runs.
    files = {_written_name(item["name"]): item["base64"] for item in case["files"]}
    steps = [{"args": step["args"], "stdin": step.get("stdin")} for step in case["steps"]]
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([files, steps], sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).digest()


def generate(cases, input_sha256, total, max_file_size):
    """At most total fresh case IDs, seeded by the input hash and each normalised source ID."""
    total = count(total)
    if not total:
        return []
    if not isinstance(input_sha256, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{64}", input_sha256):
        raise ValueError("fuzzing needs the input SHA-256")
    if type(max_file_size) is not int or max_file_size < 1:
        raise ValueError("fuzz file cap must be positive")
    reserved, sources, seen = set(), [], set()
    for case in cases:
        if not isinstance(case.get("id"), str):
            raise ValueError("fuzz source cases need string IDs")
        name = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", case["id"])[:64]
        if not name or name in reserved:
            raise ValueError("fuzz source IDs must be unique after normalisation")
        reserved.add(name)
        source = copy.deepcopy(case)
        source["id"] = name
        kept, data, destinations = [], [], {}
        for item in case.get("files", []):
            destination = _written_name(item["name"])
            if destination is None:
                continue  # Match run_cases: an escaping entry is not decoded or written.
            destinations[destination] = len(kept)
            kept.append(item)
            data.append((base64.b64decode(item["base64"]) if item.get("base64")
                         else item.get("text", "").encode())[:max_file_size])
        source["files"] = [{"name": item["name"], "base64": base64.b64encode(content).decode("ascii")}
                           for item, content in zip(kept, data)]
        seen.add(_input_key(source))
        if data:
            seed = hashlib.sha256(f"hive-fuzz-v1\0{input_sha256.lower()}\0{name}".encode()).digest()
            sources.append((source, data, random.Random(int.from_bytes(seed, "big")), tuple(destinations.values())))
    sources.sort(key=lambda item: item[0]["id"])
    if not sources:
        return []
    operations = MUTATORS if len(sources) > 1 else MUTATORS[:-1]
    mutants, sequence = [], 1
    visits = list(range(len(sources)))
    for attempt in range(total * ATTEMPTS_PER_MUTANT):
        if len(mutants) == total:
            break
        index = attempt % len(sources)
        source, files, rng, written = sources[index]
        operation = operations[visits[index] % len(operations)]
        visits[index] += 1  # An independent cycle for each source, including rejected attempts.
        at, other = rng.choice(written), b""
        if operation == "splice":
            donors = [contents[index] for case, contents, _, active in sources
                      if case["id"] != source["id"] for index in active]
            other = rng.choice(donors)
        mutant = copy.deepcopy(source)
        changed = mutate(files[at], operation, rng, max_file_size, other)
        mutant["files"][at]["base64"] = base64.b64encode(changed).decode("ascii")
        identity = _input_key(mutant)
        if identity in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(identity)
        while True:
            suffix = f"-{sequence}"
            name = "fz-" + source["id"][:64 - 3 - len(suffix)] + suffix
            sequence += 1
            if name not in reserved:
                break
        reserved.add(name)
        mutant["id"] = name
        mutants.append(mutant)
    return mutants


def summarise(cases, original, rebuilt, seed, compare):
    """Compare every complete pair, keeping missing or timed-out mutants separate."""
    def complete(case, executions):
        row = executions.get(case["id"]) if isinstance(executions, dict) else None
        steps = row.get("steps") if isinstance(row, dict) else None
        return (bool(case.get("steps")) and isinstance(steps, list) and len(steps) == len(case["steps"])
                and all(isinstance(step, dict) and type(step.get("code")) is int for step in steps))
    unique = len({case["id"] for case in cases}) == len(cases)
    completed, incomplete = [], []
    for case in cases:
        target = completed if unique and complete(case, original) and complete(case, rebuilt) else incomplete
        target.append(case["id"])
    same, different = compare({key: original[key] for key in completed}, {key: rebuilt[key] for key in completed})
    result = {"cases": len(cases), "completed": len(completed), "identical": len(same), "different": different,
              "incomplete": incomplete, "seed": seed, "ran": bool(cases) and not incomplete}
    if incomplete:
        result["reason"] = f"{len(incomplete)} fuzz mutant(s) incomplete or timed out: " + ", ".join(incomplete)
    elif not cases:
        result["reason"] = "no distinct mutants (no case files or attempts exhausted)"
    return result


def write_report(path, summary, cases):
    """Keep bounded reproduction inputs for differing and incomplete mutants."""
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    retained = set(summary["different"]) | set(summary.get("incomplete", []))
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(dict(summary, inputs=[case for case in cases if case["id"] in retained]), handle,
                  indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
        handle.write("\n")

```

`hive/languages.py`:

```py
"""Target languages for the hive: what the bees write and how the queen compiles it.

The hive rebuilds a native program in the language it was most likely written in: C, or
C++ when the program map shows C++ (mangled or qualified names, the C++ runtime's imports).
The operator can force either. Other languages (Java for Android apps, ports to Rust, Go
or Python) are not handled yet.
"""

import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Language:
    name: str
    label: str
    extension: str
    header: str
    compiler_env: str
    compiler: str
    standard: str
    syntax_kind: str
    guidance: str

    def cc(self):
        return os.environ.get(self.compiler_env, self.compiler)

    def source(self, module_id):
        return f"{module_id}{self.extension}"


C = Language(
    name="c", label="C", extension=".c", header="contract.h", compiler_env="CC", compiler="cc",
    standard="-std=gnu11", syntax_kind="c",
    guidance="Write C (C11 with GNU extensions allowed). Use plain structs and functions.")
CPP = Language(
    name="cpp", label="C++", extension=".cpp", header="contract.hpp", compiler_env="CXX", compiler="c++",
    standard="-std=gnu++17", syntax_kind="c++",
    guidance=("Write C++17. Rebuild classes with the member layout the assembly shows and pin it with "
              "static_assert(offsetof(...)) and static_assert(sizeof(...)); declare virtual methods in the "
              "vtable order the assembly uses; keep constructors, destructors, exceptions and the standard "
              "library types the binary links (std::string, std::vector, ...) only where the evidence shows them. "
              "Free functions and static members get the names the contract gives them."))
LANGUAGES = {"c": C, "cpp": CPP}

_MANGLED = re.compile(r"^_{1,2}Z[A-Za-z0-9_]")
_CPP_RUNTIME = ("__cxa_throw", "__cxa_begin_catch", "__cxa_allocate_exception", "__gxx_personality_v0",
                "_Unwind_Resume", "__cxa_atexit", "__cxa_guard_acquire", "__dynamic_cast")
_CPP_OPERATORS = ("_Znwm", "_Znam", "_ZdlPv", "_ZdaPv", "_Znwj", "_ZdlPvm")


def detect(program_map):
    """Return ("c" or "cpp", reasons) from the names and imports in the program map."""
    names = [f.get("name") or "" for f in program_map.get("functions", [])]
    imports = [i.lstrip("_") for i in program_map.get("imports", [])]
    reasons = []
    mangled = sum(1 for n in names + program_map.get("imports", []) if _MANGLED.match(n))
    if mangled:
        reasons.append(f"{mangled} mangled C++ names")
    qualified = sum(1 for n in names if "::" in n)
    if qualified:
        reasons.append(f"{qualified} qualified names (Class::method)")
    runtime = sorted({i for i in imports if any(i.endswith(r.lstrip("_")) for r in _CPP_RUNTIME)})
    if runtime:
        reasons.append("C++ runtime imports: " + ", ".join(runtime[:5]))
    operators = sorted({i for i in imports if i.lstrip("_") in {o.lstrip("_") for o in _CPP_OPERATORS}})
    if operators:
        reasons.append("operator new/delete imports: " + ", ".join(operators))
    score = (mangled >= 3) + (qualified >= 3) + bool(runtime) + bool(operators)
    return ("cpp", reasons) if score >= 2 else ("c", reasons or ["no C++ names or runtime imports"])


def choose(requested, program_map):
    """The language for a run: forced by the operator, or detected from the map with `auto`."""
    if requested in LANGUAGES:
        return LANGUAGES[requested], [f"chosen by the operator ({requested})"]
    if requested != "auto":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown language {requested!r}; choose auto, c or cpp")
    name, reasons = detect(program_map)
    return LANGUAGES[name], reasons

```

`hive/partition.py`:

```py
"""Deterministic, model-free map partitioning for the first planning stage.

``partition`` returns bounded map views, complete side-file evidence, all directed
cut calls, and a bounded summary. Count/byte caps take precedence over affinity:
a connected component may be split. No function is classified or skipped;
library/runtime metadata survives.
Byte limits refer to ``encode(slice)`` (compact, sorted-key UTF-8 JSON). Oversized
singletons have bounded views and complete side-file payloads; write_side_files
materializes them. No program execution or model invocation is performed.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import re
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path


def encode(value):
    """Canonical serialization used for the slice and summary byte budgets."""
    try:
        return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                          allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8")
    except (TypeError, ValueError, UnicodeError, RecursionError) as error:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid UTF-8 JSON: {error}") from None


def _address(value):
    if isinstance(value, str):
        try:
            value = int(value, 0)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid address: {value!r}") from None
    if type(value) is not int or not 0 <= value < 2**64:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid address: {value!r}")
    return value


def _entry(value):
    return _address(value.get("entry", value.get("hex"))) if isinstance(value, dict) else _address(value)


def _validate(source):
    if not isinstance(source, dict):
        raise ValueError("program map must be a JSON object")
    if "functions" not in source:
        raise ValueError("map.functions is required")
    for key in ("functions", "calls", "strings", "references", "data_refs", "entry_points", "imports"):
        if key in source and not isinstance(source[key], list):
            raise ValueError(f"map.{key} must be a list")
    for key in ("functions", "calls", "strings", "references", "data_refs"):
        for index, row in enumerate(source.get(key, [])):
            label = f"{key}[{index}]"
            if not isinstance(row, dict):
                raise ValueError(f"{label} must be an object")
            fields = (("entry",) if "entry" in row else ("hex",)) if key == "functions" else (
                "from", "address" if key == "strings" else "to")
            for field in fields:
                try:
                    _address(row[field])
                except (KeyError, ValueError):
                    raise ValueError(f"{label}.{field} must contain a valid address") from None
            if key == "strings" and not isinstance(row.get("text"), str):
                raise ValueError(f"{label}.text must be a string")
            if key == "functions" and "name" in row and not isinstance(row["name"], str):
                raise ValueError(f"{label}.name must be a string")
            if key == "calls" and row.get("to_name") is not None and not isinstance(row["to_name"], str):
                raise ValueError(f"{label}.to_name must be a string or null")
    if any(not isinstance(name, str) for name in source.get("imports", [])):
        raise ValueError("map.imports must contain strings")
    for index, entry in enumerate(source.get("entry_points", [])):
        try:
            _entry(entry)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(f"entry_points[{index}] must contain a valid address") from None


def write_side_files(result, folder):
    """Write current payloads and remove only stale JSON names this writer owns."""
    folder = Path(folder)
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prepared = {}
    for name, payload in result["side_files"].items():
        if Path(name).name != name or not name.endswith(".json"):
            raise ValueError("invalid side-file name")
        prepared[name] = encode(payload)
    for old in folder.iterdir():
        owned = old.name == "unattached.json" or re.fullmatch(
            r"g[0-9]{4,}-(incoming_calls|outgoing_calls|strings|references|data_refs)\.json", old.name)
        if owned and old.name not in prepared and (old.is_file() or old.is_symlink()):
            old.unlink()
    for name, data in prepared.items():
        (folder / name).write_bytes(data)


def _summary(groups, cuts, declared, hints, named_hints, unattached, budget):
    hint_order = sorted(hints - declared)
    lists = {
        "groups": [{"id": g["id"], "functions": len(g["functions"]), "bytes": g["bytes"],
                    **({"oversized": True} if g["oversized"] else {})} for g in groups],
        "cut_edges": [{k: c[k] for k in ("from", "to", "from_group", "to_group")} for c in cuts],
        "entry_points": [hex(e) for e in sorted(declared)],
        "entry_hints": [hex(e) for e in hint_order if e in named_hints]
                       + [hex(e) for e in hint_order if e not in named_hints],
    }
    result = {key: [] for key in lists}
    result["totals"] = {key: len(rows) for key, rows in lists.items()}
    result["totals"]["functions"] = sum(len(g["functions"]) for g in groups)
    result["omitted"] = {key: len(rows) for key, rows in lists.items()}
    result["unattached"] = {key: len(rows) for key, rows in unattached.items()}
    result["oversized"] = sum(g["oversized"] for g in groups)
    if len(encode(result)) > budget:
        raise ValueError("summary budget cannot hold its counts and omission labels")
    # Round-robin samples keep group sizes, entry points and cut edges represented.
    active = [key for key, rows in lists.items() if rows]
    while active:
        for key in active[:]:
            index = len(result[key])
            result[key].append(lists[key][index])
            result["omitted"][key] -= 1
            if len(encode(result)) > budget:
                result[key].pop()
                result["omitted"][key] += 1
                active.remove(key)
            elif len(result[key]) == len(lists[key]):
                active.remove(key)
    return result


def partition(program_map, *, max_functions=128, max_bytes=65536, summary_bytes=8192,
              incoming_limit=128, string_limit=128, outgoing_limit=128, reference_limit=128):
    """Group related functions within hard caps; return groups/cut_edges/summary.

    Function rows must have consistent unique numeric entry/hex addresses. Call
    slices include incoming and outgoing edges. Strings and data references stay
    with their source (and referenced functions, when present). ``references`` and
    ``data_refs`` use the export's from/to fields. Imports are the supplied names
    actually called by the group. Entry-point lists are restricted to the slice;
    other top-level metadata is preserved and counts toward the byte cap.

    Affinity combines calls, shared string addresses/text and shared data targets.
    Sorted adjacent users represent a shared resource in O(users) edges rather
    than a quadratic clique. Greedy unions prefer stronger affinity, with numeric
    address tie breaks. Remaining groups are packed in address order. This is a
    bounded deterministic heuristic, not a minimum-cut claim.

    Entry hints include entry/main/start names and functions without callers;
    these are not proven entry points. Oversized singletons stay isolated. Their
    bounded map view samples incoming/outgoing calls, references,
    data_refs and strings up to their limits (fewer if needed for bytes).
    reference_limit applies separately to references and data_refs. Outgoing
    samples prefer self calls. The manifest's by_group counts only deferred rows; side
    files keep complete rows and complete counts. Unknown call sources use
    unknown_caller; unknown reference sources/targets have their own buckets.
    Side files are independent JSON objects. Only views shorten, never evidence.
    Call write_side_files on the result to materialize the referenced JSON files.
    """
    for name, value in (("max_functions", max_functions), ("max_bytes", max_bytes),
                        ("summary_bytes", summary_bytes), ("incoming_limit", incoming_limit),
                        ("string_limit", string_limit), ("outgoing_limit", outgoing_limit),
                        ("reference_limit", reference_limit)):
        if type(value) is not int or value < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
    # Detach every output from the caller, while rejecting non-JSON/NaN inputs.
    source = json.loads(encode(program_map))
    _validate(source)
    functions = {}
    for row in source["functions"]:
        entry = _entry(row)
        if "hex" in row and _address(row["hex"]) != entry:
            raise ValueError(f"inconsistent function address at {hex(entry)}")
        if entry in functions:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate function at {hex(entry)}")
        functions[entry] = row
    known = set(functions)
    declared = {_entry(e) for e in source.get("entry_points", [])}
    if source.get("entry_point") is not None:
        declared.add(_entry(source["entry_point"]))
    declared.update(e for e, f in functions.items() if f.get("is_entry") is True)
    hints = {e for e, f in functions.items() if f.get("name") in ("entry", "main", "_main", "start", "_start")}

    tables = {key: sorted(source[key], key=encode)
              for key in ("calls", "strings", "references", "data_refs") if key in source}
    attached = {e: set() for e in known}
    affinity, resources = defaultdict(int), defaultdict(set)

    def relate(a, b, weight):
        if a in known and b in known and a != b:
            affinity[tuple(sorted((a, b)))] += weight

    for key, rows in tables.items():
        for index, row in enumerate(rows):
            start = _address(row["from"])
            target = _address(row["address"] if key == "strings" else row["to"])
            if start in known:
                attached[start].add((key, index))
            if key != "strings" and target in known:
                attached[target].add((key, index))
            if key == "calls":
                relate(start, target, 4)
            elif start in known:
                resources[("address", target)].add(start)
                if key == "strings" and row.get("text"):
                    resources[("text", row["text"])].add(start)
    for (kind, _), users in sorted(resources.items()):
        ordered = sorted(users)
        for a, b in zip(ordered, ordered[1:]):
            relate(a, b, 2 if kind == "text" else 3)
    named_hints = set(hints)
    hints.update(known - {_address(row["to"]) for row in tables.get("calls", [])})
    assigned = set().union(*attached.values()) if attached else set()
    unattached = {key: [row for i, row in enumerate(values) if (key, i) not in assigned]
                  for key, values in tables.items()}

    def slice_map(entries, row_ids):
        result = dict(source)
        result["functions"] = [functions[e] for e in sorted(entries)]
        for key, rows in tables.items():
            result[key] = [rows[i] for table, i in sorted(row_ids) if table == key]
        if "imports" in source:
            called = {r.get("to_name") for r in result.get("calls", [])
                      if _address(r["from"]) in entries and _address(r["to"]) not in known}
            result["imports"] = sorted(name for name in source["imports"] if name in called)
        if "entry_points" in source:
            result["entry_points"] = sorted((e for e in source["entry_points"] if _entry(e) in entries), key=encode)
        return result

    def overflow_parts(e, row_ids):
        ordered = sorted(row_ids)
        return (("incoming_calls", incoming_limit,
                 [(key, i) for key, i in ordered if key == "calls" and _address(tables[key][i]["from"]) != e]),
                ("outgoing_calls", outgoing_limit,
                 sorted([(key, i) for key, i in ordered if key == "calls" and _address(tables[key][i]["from"]) == e],
                        key=lambda item: (_address(tables[item[0]][item[1]]["to"]) != e, item))),
                ("references", reference_limit, [item for item in ordered if item[0] == "references"]),
                ("data_refs", reference_limit, [item for item in ordered if item[0] == "data_refs"]),
                ("strings", string_limit, [item for item in ordered if item[0] == "strings"]))

    parent = {e: e for e in known}
    members = {e: {e} for e in known}
    rows = {e: attached[e] for e in known}
    oversized, full_rows, original_bytes = set(), {}, {}

    def root(e):
        while parent[e] != e:
            parent[e] = parent[parent[e]]
            e = parent[e]
        return e

    def merge(a, b):
        if a in oversized or b in oversized:
            return False
        entries = members[a] | members[b]
        if len(entries) > max_functions:
            return False
        together = rows[a] | rows[b]
        if len(encode(slice_map(entries, together))) > max_bytes:
            return False
        a, b = sorted((a, b))
        parent[b] = a
        members[a], rows[a] = entries, together
        del members[b], rows[b]
        return True

    offenders = []
    for e in sorted(known):
        needed = len(encode(slice_map({e}, rows[e])))
        if needed <= max_bytes:
            continue
        oversized.add(e)
        full_rows[e], original_bytes[e] = rows[e], needed
        parts = overflow_parts(e, rows[e])
        retained = rows[e] - {item for _, _, items in parts for item in items}
        core_bytes = len(encode(slice_map({e}, retained)))
        if core_bytes > max_bytes:
            offenders.append(f"{hex(e)} needs {core_bytes} core bytes (original {needed})")
            continue
        for _, limit, candidates in parts:
            lo, hi = 0, min(len(candidates), limit)
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
                if len(encode(slice_map({e}, retained | set(candidates[:mid])))) <= max_bytes:
                    lo = mid
                else:
                    hi = mid - 1
            retained.update(candidates[:lo])
        rows[e] = retained
    if offenders:
        raise ValueError(f"irreducible slices exceed max_bytes={max_bytes}: " + "; ".join(offenders))
    for (a, b), weight in sorted(affinity.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0])):
        a, b = root(a), root(b)
        if a != b:
            merge(a, b)
    current = None
    for e in sorted(members):
        if current is None or not merge(current, e):
            current = e

    groups, owners = [], {}
    for number, (e, entries) in enumerate(sorted(members.items()), 1):
        mid = f"g{number:04d}"
        # Separate slices may touch the same row; give each its own JSON objects.
        data = encode(slice_map(entries, rows[e]))
        groups.append({"id": mid, "functions": [hex(a) for a in sorted(entries)],
                       "map": json.loads(data), "bytes": len(data), "oversized": e in oversized})
        owners.update((a, mid) for a in entries)
    cuts = []
    for row in tables.get("calls", []):
        a, b = _address(row["from"]), _address(row["to"])
        if a in known and b in known and owners[a] != owners[b]:
            cuts.append({**row, "from_group": owners[a], "to_group": owners[b]})
    side_files = {}
    if any(unattached.values()):
        side_files["unattached.json"] = unattached

    def group_counts(items, kind, entry):
        counts = defaultdict(int)
        for table, i in items:
            row = tables[table][i]
            if kind == "strings":
                counterpart, unknown = entry, "unknown_source"
            elif _address(row["from"]) == entry:
                counterpart, unknown = _address(row["to"]), "unknown_target"
            else:
                counterpart = _address(row["from"])
                unknown = "unknown_caller" if table == "calls" else "unknown_source"
            counts[owners.get(counterpart, unknown)] += 1
        return dict(sorted(counts.items()))

    for group in groups:
        e = _address(group["functions"][0])
        if e not in oversized:
            continue
        group["original_bytes"], group["overflow"] = original_bytes[e], {}
        for kind, _, selected in overflow_parts(e, full_rows[e]):
            retained = sum(item in rows[e] for item in selected)
            if retained == len(selected):
                continue
            payload = {"rows": [tables[key][i] for key, i in selected],
                       "by_group": group_counts(selected, kind, e)}
            filename = f"{group['id']}-{kind}.json"
            side_files[filename] = payload
            group["overflow"][kind] = {"file": filename, "total": len(selected), "retained": retained,
                                       "deferred": len(selected) - retained,
                                       "by_group": group_counts([item for item in selected if item not in rows[e]], kind, e),
                                       "sha256": hashlib.sha256(encode(payload)).hexdigest()}
    summary = _summary(groups, cuts, declared, hints, named_hints, unattached, summary_bytes)
    return {"groups": groups, "cut_edges": cuts, "summary": summary, "summary_bytes": len(encode(summary)),
            "unattached": unattached, "side_files": json.loads(encode(side_files))}

```

`hive/planning.py`:

```py
"""Bounded group planning and byte-bound interfaces; model calls belong to the queen."""

from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import re
import stat
import tempfile

from hive.partition import encode


def _object(properties):
```
