```py
                                            "flags": 7, "writable": True, "executable": True})
        self.assertTrue(all("name" not in value for value in values(reply)))
        m1 = [o.value for o in structure.sections(data, {"max_sections": 64})]
        for mine, theirs in zip(values(reply), m1):
            for field in ("index", "offset", "size", "flags", "writable", "executable"):
                self.assertEqual(mine[field], theirs[field], field)

    def test_elf_rows_equal_m1_and_known_answers_for_every_width_and_byte_order(self):
        for label, (data, layout) in (("elf64 le", elf()), ("elf32 le", elf(width=32)),
                                      ("elf32 be", elf(width=32, order=">", kind=3, machine=8)), ("elf64 be", elf(order=">", machine=21))):
            with self.subTest(label):
                reply = run("lief.sections", data)
                m1 = structure.sections(data, {"max_sections": 64})
                self.assertEqual([item["location"] for item in reply["observations"]],
                                 [{"offset": o.location.offset, "length": o.location.length} for o in m1])
                for mine, theirs in zip(values(reply), m1):
                    self.assertEqual({k: mine[k] for k in ("index", "offset", "size", "flags", "writable", "executable")},
                                     {k: theirs.value[k] for k in ("index", "offset", "size", "flags", "writable", "executable")})
                self.assertEqual([(v["offset"], v["size"], v["flags"]) for v in values(reply)[1:4]],
                                 [(layout["offsets"][0], 32, 0x6), (layout["offsets"][1], 16, 0x3), (layout["offsets"][2], 8, 0x7)])

    def test_pe_rows_report_the_raw_size_not_the_virtual_size(self):
        data, layout = pe()
        for index in range(3):
            data = patched(data, layout["table_offset"] + 40 * index + 8, "<I", 0x123 + index)  # VirtualSize
        rows, m1 = values(run("lief.sections", data)), [o.value for o in structure.sections(data, {"max_sections": 64})]
        self.assertEqual([v["virtual_size"] for v in m1], [0x123, 0x124, 0x125])
        self.assertEqual([(r["offset"], r["size"]) for r in rows], [(offset, 0x200) for offset in layout["raw_offsets"]])
        self.assertEqual([(r["offset"], r["size"], r["characteristics"]) for r in rows],
                         [(v["offset"], v["size"], v["characteristics"]) for v in m1])

    def test_a_20_byte_optional_header_moves_the_section_table(self):
        data, layout = pe(optional_size=20)
        self.assertEqual(layout["table_offset"], 0x80 + 24 + 20)
        self.assertEqual(run("lief.headers", data)["observations"][2],
                         {"location": {"offset": 0x98, "length": 20},
                          "value": {"structure": "optional", "optional_magic": "pe32+", "entry_rva": 0x1000}})
        reply = run("lief.sections", data)
        self.assertEqual([item["location"] for item in reply["observations"]],
                         [{"offset": 0xAC + 40 * i, "length": 40} for i in range(3)])
        m1 = [o.value for o in structure.sections(data, {"max_sections": 64})]
        self.assertEqual([(v["offset"], v["size"], v["characteristics"]) for v in values(reply)],
                         [(v["offset"], v["size"], v["characteristics"]) for v in m1])

    def test_pe_sections(self):
        data, layout = pe()
        reply = run("lief.sections", data)
        self.assertEqual([item["location"] for item in reply["observations"]],
                         [{"offset": layout["table_offset"] + 40 * i, "length": 40} for i in range(3)])
        self.assertEqual([v["index"] for v in values(reply) if v["writable"] and v["executable"]], [2])
        self.assertEqual(values(reply)[0], {"structure": "section", "index": 0, "offset": layout["raw_offsets"][0], "size": 0x200,
                                            "characteristics": 0x60000020, "writable": False, "executable": True})

    def test_max_sections_caps_the_entries(self):
        self.assertEqual(len(run("lief.sections", elf()[0], max_sections=2)["observations"]), 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(run("lief.sections", elf()[0])["observations"]), 5)
        self.assertEqual([v["index"] for v in values(run("lief.sections", pe()[0], max_sections=2))], [0, 1])
        self.assertEqual(len(run("lief.sections", pe()[0])["observations"]), 3)

    def test_elf_extended_numbering_is_refused_not_listed_empty(self):
        data, _ = elf(extended=True)
        self.assertEqual(run("lief.sections", data)["error"], "UnsupportedLayout")
        self.assertEqual(values(run("lief.headers", data))[0]["shnum"], 0)  # with shoff set: no count claim can follow


class RefusalTests(unittest.TestCase):
    # Expected (headers, sections) outcome per malformed host input. The worker differs from the host by design where names
    # are deferred (a bad name table does not matter) and where the PE optional header is read only inside its
    # declared size, the section table then starting where the COFF header says, as the Windows loader does.
    MALFORMED = {
        "elf truncated identification": ("TruncatedStructure", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "elf truncated header": ("TruncatedStructure", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "elf bad class": ("UnsupportedLayout", "UnsupportedLayout"),
        "elf bad byte order": ("UnsupportedLayout", "UnsupportedLayout"),
        "elf section table past end": ("ok", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "elf huge section count": ("ok", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "elf wrong section entry size": ("ok", "UnsupportedLayout"),
        "elf name table past end": ("ok", "ok"),
        "elf truncated section table": ("ok", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "pe truncated coff": ("TruncatedStructure", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "pe truncated optional": ("TruncatedStructure", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "pe huge section count": ("ok", "TruncatedStructure"),
        "pe huge optional size": ("StructureTooLarge", "StructureTooLarge"),
        "pe zero optional size": ("ok", "ok"),
        "pe optional size below its fields": ("ok", "ok"),
        "pe truncated section table": ("ok", "TruncatedStructure"),
    }

    def test_malformed_inputs_have_exact_outcomes_and_in_range_locations(self):
        cases = malformed()
        self.assertEqual(set(cases), set(self.MALFORMED))
        for name, (data, _) in cases.items():
            for operation, expected in zip(("lief.headers", "lief.sections"), self.MALFORMED[name]):
                with self.subTest(name=name, operation=operation):
                    reply = run(operation, data)
                    self.assertEqual(reply.get("error", reply["status"]), expected)
                    for item in reply.get("observations", ()):
                        location = item["location"]
                        self.assertTrue(0 < location["length"] <= 4096 and location["offset"] + location["length"] <= len(data))

    def test_only_elf_and_pe_are_accepted(self):
        for data in (b"", b"PK\x03\x04" + bytes(40), b"\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe" + bytes(40), b"MZ" + bytes(100)):
            with self.subTest(data=data[:4]):
                self.assertEqual(run("lief.headers", data)["error"], "UnsupportedFormat")
        # A 64-byte DOS header is the smallest PE candidate: here the signature fits, the COFF header does not.
        smallest = patched(b"MZ" + bytes(0x2E) + b"PE\0\0" + bytes(0x0C), 0x3C, "<I", 0x30)
        self.assertEqual(run("lief.headers", smallest)["error"], "TruncatedStructure")
        self.assertEqual(run("lief.headers", smallest[:0x3F])["error"], "UnsupportedFormat")

    # Every field LIEF must confirm, listed here rather than read from the worker, so a dropped check fails.
    ELF_FIELDS = ("type", "machine", "entry", "shoff", "shentsize", "shnum")
    PE_FIELDS = ("e_lfanew", "machine", "number_of_sections", "timestamp", "characteristics", "sizeof_optional_header")

    def test_every_checked_header_field_must_agree_with_lief(self):
        cases = [(operation, data, field) for operation in ("lief.headers", "lief.sections")
                 for data, fields in ((elf()[0], self.ELF_FIELDS), (elf(width=32, order=">")[0], self.ELF_FIELDS),
                                      (pe()[0], self.PE_FIELDS))
                 for field in fields]
        cases += [("lief.headers", pe()[0], field) for field in ("optional_magic", "entry_rva")]
        for operation, data, field in cases:
            with self.subTest(operation=operation, field=field, size=len(data)):
                self.assertEqual(run(operation, data)["status"], "ok")
                bumped = changed(lambda facts: facts.update({field: facts[field] + 1}))
                self.assertEqual(run(operation, data, facts_of=bumped)["error"], "InconsistentParse")

    def test_every_reported_section_row_must_agree_with_lief(self):
        for label, data in (("elf64", elf()[0]), ("elf32 be", elf(width=32, order=">")[0]), ("pe", pe()[0])):
            declared = len(faithful(data, "elf" if label.startswith("elf") else "pe")["sections"])
            for index in range(declared):
                for position, name in enumerate(("offset", "size", "flags")):
                    def bump(facts):
                        row = list(facts["sections"][index])
                        row[position] += 1
                        facts["sections"][index] = tuple(row)
                    with self.subTest(label, index=index, field=name):
                        self.assertEqual(run("lief.sections", data, facts_of=changed(bump))["error"], "InconsistentParse")

    def test_class_and_byte_order_come_from_the_bytes_alone(self):
        # LIEF only echoes e_ident; a byte order it does not follow shows up in the multi-byte fields it confirms.
        self.assertNotIn("class", worker.ELF_CHECKED)
        self.assertNotIn("endianness", worker.ELF_CHECKED)
        little_reading = changed(lambda facts: facts.update(machine=int.from_bytes(facts["machine"].to_bytes(2, "big"), "little")))
        self.assertEqual(run("lief.headers", elf(order=">", machine=21)[0], facts_of=little_reading)["error"], "InconsistentParse")

    def test_lief_must_list_exactly_the_declared_sections(self):
        def listing(change):
            def facts_of(data, format_):
                facts = faithful(data, format_)
                facts["sections"] = change(facts["sections"])
                return facts
            return facts_of
        for label, change in (("one more", lambda listed: listed + [(0, 0, 0)]), ("one fewer", lambda listed: listed[:-1])):
            with self.subTest(label):
                self.assertEqual(run("lief.sections", elf()[0], facts_of=listing(change), max_sections=2)["error"], "InconsistentParse")

    def test_the_whole_declared_table_must_be_inside_the_input_even_when_fewer_entries_are_read(self):
        data, layout = elf()
        cut = data[:layout["shoff"] + 2 * 64]  # entries 0 and 1 fit, the declared five do not
        self.assertEqual(run("lief.sections", cut, max_sections=1)["error"], "TruncatedStructure")
        table = pe()[1]["table_offset"]
        self.assertEqual(run("lief.sections", pe()[0][:table + 40], max_sections=1)["error"], "TruncatedStructure")

    def test_requests_are_exact(self):
        data = elf()[0]
        for request in ([], ["lief.headers"], ["lief.headers", "{}", "x"], ["lief.imports", "{}"], ["lief.headers", '{"x": 1}'],
                        ["lief.sections", '{"max_sections": 0}'], ["lief.sections", '{"max_sections": 65}'],
                        ["lief.sections", '{"max_sections": true}'], ["lief.sections", '{"max_sections": "8"}'],
                        ["lief.sections", '{"max_sections": 8, "max_sections": 9}'], ["lief.sections", "[]"],
                        ["lief.sections", "not json"]):
            with self.subTest(request=request):
                self.assertEqual(worker.reply(request, data, faithful)["error"], "InvalidRequest")

    def test_unexpected_failures_become_short_error_names(self):
        def broken(data, format_):
            raise RuntimeError("detail with /host/path and bytes")
        reply = run("lief.headers", elf()[0], facts_of=broken)
        self.assertEqual(reply, {"protocol": worker.PROTOCOL, "status": "error", "snapshot_sha256": sha256_hex(elf()[0]),
                                 "error": "RuntimeError"})


def config_class(names, ignored=()):
    """A stand-in ParserConfig: each named option defaults to True; setting an ignored one silently does nothing."""
    class Config:
        def __setattr__(self, name, value):
            if name not in ignored:
                object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
    for name in names:
        setattr(Config, name, True)
    return Config

class SnapshotTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def main(self, snapshot, request=("lief.headers", "{}")):
        out = io.StringIO()
        with patch.object(worker, "lief_facts", faithful), contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
            self.assertEqual(worker.main(list(request), snapshot=str(snapshot)), 0)
        return json.loads(out.getvalue())

    def test_an_unreadable_snapshot_has_its_own_error(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            for path in (Path(temporary, "missing"), Path(temporary)):
                with self.subTest(path=path.name):
                    self.assertEqual(self.main(path)["error"], "SnapshotUnreadable")

    def test_a_too_large_snapshot_reports_the_digest_of_the_whole_file(self):
        data = bytes(range(256)) * 12_000  # about 3 MiB: several read chunks
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary, patch.object(worker, "MAX_INPUT_BYTES", 1_500_000):
            snapshot = Path(temporary, "input")
            snapshot.write_bytes(data)
            self.assertEqual(worker.read_snapshot(snapshot), (data[:1_500_001], hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()))
            reply = self.main(snapshot)
        self.assertEqual((reply["error"], reply["snapshot_sha256"]), ("InputTooLarge", hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()))


class ProtocolTests(unittest.TestCase):

        self.assertIn('ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "-I", "-B", "/opt/reverseai/worker.py"]', dockerfile)
        self.assertIn("USER 65534:65534", dockerfile)
        lock = ROOT / "containers" / "lief" / "image.lock.json"
        if lock.exists():
            value = json.loads(lock.read_text())
            self.assertEqual(set(value), {"image_id", "platform", "base_digest", "wheel_sha256", "adapter_version"})
            self.assertEqual((value["base_digest"], value["platform"], value["adapter_version"]),
                             (digest, "linux/arm64", worker.ADAPTER_VERSION))
```

```py
"""tools/linux_proof.py with stand-in git, Docker and pip; nothing here builds, runs or pulls an image."""
import contextlib
import importlib.util
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("linux_proof", ROOT / "tools/linux_proof.py")
P = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(P)

COMMIT = "c" * 40
IMAGE = "sha256:" + "e" * 64
WHEEL = "reverseai-0.9.0-py3-none-any.whl"


def doctor_facts(version="0.9.0"):
    return {"reverseai": version, "host_ok": True, "docker": {"answered": False},
            "tools": [{"tool": name, "lock_loads": True,
                       "lock": f"/tmp/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reverseai/_locks/{name}.json"}
                      for name in ("lief", "yarax", "ghidra", "jadx", "jsparser")]}


def inside_facts(**changes):
    facts = {"python": "3.12.9", "platform": "Linux-6.10-aarch64-with-glibc2.36", "machine": "aarch64", "uid": 65534,
             "suite": {"ran": 1750, "skipped": 1, "failures": 0, "errors": 0, "expected_failures": 0,
                       "unexpected_successes": 0, "ok": True},
             "wheel": {"name": WHEEL, "size": 1, "sha256": "0" * 64}, "version": "reverseai 0.9.0",
             "imported_from": "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reverseai/__init__.py",
             "doctor": doctor_facts(), "analyze": {"reports": ["report.json", "report.md"]},
             "query": {"reports": ["report.json", "report.md"]}, "venv": "/tmp/venv",
             "steps": {name: {"exit": 0} for name in P.REQUIRED_STEPS}}
    facts.update(changes)
    return facts


def marker(**changes):
    return P.MARKER + json.dumps(inside_facts(**changes)) + "\n"


class HostDocker:
    """Stateful stand-in for git and docker on the host; records every argv.

    run is (exit, stdout, stderr) or an exception; leaves says whether --rm removed the container by itself, so a
    lost client connection (nonzero exit) leaves it running until "docker rm --force" removes it."""
    def __init__(self, base=True, run=None, leaves=None, build=0, silent=False):
        self.calls, self.base, self.build, self.silent = [], base, build, silent
        self.run = (0, "noise\n" + marker(), "") if run is None else run
        self.leaves = (isinstance(self.run, tuple) and self.run[0] == 0) if leaves is None else leaves
        self.containers, self.images = set(), set()

    def __call__(self, argv, *, timeout, cwd=None, env=None):
        self.calls.append(list(argv))
        if argv[:4] == ["git", "-C", str(P.ROOT), "rev-parse"]:
            return 0, COMMIT + "\n", ""
        if argv[:4] == ["git", "-C", str(P.ROOT), "archive"]:
            Path(argv[argv.index("-o") + 1]).write_bytes(b"tar")
            return 0, "", ""
        if argv[:4] == ["git", "-C", str(P.ROOT), "show"]:
            return 0, '"""ReverseAI."""\n\n__version__ = "0.9.0"\n', ""
        if self.silent and argv[:2] == ["docker", "image"] and argv[2] in ("rm", "inspect") and argv[-1] == IMAGE:
            return None, "", ""
        if argv[:5] == ["docker", "image", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Id}}"]:
            if argv[5] == P.BASE:
                return (0, "sha256:base\n", "") if self.base else (1, "", "Error: No such image")
            return (0, IMAGE, "") if argv[5] in self.images else (1, "", "Error: No such image: " + argv[5])
        if argv[:5] == ["docker", "container", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Id}}"]:
            return (0, "id", "") if argv[5] in self.containers else (1, "", "Error: No such container: " + argv[5])
        if argv[:2] == ["docker", "build"]:
            Path(argv[argv.index("--iidfile") + 1]).write_text(IMAGE)
            self.images.add(IMAGE)
            return self.build, "", "client lost" if self.build else ""
        if argv[:2] == ["docker", "run"]:
            name = argv[argv.index("--name") + 1]
            self.containers.add(name)
            if isinstance(self.run, BaseException):
                raise self.run
            if self.leaves:
                self.containers.discard(name)
            return self.run
        if argv[:3] == ["docker", "rm", "--force"]:
            if argv[3] not in self.containers:
                return 1, "", "Error: No such container: " + argv[3]
            self.containers.discard(argv[3])
            return 0, argv[3], ""
        if argv[:4] == ["docker", "image", "rm", "--no-prune"]:
            self.images.discard(argv[4])
            return 0, "", ""
        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected argv {argv}")


class DockerfileAndArgvTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_image_is_the_pinned_base_plus_the_archive_with_no_run_step(self):
        lines = P.DOCKERFILE.splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(lines[0], "FROM " + P.BASE)
        self.assertEqual(lines[1:3], ["ADD source.tar /opt/", "USER 65534:65534"])
        self.assertFalse(any(line.split()[0] in ("RUN", "COPY", "VOLUME", "EXPOSE") for line in lines))
        for tool in ("lief", "yarax", "ghidra", "jadx", "jsparser"):
            lock = json.loads((ROOT / f"containers/{tool}/image.lock.json").read_text())
            self.assertEqual(lock["base_digest"], P.BASE_DIGEST)
        self.assertTrue(P.DOCKERFILE.isascii())

    def test_docker_calls_never_pull_mount_or_open_the_network(self):
        build = P.build_argv(Path("/ctx"), Path("/ctx/image.id"), "reverseai-linux-proof:" + COMMIT[:12])
        self.assertEqual(build[:2], ["docker", "build"])
        self.assertIn("--pull=false", build)
        self.assertIn("--network=none", build)
        run = P.run_argv(IMAGE, "reverseai-linux-proof-0123")
        for flag in (["--pull", "never"], ["--network", "none"], ["--user", "65534:65534"], ["--cap-drop", "ALL"],
                     ["--security-opt", "no-new-privileges"], ["--platform", "linux/arm64"]):
            self.assertIn(flag, [run[i:i + 2] for i in range(len(run) - 1)])
        self.assertIn("--read-only", run)
        self.assertEqual(run[-1], IMAGE)
        self.assertFalse({"-v", "--volume", "--mount", "--privileged", "--network=host"} & set(run))
        self.assertEqual(P.remove_argv(IMAGE), ["docker", "image", "rm", "--no-prune", IMAGE])


class SuiteCountTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_closing_lines_give_exact_counts_or_none(self):
        self.assertEqual(P.suite_counts("....\nRan 1748 tests in 41.453s\n\nOK (skipped=1)\n"),
                         {"ran": 1748, "skipped": 1, "failures": 0, "errors": 0, "expected_failures": 0,
                          "unexpected_successes": 0, "ok": True})
        failed = P.suite_counts("Ran 9 tests in 1s\n\nFAILED (failures=2, errors=1, skipped=3, expected failures=1)")
        self.assertEqual((failed["ok"], failed["failures"], failed["errors"], failed["skipped"],
                          failed["expected_failures"]), (False, 2, 1, 3, 1))
        self.assertEqual(P.suite_counts("Ran 1 test in 0.1s\n\nOK")["ran"], 1)
        for text in ("", "OK", "Ran 3 tests in 1s\n\nOK (mystery=1)", "Ran 3 tests in 1s\n\nInterrupted"):
            with self.subTest(text=text):
                self.assertIsNone(P.suite_counts(text))


class ProveTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def prove(self, docker):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder, contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()) as stdout:
            receipt = Path(folder, "platform-linux-arm64.json")
            code = P.prove("m6-rc1", receipt, runner=docker, pause=0)
            return code, json.loads(receipt.read_text()), stdout.getvalue()

    def assert_cleaned(self, docker, receipt):
        self.assertEqual((docker.containers, docker.images), (set(), set()))
        self.assertIn(["docker", "image", "rm", "--no-prune", IMAGE], docker.calls)
        self.assertTrue(all(argv[3] == receipt["container"] for argv in docker.calls if argv[:2] == ["docker", "rm"]))
        self.assertEqual((receipt["container_removed"], receipt["image_removed"]), (True, True))

    def test_a_passing_run_writes_the_receipt_and_removes_its_image(self):
        docker = HostDocker()
        code, receipt, printed = self.prove(docker)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, receipt)
        self.assertEqual((receipt["commit"], receipt["base_digest"], receipt["platform"], receipt["image_id"]),
                         (COMMIT, P.BASE_DIGEST, "linux/arm64", IMAGE))
        self.assertEqual((receipt["passed"], receipt["docker_exit"], receipt["error"]), (True, 0, None))
        self.assertEqual(receipt["inside"]["suite"]["ran"], 1750)
        self.assertIn("passed: " + COMMIT[:12], printed)
        self.assert_cleaned(docker, receipt)
        kinds = [" ".join(argv[:3]) for argv in docker.calls]
        self.assertEqual(kinds, ["git -C " + str(P.ROOT), "docker image inspect", "git -C " + str(P.ROOT),
                                 "git -C " + str(P.ROOT), "docker build --platform", "docker run --rm",
                                 "docker rm --force", "docker container inspect", "docker image rm",
                                 "docker image inspect"])
        archive = next(argv for argv in docker.calls if "archive" in argv)
        self.assertEqual(archive[-1], COMMIT)
        self.assertIn("--prefix=src/", archive)

    def test_failures_still_remove_the_owned_container_and_image_and_fail_the_receipt(self):
        bad_suite = {"ran": 3, "skipped": 0, "failures": 1, "errors": 0, "expected_failures": 0,
                     "unexpected_successes": 0, "ok": False}
        cases = {"timeout": (None, "", ""), "no marker": (1, "Traceback", "boom"),
                 "lost client after a success marker": (77, marker(), "connection lost"),
                 "suite failed": (0, marker(suite=bad_suite), ""),
                 "source tree imported": (0, marker(imported_from="/opt/src/reverseai/__init__.py"), ""),
                 "lock from the checkout": (0, marker(doctor={**doctor_facts(), "tools": [
                     {**doctor_facts()["tools"][0], "lock": "/opt/src/containers/x"}]}), ""),
                 "two markers": (0, marker() * 2, "")}
        for label, outcome in cases.items():
            with self.subTest(label=label):
                docker = HostDocker(run=outcome)
                code, receipt, printed = self.prove(docker)
                self.assertEqual((code, receipt["passed"], receipt["docker_exit"]), (1, False, outcome[0]))
                self.assert_cleaned(docker, receipt)
                self.assertTrue(printed.startswith("FAILED"))
        _, receipt, _ = self.prove(HostDocker(run=(77, marker(), "connection lost")))
        self.assertIn("docker run exited 77", receipt["error"])
        self.assertEqual(receipt["inside"]["suite"]["ran"], 1750)  # kept for diagnosis, not trusted

    def test_an_interrupt_after_the_container_started_still_removes_it_and_the_image(self):
        docker = HostDocker(run=KeyboardInterrupt())
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder, self.assertRaises(KeyboardInterrupt):
            P.prove("m6-rc1", Path(folder, "receipt.json"), runner=docker, pause=0)
        self.assertEqual((docker.containers, docker.images), (set(), set()))
        name = next(argv[argv.index("--name") + 1] for argv in docker.calls if argv[:2] == ["docker", "run"])
        self.assertIn(["docker", "rm", "--force", name], docker.calls)

    def test_a_build_that_named_an_image_and_then_failed_removes_that_image(self):
        docker = HostDocker(build=1)
        code, receipt, _ = self.prove(docker)
        self.assertEqual((code, receipt["passed"], receipt["image_id"]), (1, False, IMAGE))
        self.assertIn("docker build failed (exit 1)", receipt["error"])
        self.assertFalse(any(argv[:2] in (["docker", "run"], ["docker", "rm"]) for argv in docker.calls))
        self.assertEqual((docker.images, receipt["image_removed"], receipt["container_removed"]), (set(), True, True))

    def test_docker_silence_is_not_counted_as_removal(self):
        code, receipt, _ = self.prove(HostDocker(silent=True))
        self.assertEqual((code, receipt["passed"], receipt["image_removed"]), (1, False, False))

    def test_a_missing_base_refuses_before_any_build(self):
        docker = HostDocker(base=False)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder, self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "never pulls"):
            P.prove("m6-rc1", Path(folder, "receipt.json"), runner=docker)
        self.assertFalse(any(argv[:2] in (["docker", "build"], ["docker", "run"]) for argv in docker.calls))

    def test_the_receipt_must_be_a_new_file(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder, contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
            existing = Path(folder, "receipt.json")
            existing.write_text("{}")
            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as raised:
                P.main(["--commit", "m6-rc1", "--receipt", str(existing)])
            self.assertEqual(raised.exception.code, 2)
            self.assertEqual(existing.read_text(), "{}")


class PassedTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_required_fact_is_needed(self):
        self.assertTrue(P.passed(inside_facts(), "0.9.0"))
        empty = {"ran": 0, "skipped": 0, "failures": 0, "errors": 0, "expected_failures": 0,
                 "unexpected_successes": 0, "ok": True}
        changes = {"zero tests": {"suite": empty}, "suite exit 17": {"steps": {
                       **inside_facts()["steps"], "suite": {"exit": 17}}},
                   "a missing step": {"steps": {name: {"exit": 0} for name in P.REQUIRED_STEPS[:-1]}},
                   "x86_64": {"machine": "x86_64"}, "macOS": {"platform": "macOS-27.0-arm64"},
                   "root": {"uid": 0}, "Python 3.13": {"python": "3.13.1"}, "no wheel": {"wheel": None}}
        for label, change in changes.items():
            with self.subTest(label=label):
                self.assertFalse(P.passed(inside_facts(**change), "0.9.0"))


class InsideTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The in-container sequence with stand-in commands: offline pip, a fresh venv, the installed entry point."""

    def runner(self, work, *, wheel_ok=True):
        calls = []

        def run(argv, *, timeout, cwd=None, env=None):
            calls.append((list(argv), cwd, env))
            if argv[1:4] == ["-B", "-m", "unittest"]:
                return 0, "", "......\nRan 6 tests in 0.1s\n\nOK (skipped=1)\n"
            if argv[1:4] == ["-m", "pip", "wheel"]:
                if wheel_ok:
                    Path(argv[argv.index("--wheel-dir") + 1]).mkdir()
                    Path(argv[argv.index("--wheel-dir") + 1], WHEEL).write_bytes(b"PK")
                return (0 if wheel_ok else 1), "", ""
            if argv[1:3] == ["-m", "venv"] or argv[1:4] == ["-m", "pip", "install"]:
                return 0, "", ""
            if argv[1:] == ["--version"]:
                return 0, "reverseai 0.9.0\n", ""
            if argv[1:3] == ["-I", "-c"]:
                return 0, "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reverseai/__init__.py\n", ""
            if argv[1:] == ["doctor", "--json"]:
                return 0, json.dumps(doctor_facts()), ""
            if argv[1:3] == ["-B", "-c"]:
                return 0, "", ""
            if argv[1] in ("analyze", "query"):
                out = Path(argv[argv.index("--out") + 1])
                out.mkdir()
                (out / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps({"input": {"sha256": "1" * 64}, "summary": {"supported": 3}}))
                (out / "report.md").write_text("# report\n")
                return 0, "", ""
            raise AssertionError(f"unexpected argv {argv}")
        return run, calls

    def test_every_step_runs_offline_in_order_and_the_facts_pass(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            work, source = Path(folder, "tmp"), Path(folder, "src")
            work.mkdir()
            source.mkdir()
            (source / "pyproject.toml").write_text("[project]\n")
            run, calls = self.runner(work)
            facts = P.inside(runner=run, work=work, source=source)
        names = list(facts["steps"])
        self.assertEqual(names, ["suite", "wheel", "venv", "install", "version", "imported_from", "doctor", "fixture",
                                 "analyze", "query"])
        self.assertEqual(tuple(names), P.REQUIRED_STEPS)
        argvs = [argv for argv, _, _ in calls]
        self.assertIn("--no-index", argvs[1])
        self.assertEqual(argvs[1][-1], str(work / "build"))
        self.assertIn("--no-index", argvs[3])
        self.assertEqual(argvs[3][-1], str(work / "dist" / WHEEL))
        self.assertEqual(argvs[4], [str(work / "venv/bin/reverseai"), "--version"])
        self.assertFalse(any("sdist" in part or part.startswith("http") for argv in argvs for part in argv))
        self.assertEqual(calls[0][1], source)
        self.assertTrue(all(env["HOME"] == str(work / "home") and env["PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR"] == "1"
                            and not {"HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY"} & set(env) for _, _, env in calls))
        self.assertEqual(facts["suite"]["ran"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(facts["wheel"]["name"], WHEEL)
        self.assertEqual(facts["analyze"]["reports"], ["report.json", "report.md"])
        container = {"machine": "aarch64", "platform": "Linux-7.0-aarch64-with-glibc2.41", "python": "3.12.15",
                     "uid": 65534, "venv": "/tmp/venv"}  # this test runs on the host; the container reports these
        self.assertTrue(P.passed({**facts, **container}, "0.9.0"))
        self.assertFalse(P.passed({**facts, **container}, "0.7.1"))

    def test_a_failed_wheel_build_stops_before_any_install(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            work, source = Path(folder, "tmp"), Path(folder, "src")
            work.mkdir()
            source.mkdir()
            run, calls = self.runner(work, wheel_ok=False)
            facts = P.inside(runner=run, work=work, source=source)
        self.assertEqual(list(facts["steps"]), ["suite", "wheel"])
        self.assertIsNone(facts["wheel"])
        self.assertFalse(P.passed(facts, "0.9.0"))

    def test_a_suite_timeout_with_bytes_output_keeps_structured_timeout_facts(self):
        def timed_out(argv, *, timeout, cwd=None, env=None):
            if argv[1:4] == ["-B", "-m", "unittest"]:
                return None, b"", b"....\nFAIL: test_x (tests.test_y.Z.test_x)\n"
            return 1, "", ""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            work, source = Path(folder, "tmp"), Path(folder, "src")
            work.mkdir()
            source.mkdir()
            facts = P.inside(runner=timed_out, work=work, source=source)
        self.assertEqual((facts["suite"], facts["steps"]["suite"]["exit"], facts["steps"]["suite"]["timed_out"]),
                         (None, None, True))
        self.assertEqual(facts["steps"]["suite"]["failed_tests"], ["FAIL: test_x (tests.test_y.Z.test_x)"])
        json.dumps(facts)

    def test_a_real_timeout_returns_text_streams(self):
        helper = "import sys, time\nsys.stdout.write('out'); sys.stderr.write('err')\nsys.stdout.flush(); sys.stderr.flush()\ntime.sleep(30)"
        code, out, err = P.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-c", helper], timeout=1)
        self.assertEqual((code, type(out), type(err)), (None, str, str))
        self.assertEqual(P.suite_counts(err), None)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

```py
import random
import struct
import unittest

from reverseai.contract import Location, Observation
from reverseai.tools import structure
from tests.fixtures_code import macho_code
from tests.fixtures_structure import MACHO_SECTIONS, macho, macho_fat, patched
from tests.test_structure import run


class MachoStructureTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exact_thin_headers_and_sections_for_both_widths(self):
        for width in (32, 64):
            data, layout = macho(width=width)
            with self.subTest(width=width):
                self.assertEqual(run("structure.headers", data), [Observation(Location(0, layout["header_size"]), {
                    "structure": "macho", "format": "macho", "machine_name": "x86_64" if width == 64 else "x86",
                    "filetype": 2, "ncmds": 4, "number_of_sections": 3})])
                expected, raw = [], layout["content_start"]
                for i, (name, segment, flags, prot, size) in enumerate(MACHO_SECTIONS):
                    expected.append(Observation(Location(layout["section_offsets"][i], layout["section_size"]), {
                        "index": i, "name": segment.decode() + "," + name.decode(), "offset": raw, "size": size,
                        "writable": bool(prot & 2), "executable": bool(prot & 4 or flags & 0x80000400)}))
                    raw += size
                self.assertEqual(run("structure.sections", data), expected)
                mapped = structure.macho_sections(data)
                self.assertEqual(mapped, [dict(o.value, addr=layout["addresses"][i]) for i, o in enumerate(expected)])
                self.assertEqual(run("structure.sections", data, max_sections=1), expected[:1])

    def test_permissions_follow_segment_initprot_and_either_instruction_attribute(self):
        rows = ((b"a", b"S", 0, 4, 1), (b"b", b"S", 0x80000000, 0, 1),
                (b"c", b"S", 0x400, 0, 1), (b"d", b"S", 0, 2, 1), (b"e", b"S", 0, 0, 1))
        values = [o.value for o in run("structure.sections", macho(sections=rows)[0])]
        self.assertEqual([v["executable"] for v in values], [True, True, True, False, False])
        self.assertEqual([v["writable"] for v in values], [False, False, False, True, False])

    def test_big_endian_thin_and_fat_only_identified(self):
        for width in (32, 64):
            thin, _ = macho(width=width, order=">")
            self.assertEqual(run("structure.identify", thin)[0].value["format"], "macho")
            for operation in ("structure.headers", "structure.sections", "structure.imports"):
                self.assertEqual(run(operation, thin), [])
            self.assertEqual(structure.macho_sections(thin), [])
            self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(thin))
            for order in (">",):
                fat = macho_fat(width=width, order=order, machines=(7, 0x1000007, 0x100000C, 999) * 3)
                self.assertEqual(run("structure.identify", fat)[0].value, {
                    "format": "macho-universal", "magic": fat[:4].hex(),
                    "architectures": ["x86", "x86_64", "aarch64", "unknown"] * 2})
                for operation in ("structure.headers", "structure.sections", "structure.imports"):
                    self.assertEqual(run(operation, fat), [])
                self.assertEqual(run("structure.identify", fat[:7])[0].value["format"], "unknown")

    def test_little_endian_fat_magics_are_not_universal(self):
        for width in (32, 64):
            data = macho_fat(width=width, order="<")
            self.assertEqual(run("structure.identify", data)[0].value["format"], "unknown")

    def test_names_escape_controls_backslashes_and_non_ascii(self):
        data, _ = macho(sections=((b"a\x1b\xff\\", b"S\x00ignored", 0, 0, 1),))
        self.assertEqual(run("structure.sections", data)[0].value["name"], "S,a\\x1b\\xff\\x5c")

    def test_mapping_refuses_zero_fill_and_out_of_segment_or_input_ranges(self):
        for width in (32, 64):
            for flag in (1, 0xC, 0x12):
                data, _ = macho(width=width, sections=((b"bss", b"RWX", flag, 7, 16),))
                self.assertTrue(run("structure.sections", data)[0].value["executable"])
                self.assertEqual(structure.macho_sections(data), [])
            data, layout = macho(width=width)
            s = layout["section_offsets"][0]
            offset_field = s + (48 if width == 64 else 40)
            # Both byte 0 and the next segment are real input, but neither belongs to this segment.
            for offset in (0, layout["content_start"] + 16, len(data)):
                self.assertEqual([r["index"] for r in structure.macho_sections(patched(data, offset_field, "<I", offset))], [1, 2])
            self.assertEqual(structure.macho_sections(data[:-1])[-1]["index"], 1)

    def test_helper_is_bounded_and_keeps_original_indices_when_filtering(self):
        rows = ((b"z", b"S", 1, 7, 1),) + ((b"a", b"S", 0, 5, 1),) * 299
        data, _ = macho(sections=rows, entry=None)
        self.assertEqual(len(run("structure.sections", data, max_sections=256)), 256)
        mapped = structure.macho_sections(data)
        self.assertEqual([r["index"] for r in mapped], list(range(1, 256)))
        self.assertEqual(run("structure.headers", data)[0].value["number_of_sections"], 300)

    def test_shared_code_fixture_exact_mapping_and_main_entry(self):
        data, layout = macho_code()
        self.assertEqual(structure.macho_sections(data), [{"index": 0, "name": "__TEXT,__text",
                         "addr": layout["text"]["address"], "offset": layout["text"]["offset"],
                         "size": layout["text"]["size"], "executable": True, "writable": False}])
        self.assertEqual(structure.macho_entry(data), layout["entry"])

    def test_main_entry_maps_nonzero_fileoff_and_rejects_ambiguous_or_out_of_bounds(self):
        for width in (32, 64):
            data, layout = macho(width=width)
            self.assertEqual(structure.macho_entry(data), layout["entry"])
            main = layout["entry_command"]
            for offset in (0, len(data), 2**64 - 1):
                self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(patched(data, main + 8, "<Q", offset)))
            no_command = patched(data, main, "<I", 0x1234)
            self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(no_command))
            self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(patched(data, main + 4, "<I", 8)))
            # The whole segment must be in the input.
            segment_filesize = layout["header_size"] + (48 if width == 64 else 36)
            self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(patched(data, segment_filesize, "<Q" if width == 64 else "<I", len(data))))
            # A second segment claiming the same file range makes LC_MAIN ambiguous.
            second = layout["section_offsets"][1] - (72 if width == 64 else 56)
            fileoff = second + (40 if width == 64 else 32)
            ambiguous = patched(data, fileoff, "<Q" if width == 64 else "<I", layout["content_start"])
            self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(ambiguous))

    def test_unixthread_x86_64_and_arm64_states_and_bad_flavors_counts(self):
        for kind, machine in (("x86_thread", 0x1000007), ("arm_thread", 0x100000C)):
            data, layout = macho(entry=kind, machine=machine)
            start = layout["entry_command"]
            self.assertEqual(structure.macho_entry(data), layout["entry"])
            for field, value in ((8, 99), (12, 0), (12, 2**32 - 1)):
                self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(patched(data, start + field, "<I", value)))
        for data in (b"", b"unrecognized", macho(entry=None)[0], macho(machine=1234, entry="x86_thread")[0]):
            self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(data))

    def test_malformed_commands_stay_inside_the_input(self):
        data, layout = macho(libraries=(b"liba",), symbols=(b"func",))
        bad = [patched(data, 16, "<I", 2**32 - 1), patched(data, 20, "<I", 2**32 - 1),
               patched(data, 36, "<I", 0), patched(data, 36, "<I", 7), patched(data, 36, "<I", len(data)),
               patched(data, 32 + 64, "<I", 2**32 - 1)]
        for item in bad:
            for operation in ("structure.headers", "structure.sections"):
                with self.subTest(operation=operation), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    run(operation, item)
            self.assertIsNone(structure.macho_entry(item))
        generator = random.Random(7301)
        for item in [data[:i] for i in range(len(data))] + [patched(data, generator.randrange(len(data)), "B", generator.randrange(256)) for _ in range(300)]:
            for operation in ("structure.identify", "structure.headers", "structure.sections", "structure.imports"):
                try:
                    found = run(operation, item)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                self.assertLessEqual(len(found), structure.TOOL.operations[operation].max_observations)
                self.assertTrue(all(o.location.within(len(item)) for o in found))
            structure.macho_entry(item)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`tests/test_mcp_client.py`:

```py
"""tests/mcp_client.py against a tiny fake stdio server written by the test; no ReverseAI server is needed."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest

from tests import mcp_client

# The fake server echoes each request's method and params as its result; "big", "silent", "noisy", "raw" and "flood"
# misbehave on purpose ("raw" writes params.text with {id} replaced, "flood" writes params.count extra replies). With
# --hang it ignores end of input. It reads only its own stdin and writes only its own streams.
FAKE_SERVER = r'''
import json, sys, time
for raw in sys.stdin.buffer:
    message = json.loads(raw)
    if "id" not in message:
        sys.stderr.write("notification " + message["method"] + "\n")
        sys.stderr.flush()
        continue
    method, params = message["method"], message.get("params") or {}
    if method == "silent":
        continue
    if method == "noisy":
        sys.stderr.write("x" * 1024 * 1024)
        sys.stderr.flush()
    if method == "big":
        head = '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": %d, "result": {"pad": "' % message["id"]
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(head.encode() + b"x" * int(params["size"]) + b'"}}\n')
    elif method == "raw":
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(params["text"].replace("{id}", str(message["id"])).encode() + b"\n")
    elif method == "flood":
        line = json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 999, "result": {"pad": "y" * int(params.get("width", 10))}})
        sys.stdout.buffer.write((line + "\n").encode() * int(params["count"]))
    else:
        reply = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": message["id"], "result": {"method": method, "params": message.get("params")}}
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(json.dumps(reply).encode() + b"\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()
if "--hang" in sys.argv:
    time.sleep(60)
'''


class ClientTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.script = Path(folder.name, "fake_server.py")
        self.script.write_text(FAKE_SERVER, encoding="utf-8")

    def client(self, *extra, **options):
        client = mcp_client.Client([sys.executable, "-I", str(self.script), *extra], **options)
        self.addCleanup(lambda: client.process.poll() is not None or client.close(timeout=1))
        return client

    def wait_for_failure(self, client):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
        while getattr(client, "failure", None) is None and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(0.02)
        return getattr(client, "failure", None)

    def test_requests_carry_the_modern_meta_and_ids_match_replies(self):
        client = self.client()
        first = client.discover()
        self.assertEqual((first["id"], first["result"]["method"]), (1, "server/discover"))
        self.assertEqual(first["result"]["params"]["_meta"], mcp_client.META)
        self.assertEqual(mcp_client.META["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"], "2026-07-28")
        call = client.call_tool("list_files")
        self.assertEqual((call["id"], call["result"]["method"]), (2, "tools/call"))
        self.assertEqual(call["result"]["params"]["name"], "list_files")
        self.assertEqual(call["result"]["params"]["arguments"], {})
        legacy = client.request("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25"}, modern=False)
        self.assertNotIn("_meta", legacy["result"]["params"])
        client.notify("notifications/initialized")
        self.assertEqual(client.request("ping")["id"], 4)  # the notification got no reply and took no id
        error = client.request("raw", {"text": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "error": {"code": -32601, '
                                               '"message": "Method not found"}}'})
        self.assertEqual(error["error"]["code"], -32601)
        brackets = client.request("raw", {"text": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "result": {"s": "' + "[{" * 500 + '"}}'})
        self.assertEqual(len(brackets["result"]["s"]), 1000)  # brackets inside a string are not nesting
        self.assertEqual(client.close(), 0)
        self.assertIn("notification notifications/initialized", client.stderr)

    def test_a_missing_reply_times_out_without_spoiling_the_session(self):
        client = self.client()
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(mcp_client.ClientError, "no reply"):
            client.request("silent", timeout=0.3)
        self.assertIsNone(client.failure)
        self.assertEqual(client.request("ping")["result"]["method"], "ping")
        self.assertEqual(client.close(), 0)

    def test_every_malformed_reply_is_refused_and_the_refusal_is_sticky(self):
        cases = {
            "not JSON": "not json",
            "NaN": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "result": {"x": NaN}}',
            "Infinity": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "result": {"x": -Infinity}}',
            "duplicate key": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "id": {id}, "result": {}}',
            "deep nesting": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "result": {"x": ' + "[" * 100_000 + "]" * 100_000 + "}}",
            "version 1.0": '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id": {id}, "result": {}}',
            "boolean id": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": true, "result": {}}',
            "string id": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "{id}", "result": {}}',
            "other id": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 7, "result": {}}',
            "result and error": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "result": {}, "error": {"code": 1, "message": "m"}}',
            "neither": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}}',
            "extra member": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "result": {}, "more": 1}',
            "result not an object": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "result": [1]}',
            "error without code": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "error": {"message": "m"}}',
            "boolean error code": '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {id}, "error": {"code": true, "message": "m"}}',
            "array": "[{}]",
        }
        for label, text in cases.items():
            with self.subTest(label=label):
                client = self.client()
                with self.assertRaises(mcp_client.ClientError):
                    client.request("raw", {"text": text})
                with self.assertRaises(mcp_client.ClientError):
                    client.request("ping")  # sticky: nothing after a breach is trusted
                self.assertEqual(client.close(), 0)

    def test_replies_nobody_asked_for_are_bounded_in_count(self):
        client = self.client()
        client.send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "flood", "params": {"count": 2000}})
        self.assertRegex(str(self.wait_for_failure(client)), "more replies than were requested")
        self.assertLessEqual(client.lines.qsize(), mcp_client.MAX_QUEUED_LINES)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(mcp_client.ClientError, "more replies"):
            client.request("ping")
        self.assertIsNotNone(client.close(timeout=1))

    def test_replies_nobody_asked_for_are_bounded_in_bytes(self):
        client = self.client(max_queued_bytes=10_000)
        client.send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "flood", "params": {"count": 20, "width": 3000}})
        self.assertRegex(str(self.wait_for_failure(client)), "more reply bytes")
        self.assertLessEqual(client.queued_bytes, 10_000)
        self.assertIsNotNone(client.close(timeout=1))

    def test_a_reply_over_the_size_bound_is_refused_whole_or_partial(self):
        client = self.client(max_line=4096)
        self.assertEqual(len(client.request("big", {"size": 1000})["result"]["pad"]), 1000)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(mcp_client.ClientError, "longer than the client's limit"):
            client.request("big", {"size": 100_000})  # still unterminated when it passes the limit
        self.assertIsNotNone(client.close(timeout=2))
        client = self.client(max_line=1000)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(mcp_client.ClientError, "longer than the client's limit"):
            client.request("big", {"size": 5000})  # one complete line in one read
        self.assertIsNotNone(client.close(timeout=2))

    def test_stderr_chatter_does_not_block_and_is_kept_bounded(self):
        client = self.client()
        self.assertEqual(client.request("noisy")["result"]["method"], "noisy")
        self.assertEqual(client.close(), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(client.stderr), mcp_client.MAX_STDERR)

    def test_close_kills_only_its_own_child_when_it_ignores_end_of_input(self):
        client = self.client("--hang")
        self.assertEqual(client.request("ping")["result"]["method"], "ping")
        code = client.close(timeout=0.5)
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIsNotNone(client.process.poll())

    def test_the_reverseai_command_line_is_fixed(self):
        captured = {}

        class Recorder(mcp_client.Client):
            def __init__(self, argv, **options):
                captured.update(argv=argv, options=options)

        Recorder.reverseai(Path("/inputs"), "--with-ghidra", timeout=5)
        self.assertEqual(captured["argv"], [sys.executable, "-B", "-m", "reverseai", "mcp", "--inputs", "/inputs",
                                            "--with-ghidra"])
        self.assertEqual(captured["options"], {"timeout": 5})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

```py
"""The MCP catalog uses the existing query bounds and confines paths without reading input bytes."""

import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import stat
import tempfile
from types import SimpleNamespace
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from reverseai import cli, mcp_tools, queries
from reverseai.contract import MAX_STRING_ARG_CHARS


class ArgumentSchemaTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_query_argument_keeps_its_declared_type_limits_choices_and_default(self):
        kinds = set()
        tools = {tool["name"]: tool for tool in mcp_tools.catalog(frozenset(mcp_tools.ENABLE))}
        for name, query in queries.TABLE.items():
            schema = tools[name]["inputSchema"]
            self.assertFalse(schema["additionalProperties"])
            self.assertEqual(schema["type"], "object")
            self.assertEqual(set(schema["properties"]), {"file", "view", *(
                "member_file" if key == "file" else key for key in query.args)})
            self.assertEqual(schema["required"], ["file", *(
                "member_file" if key == "file" else key for key, spec in query.args.items() if spec.default is None)])
            for key, spec in query.args.items():
                with self.subTest(query=name, argument=key):
                    kinds.add(spec.kind)
                    field = schema["properties"]["member_file" if key == "file" else key]
                    if spec.kind == "int":
                        self.assertEqual(field, {"type": "integer", "minimum": spec.minimum,
                                                "maximum": spec.maximum, **(
                                                    {"default": spec.default} if spec.default is not None else {})})
                    else:
                        self.assertEqual(field["type"], "string")
                        if spec.kind == "enum":
                            self.assertEqual(field["enum"], list(spec.choices))
                        else:
                            self.assertEqual(field["minLength"], spec.minimum if spec.kind != "str" else 0)
                            self.assertEqual(field["maxLength"], spec.maximum if spec.kind != "str"
                                             else MAX_STRING_ARG_CHARS)
                        self.assertEqual(field.get("default"), spec.default)
                        self.assertEqual("default" in field, spec.default is not None)
        self.assertEqual(kinds, {"int", "str", "enum", "literal", "identity"})

    def test_catalog_order_worker_filtering_annotations_and_no_argument_inventory(self):
        host_names = ["binary_overview", "list_segments", "inspect_native_load_image", "list_names", "read_bytes",
                      "list_strings", "search_strings", "inspect_android_package", "search_android_classes",
                      "inspect_android_class", "inspect_android_method", "trace_android_references",
                      "analyze_javascript_application"]
        host = mcp_tools.catalog(frozenset())
        self.assertEqual([tool["name"] for tool in host], ["list_files", "analyze_file", *host_names])
        full = mcp_tools.catalog(frozenset(mcp_tools.ENABLE))
        self.assertEqual([tool["name"] for tool in full], ["list_files", "analyze_file", "prepare_file", *queries.TABLE])
        self.assertEqual(host[0]["inputSchema"], {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": [],
                                                "additionalProperties": False})
        for tool in full:
            self.assertTrue(tool["title"] and tool["description"])
            self.assertEqual(tool["annotations"], {"readOnlyHint": tool["name"] != "prepare_file", "destructiveHint": False,
                                                   "idempotentHint": True, "openWorldHint": False})
        for enabled in (frozenset(), frozenset({"jadx"}), frozenset({"jsparser"}), frozenset({"ghidra"})):
            with self.subTest(enabled=enabled):
                tools = {tool["name"]: tool for tool in mcp_tools.catalog(enabled)}
                self.assertEqual("procedure_info" in tools, "ghidra" in enabled)
                details = tools["analyze_javascript_application"]["inputSchema"]["properties"]["detail"]["enum"]
                self.assertEqual(details, ["summary", "files", "package", "hints", "modules", "calls", "parse"]
                                 if "jsparser" in enabled else ["summary", "files", "package", "hints"])

    def test_prepare_annotations_disclose_the_private_cache_write(self):
        tools = {tool["name"]: tool for tool in mcp_tools.catalog(frozenset({"ghidra"}))}
        self.assertEqual(tools["prepare_file"]["annotations"],
                         {"readOnlyHint": False, "destructiveHint": False,
                          "idempotentHint": True, "openWorldHint": False})
        self.assertTrue(all(tool["annotations"]["readOnlyHint"] for name, tool in tools.items()
                            if name != "prepare_file"))

    def test_catalog_calls_are_independent_and_do_not_probe_workers(self):
        with patch("subprocess.run", side_effect=AssertionError("no process")), \
                patch("subprocess.Popen", side_effect=AssertionError("no process")):
            first = mcp_tools.catalog(frozenset(mcp_tools.ENABLE))
            first[0]["annotations"]["readOnlyHint"] = False
            first[-1]["inputSchema"]["properties"]["detail"]["enum"].append("injected")
            first[1]["inputSchema"]["properties"]["file"]["maxLength"] = 999999
            fresh = mcp_tools.catalog(frozenset(mcp_tools.ENABLE))
        self.assertTrue(fresh[0]["annotations"]["readOnlyHint"])
        self.assertNotIn("injected", fresh[-1]["inputSchema"]["properties"]["detail"]["enum"])
        self.assertEqual(fresh[1]["inputSchema"]["properties"]["file"]["maxLength"], 1024)
        for flags in (None, "ghidra", ["ghidra"], {"ghidra"}, frozenset({"unknown"})):
            with self.subTest(flags=flags), self.assertRaises(mcp_tools.ToolInputError):
                mcp_tools.catalog(flags)

    def test_member_selector_description_explains_the_details_that_use_it(self):
        for enabled in (frozenset(), frozenset({"jsparser"})):
            tools = {tool["name"]: tool for tool in mcp_tools.catalog(enabled)}
            field = tools["analyze_javascript_application"]["inputSchema"]["properties"]["member_file"]
            self.assertEqual(field["description"], "Printable archive member selector used with detail hints, "
                             "package, modules, calls or parse; leave empty for summary or files.")


class RelativeNameTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_relative_posix_segments_and_utf8_byte_bound(self):
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools._relative_parts("folder/inert.bin"), ["folder", "inert.bin"])
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools._relative_parts("café.bin"), ["café.bin"])
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools._relative_parts("x" * 1024), ["x" * 1024])
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools._relative_parts("é" * 512), ["é" * 512])
        for bad in ("", ".", "..", "../x", "a/../x", "a/./x", "a//x", "a/", "/x", "//x",
                    "a\x00b", "x" * 1025, "é" * 513, "bad\udcff", "C:/x", "C:x", "a:stream", "a\\b",
                    "a\nb", "a\x1bb", "a\x85b", "a\u202eb", None, 1, b"bytes", []):
            with self.subTest(name=repr(bad)):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(mcp_tools.ToolInputError, "^file must be a relative POSIX path"):
                    mcp_tools._relative_parts(bad)


class FileTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reverseai-mcp-tools-")
        self.addCleanup(temporary.cleanup)
        self.work = Path(temporary.name).resolve()
        self.root = self.work / "inputs"
        self.root.mkdir()
        self.out = self.work / "new-report"

    def make_file(self, name="inert.bin", data=b"neutral fixture string\x00"):
        path = self.root / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(data)
        return path

    def command(self, name="analyze_file", arguments=None, enabled=frozenset()):
        return mcp_tools.command(name, {"file": "inert.bin"} if arguments is None else arguments,
                                 root=str(self.root), out=str(self.out), enabled=enabled)

    def symlink(self, target, link):
        try:
            link.symlink_to(target, target_is_directory=target.is_dir())
        except OSError:
            if os.name == "nt":
                self.skipTest("Windows account cannot create test links")
            raise

    def test_empty_inventory_and_sorted_lstat_sizes_without_input_reads(self):
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {"files": [], "truncated": False})
        self.make_file("z.bin", b"123")
        self.make_file("folder/a.bin", b"12345")
        self.make_file("café.bin", b"")
        with patch.object(Path, "open", side_effect=AssertionError("no input bytes")):
            self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {"files": [
                {"name": "café.bin", "size": 0}, {"name": "folder/a.bin", "size": 5},
                {"name": "z.bin", "size": 3}], "truncated": False})

    def test_links_to_files_and_directories_are_never_followed(self):
        self.make_file("ordinary.bin", b"one")
        outside = self.work / "outside"
        outside.mkdir()
        (outside / "hidden.bin").write_bytes(b"secret")
        self.symlink(self.root / "ordinary.bin", self.root / "alias.bin")
        self.symlink(outside, self.root / "linked")
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {
            "files": [{"name": "ordinary.bin", "size": 3}], "truncated": False})

    def test_inventory_skips_reparse_entries_before_listing_or_descending(self):
        outside = SimpleNamespace(name="outside.bin", path=str(self.work / "outside.bin"),
                                  stat=lambda **kwargs: SimpleNamespace(st_mode=stat.S_IFREG | 0o600, st_size=7))
        for mode in (stat.S_IFDIR, stat.S_IFREG):
            with self.subTest(mode=mode):
                entry = SimpleNamespace(name="reparse", path=str(self.root / "reparse"),
                                        stat=lambda **kwargs: SimpleNamespace(
                                            st_mode=mode | 0o700, st_file_attributes=0x400, st_size=7))

                def scan(path):
                    return contextlib.nullcontext(iter([entry] if path == str(self.root) else [outside]))

                with patch.object(mcp_tools.os, "scandir", side_effect=scan) as scanned:
                    self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {"files": [], "truncated": False})
                scanned.assert_called_once_with(str(self.root))

    def test_unaddressable_names_are_omitted_with_an_honest_partial_listing(self):
        self.make_file()
        if os.name != "nt":
            for name in ("bad\\name", "bad:stream", "line\nbreak", "bidi\u202e.bin"):
                self.make_file(name)
        else:
            self.make_file("bidi\u202e.bin")
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {
            "files": [{"name": "inert.bin", "size": 23}], "truncated": True})
        # Some filesystems refuse non-UTF-8 names at creation time.
        with patch.object(mcp_tools.os, "scandir", return_value=contextlib.nullcontext(iter([
                SimpleNamespace(name="bad-\udcff.bin")]))):
            self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {"files": [], "truncated": True})

    def test_file_count_is_capped_at_one_thousand(self):
        for index in range(1001):
            self.make_file(f"f{index:04}.bin", b"")
        listed = mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root))
        self.assertTrue(listed["truncated"])
        self.assertEqual(listed["files"], [{"name": f"f{index:04}.bin", "size": 0} for index in range(1000)])

    def test_file_depth_eight_is_included_and_nine_is_truncated(self):
        parent = "/".join("d" + str(i) for i in range(1, 8))
        self.make_file(parent + "/at_depth_eight.bin", b"ok")
        self.make_file(parent + "/d8/hidden.bin", b"hidden")
        self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {
            "files": [{"name": parent + "/at_depth_eight.bin", "size": 2}], "truncated": True})

    def test_directory_only_trees_have_a_ten_thousand_entry_scan_cap(self):
        seen, calls = [], []

        @contextlib.contextmanager
        def scan(path):
            calls.append(path)

            def entries():
                for index in range(10001):
                    seen.append(index)
                    yield SimpleNamespace(name=f"d{index:05}", path=str(self.root / f"d{index:05}"),
                                          stat=lambda **kwargs: SimpleNamespace(st_mode=stat.S_IFDIR | 0o700))
            yield entries()

        with patch.object(mcp_tools.os, "scandir", side_effect=scan):
            self.assertEqual(mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root)), {"files": [], "truncated": True})
        self.assertEqual(len(seen), 10000)
        self.assertEqual(calls, [str(self.root)])

    def test_listing_errors_do_not_expose_absolute_paths(self):
        with patch.object(mcp_tools.os, "scandir", side_effect=PermissionError(str(self.work / "private"))):
            with self.assertRaises(mcp_tools.ToolInputError) as caught:
                mcp_tools.list_files(str(self.root))
        self.assertEqual(str(caught.exception), "The input directory could not be listed; check its accessibility and retry.")

    def test_command_rejects_traversal_external_and_internal_links_and_linked_parents(self):
        source = self.make_file()

        external = self.work / "private.bin"
        external.write_bytes(b"private")
        self.symlink(external, self.root / "external.bin")
        self.symlink(source, self.root / "internal.bin")

        for name in ("../private.bin", str(external), "external.bin", "internal.bin", "parent/inside.bin",
                     "sub/../inert.bin", "sub//inside.bin", "sub/./inside.bin", "sub", "absent.bin"):
            with self.subTest(name=name), self.assertRaises(mcp_tools.ToolInputError) as caught:
                self.command(arguments={"file": name})
            self.assertNotIn(str(self.work), str(caught.exception))

    def test_reparse_points_are_refused_even_when_their_stat_type_is_a_directory(self):
        self.make_file("junction/inside.bin")
        original = os.lstat

        def inspected(path, *args, **kwargs):
            if os.fspath(path) == str(self.root / "junction"):
                return SimpleNamespace(st_mode=stat.S_IFDIR | 0o700, st_file_attributes=0x400)
            return original(path, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(mcp_tools.os, "lstat", side_effect=inspected):
            with self.assertRaises(mcp_tools.ToolInputError):
                self.command(arguments={"file": "junction/inside.bin"})

    def test_hard_link_refusal_reuses_intake_and_command_never_reads_the_sample(self):
        source = self.make_file()
        with patch.object(Path, "open", side_effect=AssertionError("no sample reads")):
            self.assertEqual(self.command(), ["analyze", str(source), "--out", str(self.out)])
        os.link(source, self.root / "second.bin")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(mcp_tools.ToolInputError, "^Hard-linked input files need a separate copy$"):
            self.command()

    def test_every_query_maps_to_the_existing_cli_with_validated_defaults(self):
        self.make_file()
        enabled = frozenset(mcp_tools.ENABLE)
        for name, spec in queries.TABLE.items():
            values = {key: (arg.minimum if arg.kind == "int" else "Lexample/App;")
                      for key, arg in spec.args.items() if arg.default is None}
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                argv = self.command(name, {"file": "inert.bin", **values}, enabled=enabled)
                self.assertEqual(argv[:6], ["query", str(self.root / "inert.bin"), "--out", str(self.out), "--query", name])
                forwarded = [argv[i + 1] for i, value in enumerate(argv) if value == "--arg"]
                self.assertEqual(queries.parse_args(name, forwarded), spec.validate(values))

    def test_enabled_workers_are_passed_only_to_applicable_commands(self):
        self.make_file()
        enabled = frozenset(mcp_tools.ENABLE)
        self.assertEqual(self.command(enabled=enabled)[4:], ["--with-lief", "--with-yarax", "--with-ghidra"])
        cases = (("list_strings", {}, []), ("procedure_info", {}, ["--with-ghidra"]),

    def test_outer_file_and_javascript_member_selector_stay_separate(self):

    def test_wrong_types_bounds_enums_missing_values_and_unknown_arguments_are_fixed_errors(self):
        self.make_file()
        cases = (("analyze_file", None), ("analyze_file", []), ("analyze_file", {}),

                 ("list_strings", {"encoding": "latin1"}), ("read_bytes", {"length": True}),
                 ("read_bytes", {"length": "12"}), ("read_bytes", {"length": 2001}),
                 ("read_bytes", {"at": -1}), ("read_bytes", {"at": 2**64}),
                 ("read_bytes", {"mode": "shell"}), ("list_strings", {"limit": 0}),
                 ("search_strings", {}), ("search_strings", {"query": "line\nbreak"}),

        for name, values in cases:
            arguments = {"file": "inert.bin", **values} if isinstance(values, dict) and name != "analyze_file" else values
            with self.subTest(name=name, values=values), self.assertRaises(mcp_tools.ToolInputError):
                mcp_tools.command(name, arguments, root=str(self.root), out=str(self.out), enabled=frozenset())
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(mcp_tools.ToolInputError, "enable --with-jsparser"):

    def test_unknown_or_disabled_tools_are_distinct_from_invalid_tool_arguments(self):

            with self.subTest(name=name), self.assertRaises(mcp_tools.UnknownTool):

    def test_shell_metacharacters_remain_literal_argv_values(self):
        self.make_file()
        text = "--flag; $(touch should-never-exist) / path"
        argv = self.command("search_strings", {"file": "inert.bin", "query": text})
        self.assertIn("query=" + text, argv)
        self.assertEqual(queries.parse_args("search_strings", [argv[i + 1] for i, value in enumerate(argv)
                                                              if value == "--arg"])["query"], text)
        self.assertFalse((self.work / "should-never-exist").exists())

    def test_real_host_cli_report_uses_the_confined_file_and_query(self):
        self.make_file(data=b"known neutral phrase\x00")
        argv = self.command("list_strings", {"file": "inert.bin", "encoding": "ascii", "min_length": 4})
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
            self.assertEqual(cli.main(argv), 0)
        result = json.loads((self.out / "report.json").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(result["input"]["name"], "inert.bin")
        self.assertEqual(result["query"]["name"], "list_strings")
        self.assertGreater(result["summary"]["supported"], 0)
        self.assertTrue((self.out / "report.md").is_file())
```

```py
"""Distribution contents, reproducibility and real offline installation; no Docker."""

import base64
import csv
from email.parser import BytesParser
import hashlib
import importlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import tomllib
import unittest
from unittest import mock
import zipfile

from reverseai import __version__, contained
from tests.fixtures_structure import elf
from tools import reverseai_build as build

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TOOLS = ("lief", "yarax", "ghidra", "jadx", "jsparser")
INFO = "reverseai-0.9.0.dist-info"


class PackagingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reverseai-packaging-")
        cls.addClassCleanup(cls.temporary.cleanup)
        cls.work = Path(cls.temporary.name)
        cls.wheel = cls.work / build.build_wheel(cls.work)
        cls.editable = cls.work / "editable" / build.build_editable(cls.work / "editable")
        cls.source = ROOT
        if not (ROOT / ".git").exists() and not (ROOT / "PKG-INFO").is_file():
            # Linux's git-archive proof has no index: exercise sdist hooks in a temporary unpacked source tree.
            cls.source = cls.work / "unpacked"
            cls.copy_sources(cls.source)
            (cls.source / "PKG-INFO").write_bytes(build._metadata())
        with mock.patch.object(build, "ROOT", cls.source):
            cls.sdist = cls.work / build.build_sdist(cls.work)

    @staticmethod
    def copy_sources(destination):
        destination.mkdir()
        for name in ("reverseai", "tools", "containers", "docs", "tests", "media"):
            if (ROOT / name).is_dir():
                shutil.copytree(ROOT / name, destination / name, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "*.pyc"))
        for name in ("README.md", "LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md", "pyproject.toml"):
            shutil.copyfile(ROOT / name, destination / name)

    def test_project_identity_and_dependency_free_build_contract(self):
        value = tomllib.loads((ROOT / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        project = value["project"]
        self.assertEqual((project["name"], project["version"], __version__), ("reverseai", "0.9.0", "0.9.0"))
        self.assertEqual(project["requires-python"], ">=3.12")
        self.assertEqual(project["readme"], "README.md")
        self.assertEqual(project["dependencies"], [])
        self.assertEqual(project["license"], "MIT")
        self.assertEqual(project["license-files"], ["LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"])
        self.assertEqual(project["scripts"], {"reverseai": "reverseai.cli:main"})
        self.assertEqual(value["build-system"], {"requires": [], "build-backend": "reverseai_build", "backend-path": ["tools"]})
        self.assertEqual(build.get_requires_for_build_wheel(), [])
        self.assertEqual(build.get_requires_for_build_sdist(), [])
        self.assertEqual(build.get_requires_for_build_editable(), [])

    def test_wheel_has_exact_files_and_fixed_metadata(self):
        expected = {path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix() for path in (ROOT / "reverseai").rglob("*.py")
                    if "__pycache__" not in path.parts}

                "Description-Content-Type": "text/markdown; charset=UTF-8", "License-Expression": "MIT"})
            self.assertEqual(raw.split(b"\n\n", 1)[1], (ROOT / "README.md").read_bytes())

    def test_record_covers_every_entry_with_actual_hashes_and_sizes(self):
        for path in (self.wheel, self.editable):
            with self.subTest(wheel=path), zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
                rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(archive.read(f"{INFO}/RECORD").decode("utf-8"))))
                self.assertEqual([row[0] for row in rows], archive.namelist())
                for name, digest, size in rows:
                    if name == f"{INFO}/RECORD":
                        self.assertEqual((digest, size), ("", ""))
                        continue
                    data = archive.read(name)
                    expected = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(data).digest()).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")
                    self.assertEqual((digest, size), ("sha256=" + expected, str(len(data))))

    def test_all_build_hooks_refuse_other_license_declarations(self):

    def test_sdist_pins_level_nine_when_the_runtime_gzip_default_changes(self):
        gzip_file = build.gzip.GzipFile
        archives, levels = [], []
        for runtime_default in (6, 9):
            def runtime_gzip(*args, compresslevel=runtime_default, **kwargs):
                levels.append(compresslevel)
                return gzip_file(*args, compresslevel=compresslevel, **kwargs)

            destination = self.work / f"gzip-default-{runtime_default}"
            with mock.patch.object(build, "ROOT", self.source), mock.patch.object(build.gzip, "GzipFile", runtime_gzip):
                archives.append((destination / build.build_sdist(destination)).read_bytes())
        self.assertTrue(archives[0] == archives[1], "The runtime gzip default changed the sdist bytes")
        self.assertEqual(levels, [9, 9])

    def test_git_archive_copy_builds_identical_wheel_but_sdist_requires_provenance(self):

    def test_sdist_exact_source_list_modes_root_and_metadata(self):
        paths = {}
        if (ROOT / ".git").exists():
            raw = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "--stage", "-z"], cwd=ROOT, check=True, capture_output=True).stdout
            for row in raw.split(b"\0"):
                if row:
                    attributes, name = row.split(b"\t", 1)
                    paths[name.decode("utf-8")] = int(attributes.split()[0], 8) & 0o777
        else:
            paths = {p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(): 0o755 if p.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else 0o644
                     for p in ROOT.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and "__pycache__" not in p.parts}
        selected = {name: mode for name, mode in paths.items()
                    if name in ("README.md", "LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md", "pyproject.toml")
                    or name.split("/", 1)[0] in ("reverseai", "tools", "containers", "docs", "tests", "media")}
        selected["PKG-INFO"] = 0o644
        prefix = "reverseai-0.9.0/"
        with tarfile.open(self.sdist, "r:gz") as archive, zipfile.ZipFile(self.wheel) as wheel:
            self.assertEqual(archive.getnames(), [prefix + name for name in sorted(selected)])
            for entry in archive.getmembers():
                name = entry.name.removeprefix(prefix)
                with self.subTest(name=name):
                    self.assertTrue(entry.isfile())
                    self.assertEqual((entry.mtime, entry.uid, entry.gid, entry.uname, entry.gname), (0, 0, 0, "", ""))
                    self.assertEqual(entry.mode, selected[name])
                    expected = wheel.read(f"{INFO}/METADATA") if name == "PKG-INFO" else (ROOT / name).read_bytes()
                    self.assertEqual(archive.extractfile(entry).read(), expected)
        header = self.sdist.read_bytes()[:10]
        self.assertEqual(header[:4], b"\x1f\x8b\x08\x00")  # no source path in the gzip filename
        self.assertEqual(header[4:8], bytes(4))

    def test_default_lock_uses_package_data_before_checkout_and_rejects_unknown_tools(self):

    def test_sdist_uses_git_executable_mode_and_excludes_untracked_files(self):
```
