`tests/test_queries_claims.py`:

```py
"""Query pages and single readings, verified on the host or derived from Ghidra."""

import unittest

from reverseai import claims
from reverseai.contract import (
    AnalysisResult, InputRef, Location, Observation, OperationSpec, ToolRef, ToolSpec, content_id, make_evidence,
    make_finding, sha256_hex,
)
from reverseai.review import review

DATA = b"MZ" + bytes(range(256)) * 3 + b"hello world\x00" + "wide".encode("utf-16-le") + b"\x00\x00" + bytes(64)
INPUT = InputRef(sha256_hex(DATA), len(DATA), "sample.bin")
STRUCTURE, STRINGS, GHIDRA = ToolRef("structure", "0.1.0"), ToolRef("strings", "0.1.0"), ToolRef("ghidra", "12.1.4-r7")
OPERATIONS = {STRUCTURE: ("structure.segments", "structure.entry", "structure.symbols", "structure.read_bytes"),
              STRINGS: ("strings.list", "strings.search"),
              GHIDRA: ("ghidra.functions", "ghidra.function", "ghidra.xrefs")}
HELLO = DATA.index(b"hello")
WIDE = DATA.index("wide".encode("utf-16-le"))


def tools(derived=True):
    def spec(ref):
        ops = {name: OperationSpec(name, {}, lambda data, args: [], derived=derived and ref is GHIDRA)
               for name in OPERATIONS[ref]}
        return ToolSpec(ref, ops)
    return {ref.name: spec(ref) for ref in OPERATIONS}


def observed(ref, operation, where, size=4, /, **value):
    return make_evidence(DATA, ref, operation, Observation(Location(where, size), value))


def judge(key, value, cited, confidence=None, registry=None):
    confidence = confidence or claims.RULES[key][0]
    finding = make_finding("code" if key.startswith("code.") else "structural", "A claim.", key, value,
                           [item.id for item in cited], confidence)
    result = AnalysisResult(content_id("tk", {"t": key}), finding.role, "ok", tuple(cited), (finding,))
    return review(DATA, INPUT, [result], registry or tools())[0].status


def segment(index, total=3, /, **change):
    row = dict(kind="segment", index=index, total=total, name="LOAD", offset=index * 64, filesz=64,
               address=0x400000 + index * 0x1000, memsz=64, readable=True, writable=False, executable=index == 0)
    row.update(change)
    return observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.segments", (64 + index * 56) % 800, 56, **row)


def text_row(operation, index, total, offset, encoding, text, truncated=False, length=None):
    width = 1 if encoding == "ascii" else 2
    return observed(STRINGS, operation, offset, length or len(text) * width, kind="string", index=index, total=total,
                    offset=offset, encoding=encoding, text=text, truncated=truncated)


class QueryClaimTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_page_is_contiguous_rows_of_one_total(self):
        rows = [segment(1), segment(2)]
        value = {"start": 1, "total": 3, "rows": [["LOAD", 64, 64, 0x401000, 64, True, False, False],
                                                   ["LOAD", 128, 64, 0x402000, 64, True, False, False]]}
        self.assertEqual(judge("segments.list", value, rows), "supported")
        self.assertEqual(judge("segments.list", value, rows[::-1]), "supported")  # cited order does not matter
        gap = [segment(0), segment(2)]
        gap_rows = [[r.observation[k] for k in ("name", "offset", "filesz", "address", "memsz", "readable", "writable",
                                                "executable")] for r in gap]
        # The claimed rows are the cited ones, so only the missing index 1 can reject them.
        self.assertEqual(judge("segments.list", {"start": 0, "total": 3, "rows": gap_rows}, gap), "unsupported")
        mixed = [segment(1), segment(2, total=4)]
        self.assertEqual(judge("segments.list", value, mixed), "unsupported")
        past = [segment(1, total=2), segment(2, total=2)]
        self.assertEqual(judge("segments.list", {**value, "total": 2}, past), "unsupported")
        for bad in ({"readable": 1}, {"offset": -1}, {"name": "a\nb"}, {"index": True}, {"extra": 0}):
            item = segment(0, **bad)
            row = {k: item.observation.get(k) for k in ("name", "offset", "filesz", "address", "memsz", "readable",
                                                        "writable", "executable")}
            self.assertEqual(judge("segments.list", {"start": 0, "total": 3, "rows": [list(row.values())]}, [item]),
                             "unsupported", bad)
        self.assertEqual(judge("segments.list", value, rows, confidence="inferred"), "unsupported")

    def test_single_readings(self):
        entry = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.entry", 24, 8, kind="entry", address=0x401000, offset=None)
        self.assertEqual(judge("load.entry", {"address": 0x401000, "offset": None}, [entry]), "supported")
        twice = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.entry", 32, 8, kind="entry", address=0x401000, offset=None)
        self.assertEqual(judge("load.entry", {"address": 0x401000, "offset": None}, [entry, twice]), "unsupported")
        odd = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.entry", 24, 8, kind="entry", address="0x401000", offset=None)
        self.assertEqual(judge("load.entry", {"address": "0x401000", "offset": None}, [odd]), "unsupported")

    def test_read_bytes_must_be_exactly_the_cited_bytes(self):
        raw = DATA[10:26]
        good = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.read_bytes", 10, 16, kind="bytes", offset=10, address=None, hex=raw.hex())
        self.assertEqual(judge("bytes.read", {"offset": 10, "address": None, "hex": raw.hex()}, [good]), "supported")
        lie = (raw[:-1] + b"\xff").hex()
        bad = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.read_bytes", 10, 16, kind="bytes", offset=10, address=None, hex=lie)
        self.assertEqual(judge("bytes.read", {"offset": 10, "address": None, "hex": lie}, [bad]), "unsupported")
        short = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.read_bytes", 10, 16, kind="bytes", offset=10, address=None,
                         hex=raw[:8].hex())
        self.assertEqual(judge("bytes.read", {"offset": 10, "address": None, "hex": raw[:8].hex()}, [short]),
                         "unsupported")
        for hex_text in ("ABCD", "abc", "zz", ""):
            item = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.read_bytes", 10, 2, kind="bytes", offset=10, address=None, hex=hex_text)
            self.assertEqual(judge("bytes.read", {"offset": 10, "address": None, "hex": hex_text}, [item]),
                             "unsupported", hex_text)

    def test_string_rows_are_checked_against_their_bytes(self):
        ascii_row = text_row("strings.search", 0, 2, HELLO, "ascii", "hello world")
        wide_row = text_row("strings.search", 1, 2, WIDE, "utf-16le", "wide")
        value = {"start": 0, "total": 2, "rows": [[HELLO, "ascii", "hello world", False],
                                                   [WIDE, "utf-16le", "wide", False]]}
        self.assertEqual(judge("strings.matches", value, [ascii_row, wide_row]), "supported")
        lie = text_row("strings.search", 0, 1, HELLO, "ascii", "hellO world")
        self.assertEqual(judge("strings.matches", {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [[HELLO, "ascii", "hellO world", False]]},
                               [lie]), "unsupported")
        cut = text_row("strings.list", 0, 1, HELLO, "ascii", "hello", truncated=True, length=11)
        self.assertEqual(judge("strings.listed", {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [[HELLO, "ascii", "hello", True]]},
                               [cut]), "supported")  # a truncated row's text is a prefix: no whole-bytes check
        other_op = text_row("strings.list", 0, 2, HELLO, "ascii", "hello world")
        self.assertEqual(judge("strings.matches", {"start": 0, "total": 2, "rows": [[HELLO, "ascii", "hello world", False]]},
                               [other_op]), "unsupported")

    def test_symbol_pages(self):
        row = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.symbols", 300, 4, kind="symbol", index=0, total=1, name="main",
                       address=0x401000, type="func", binding="global", defined=True)
        value = {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [["main", 0x401000, "func", "global", True]]}
        self.assertEqual(judge("symbols.list", value, [row]), "supported")
        for change in ({"type": "function"}, {"binding": "GLOBAL"}, {"defined": "yes"}, {"name": ""}, {"name": "x" * 129}):
            item = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.symbols", 300, 4, **{**row.observation, **change})
            rows = [[item.observation[k] for k in ("name", "address", "type", "binding", "defined")]]
            self.assertEqual(judge("symbols.list", {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": rows}, [item]), "unsupported", change)

    def test_ghidra_query_claims_are_derived(self):
        function = observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.functions", 0, 32, kind="function_row", index=0, total=1, name="entry",
                            entry=0x1000, size=32)
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.function_list", {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [["entry", 0x1000, 32]]},
                               [function]), "derived")
        target = observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.function", 0, 32, kind="target", name="entry", entry=0x1000, size=32,
                          matches=1, callers_total=2, callees_total=1)
        info = {"name": "entry", "entry": 0x1000, "size": 32, "matches": 1, "callers_total": 2, "callees_total": 1}
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.function_info", info, [target]), "derived")
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.function_info", info, [target], registry=tools(derived=False)), "derived")
        callers = [observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.function", 40, 5, kind="caller", at=0x1100, **{"from": 0x1080}, to=0x1000),
                   observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.function", 60, 5, kind="caller", at=0x1200, **{"from": None}, to=0x1000)]
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.callers", {"to": 0x1000, "rows": [[0x1100, 0x1080], [0x1200, None]]}, callers),
                         "derived")
        split = callers[:1] + [observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.function", 60, 5, kind="caller", at=0x1200, **{"from": None},
                                        to=0x2000)]
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.callers", {"to": 0x1000, "rows": [[0x1100, 0x1080], [0x1200, None]]}, split),
                         "unsupported")
        xref = observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.xrefs", 40, 5, kind="xref", index=3, total=4, at=0x1100, **{"from": 0x1080},
                        to=0x2000, type="read")
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.xrefs", {"to": 0x2000, "start": 3, "total": 4, "rows": [[0x1100, 0x1080, "read"]]},
                               [xref]), "derived")
        wrong = observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.xrefs", 40, 5, **{**xref.observation, "type": "flow"})
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.xrefs", {"to": 0x2000, "start": 3, "total": 4, "rows": [[0x1100, 0x1080, "flow"]]},
                               [wrong]), "unsupported")

    def test_an_instruction_page_spans_exactly_its_cited_bytes(self):
        rows = [[8, 1, "PUSH RBP"], [9, 3, "MOV RBP,RSP"]]
        page = dict(kind="instructions", entry=0x1000, start=2, total=9, rows=rows, truncated=False)
        good = observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.function", 8, 4, **page)
        value = {k: page[k] for k in ("entry", "start", "total", "rows", "truncated")}
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.instructions", value, [good]), "derived")
        wide = observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.function", 8, 16, **page)
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.instructions", value, [wide]), "unsupported")
        over = observed(GHIDRA, "ghidra.function", 8, 4, **{**page, "total": 2})
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.instructions", {**value, "total": 2}, [over]), "unsupported")

    def test_assembly_rows_must_end_inside_the_cited_anchor(self):
        # The reviewer itself checks rows against the cited location.
        rows = [[0, 1, "PUSH RBP"], [1, 3, "MOV RBP,RSP"]]
        listing = dict(kind="assembly", index=0, entry=0x1000, instructions=rows, truncated=False)
        value = {"entry": 0x1000, "instructions": rows, "truncated": False}
        inside = make_evidence(DATA, GHIDRA, "ghidra.analyze", Observation(Location(0, 4), listing))
        outside = make_evidence(DATA, GHIDRA, "ghidra.analyze", Observation(Location(0, 3), listing))
        registry = {"ghidra": ToolSpec(GHIDRA, {"ghidra.analyze": OperationSpec("ghidra.analyze", {}, lambda d, a: [],
                                                                                derived=True)})}
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.assembly", value, [inside], registry=registry), "derived")
        self.assertEqual(judge("code.assembly", value, [outside], registry=registry), "unsupported")

    def test_m3a_code_rules_refuse_malformed_readings_without_failing(self):
        registry = {"ghidra": ToolSpec(GHIDRA, {"ghidra.analyze": OperationSpec("ghidra.analyze", {}, lambda d, a: [],
                                                                                derived=True)})}
        cases = [("code.functions", ["x"], dict(kind="function", index=0, name="x", entry=1)),
                 ("code.functions", [None], dict(kind="function", index="0", name=None, entry=1, size=1)),
                 ("code.pseudocode", {"entry": 1, "text": None, "truncated": False},
                  dict(kind="pseudocode", index=0, entry=1, text=None, truncated=False)),
                 ("code.calls", [[1, None]], dict(kind="call", to=2, to_name=None, **{"from": 1})),
                 ("code.calls", [["a", "b"]], dict(kind="call", to=2, to_name="b", **{"from": "a"}))]
        for key, value, observation in cases:
            item = make_evidence(DATA, GHIDRA, "ghidra.analyze", Observation(Location(0, 4), observation))
            self.assertEqual(judge(key, value, [item], registry=registry), "unsupported", (key, observation))

    def test_every_query_claim_has_a_statement(self):
        for key in ("segments.list", "load.entry", "symbols.list", "bytes.read", "strings.listed", "strings.matches",
                    "code.function_list", "code.function_info", "code.instructions", "code.callers", "code.xrefs"):
            self.assertNotEqual(claims.statement(key), "No claim rule", key)
        self.assertEqual({k for k in claims.RULES if claims.RULES[k][0] == "observed"} & claims.DERIVED_CLAIMS, set())

class ReviewerHardeningTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Malformed rows refused without failing, offsets bound, queries kept apart."""

    def test_a_non_ascii_text_row_is_refused_not_raised(self):
        for operation, key in (("strings.list", "strings.listed"), ("strings.search", "strings.matches")):
            for encoding in ("ascii", "utf-16le"):
                row = text_row(operation, 0, 1, HELLO, encoding, "caf\u00e9", length=11)
                value = {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [[HELLO, encoding, "caf\u00e9", False]]}
                self.assertEqual(judge(key, value, [row]), "unsupported", (key, encoding))

    def test_bytes_and_string_rows_must_sit_at_their_cited_offset(self):
        raw = DATA[10:26]
        moved = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.read_bytes", 10, 16, kind="bytes", offset=999999, address=None, hex=raw.hex())
        self.assertEqual(judge("bytes.read", {"offset": 999999, "address": None, "hex": raw.hex()}, [moved]), "unsupported")
        row = observed(STRINGS, "strings.search", HELLO, 11, kind="string", index=0, total=1, offset=999999,
                       encoding="ascii", text="hello world", truncated=False)
        value = {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [[999999, "ascii", "hello world", False]]}
        self.assertEqual(judge("strings.matches", value, [row]), "unsupported")
        cut = observed(STRINGS, "strings.list", HELLO, 11, kind="string", index=0, total=1, offset=HELLO + 1,
                       encoding="ascii", text="hello", truncated=True)
        self.assertEqual(judge("strings.listed", {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [[HELLO + 1, "ascii", "hello", True]]},
                               [cut]), "unsupported")

    def test_different_queries_reviewed_together_do_not_contradict(self):
        def result(task, key, value, cited):
            finding = make_finding("structural", "A claim.", key, value, [item.id for item in cited], "observed")
            return finding, AnalysisResult(content_id("tk", {"t": task}), "structural", "ok", tuple(cited), (finding,))

        first = text_row("strings.search", 0, 1, HELLO, "ascii", "hello world")
        second = text_row("strings.search", 0, 1, WIDE, "utf-16le", "wide")
        a, ra = result("alpha", "strings.matches", {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [[HELLO, "ascii", "hello world", False]]},
                       [first])
        b, rb = result("beta", "strings.matches", {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [[WIDE, "utf-16le", "wide", False]]},
                       [second])
        reads = []
        for task, start in (("read-0", 0), ("read-6", 6)):
            raw = DATA[start:start + 8]
            item = observed(STRUCTURE, "structure.read_bytes", start, 8, kind="bytes", offset=start, address=None,
                            hex=raw.hex())
            reads.append(result(task, "bytes.read", {"offset": start, "address": None, "hex": raw.hex()}, [item]))
        judged = {v.finding_id: v.status for v in review(DATA, INPUT, [ra, rb, reads[0][1], reads[1][1]], tools())}
        self.assertEqual({judged[f.id] for f in (a, b, reads[0][0], reads[1][0])}, {"supported"})
        # Within one task, two readings of one index still contradict (PageReviewTests).


class PageReviewTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Pages of one verified list are compatible; a different total or row at one index contradicts."""

    def verdicts(self, pages):
        findings, evidence = [], []
        for rows in pages:
            value = {"start": rows[0].observation["index"], "total": rows[0].observation["total"],
                     "rows": [[r.observation[k] for k in ("name", "offset", "filesz", "address", "memsz", "readable",
                                                         "writable", "executable")] for r in rows]}
            findings.append(make_finding("structural", "Segments.", "segments.list", value, [r.id for r in rows], "observed"))
            evidence.extend(rows)
        result = AnalysisResult(content_id("tk", {"t": "pages"}), "structural", "ok", tuple({item.id: item for item in evidence}.values()),
                                tuple(findings))
        judged = {v.finding_id: v.status for v in review(DATA, INPUT, [result], tools())}
        return [judged[f.id] for f in findings]

    def test_contiguous_chunks_of_one_list_are_all_supported(self):
        rows = [segment(i, 130) for i in range(130)]
        self.assertEqual(self.verdicts([rows[:64], rows[64:128], rows[128:]]), ["supported"] * 3)
        self.assertEqual(self.verdicts([rows[:64], rows[10:20]]), ["supported"] * 2)  # overlapping, same rows

    def test_a_different_row_or_total_contradicts(self):
        first = [segment(0, 3), segment(1, 3)]
        other = [segment(1, 3, name="TEXT")]
        self.assertEqual(self.verdicts([first, other]), ["contradicted"] * 2)
        longer = [segment(2, 4)]
        self.assertEqual(self.verdicts([first, longer]), ["contradicted"] * 2)
```

```py
from dataclasses import replace
import json
import unittest

from reverseai import pipeline, report
from reverseai.report import Analysis
from reverseai.contract import (
    AnalysisResult, InputRef, Location, Observation, ReviewVerdict, ToolRef, make_evidence, make_finding, sha256_hex,
)

DATA = b"MZ" + bytes(62) + b"http://example.invalid/a|b`c\x00"
TOOL = ToolRef("strings", "0.1.0")


def analysis(verdict_status="supported"):
    evidence = make_evidence(DATA, TOOL, "strings.extract", Observation(Location(64, 27), {"text": "http://example.invalid/a|b`c"}))
    finding = make_finding("capability", "The input contains a URL.", "strings.urls", ["http://example.invalid/a|b`c"], [evidence.id])
    orphan = make_finding("capability", "Claim with no evidence.", "capability.network", ["net"], [], "inferred")
    result = AnalysisResult("tk-0123456789abcdef", "capability", "ok", (evidence,), (finding, orphan))
    verdicts = (
        ReviewVerdict(finding.id, verdict_status, () if verdict_status == "supported" else ("cited evidence failed",)),
        ReviewVerdict(orphan.id, "unsupported", ("no evidence cited",)),
    )
    ref = InputRef(sha256_hex(DATA), len(DATA), "sample.exe")
    return Analysis(ref, (TOOL,), (result,), verdicts)


def code_analysis(*, status="derived", instruction="MOV rax, [message]", name="message", text="hello"):
    tool = ToolRef("ghidra", "12.1.4-r5")
    values = (
        (Location(8, 16), {"kind": "assembly", "index": 0, "entry": 0x1000,
                          "instructions": [[2, 3, instruction]], "truncated": True}, "code.assembly",
         {"entry": 0x1000, "instructions": [[2, 3, instruction]], "truncated": True}),
        (Location(10, 3), {"kind": "ref", "from": 0x1000, "to": 0x2000, "type": "read", "to_name": name},
         "code.references", [[0x1000, "read", 0x2000, name]]),
        (Location(64, len(text)), {"kind": "string", "address": 0x2000, "encoding": "ascii", "text": text,
                                 "truncated": False, "from": [0x1000]}, "code.strings",
         [{"address": 0x2000, "encoding": "ascii", "text": text, "truncated": False, "from": [0x1000]}]),
    )
    evidence = tuple(make_evidence(DATA, tool, "ghidra.analyze", Observation(location, value))
                     for location, value, _, _ in values)
    findings = tuple(make_finding("code", "Tool interpretation.", key, value, [item.id], "inferred")
                     for item, (_, _, key, value) in zip(evidence, values))
    result = AnalysisResult("tk-0123456789abcdef", "code", "ok", evidence, findings)
    return Analysis(InputRef(sha256_hex(DATA), len(DATA), "inline"), (tool,), (result,),
                    tuple(ReviewVerdict(f.id, status, ("Tool reading; not verified.",)) for f in findings))


def android_query(name, args, layout_change=None):
    from tests import fixtures_apk
    from tests.test_queries import android_standins
    data, layout = fixtures_apk.apk_basic()
    if layout_change:
        layout_change(layout)
    ref = InputRef(sha256_hex(data), len(data), "fixture.apk")
    return pipeline.query_bytes(data, ref, name, args, tools=android_standins(layout))


class ReportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_json_is_deterministic_and_complete(self):
        first, second = report.to_json(analysis()), report.to_json(analysis())
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        data = json.loads(first)
        self.assertEqual(data["contract"], "reverseai.contract/3")
        self.assertEqual(data["input"]["sha256"], sha256_hex(DATA))
        self.assertEqual(data["summary"], {"supported": 1, "derived": 0, "unsupported": 1, "contradicted": 0, "unreviewed": 0})
        verdicts = {f["claim_key"]: f["verdict"] for f in data["results"][0]["findings"]}
        self.assertEqual(verdicts, {"strings.urls": "supported", "capability.network": "unsupported"})

    def test_unreviewed_findings_are_counted_not_hidden(self):
        partial = analysis()
        partial = Analysis(partial.input, partial.tools, partial.results, partial.verdicts[:1])
        data = report.to_dict(partial)
        self.assertEqual(data["summary"]["unreviewed"], 1)

    def test_markdown_separates_rejected_claims_and_escapes_cells(self):
        text = report.to_markdown(analysis())
        supported, rejected = text.split("## Rejected or unreviewed claims")
        self.assertIn("URL strings in the input", supported)
        self.assertNotIn("The input contains a URL.", supported)
        self.assertIn("strings.extract @ 64+27", supported)
        self.assertIn("Claim with no evidence.", rejected)
        self.assertNotIn("Claim with no evidence.", supported)
        self.assertIn("a\\|b'c", supported)
        self.assertIn("The sample was not executed.", text)

    def test_cells_are_inert_code_spans(self):
        self.assertEqual(report._cell("x" * 300), "`" + "x" * 199 + "…`")
        self.assertEqual(report._cell("a|b`c"), "`a\\|b'c`")
        self.assertEqual(report._cell("\udcff\x00"), "`\ufffd\ufffd`")
        self.assertEqual(report._cell(""), "-")

    def test_analyst_prose_is_never_shown_as_a_verified_statement(self):
        data = report.to_dict(analysis())
        urls = [f for f in data["results"][0]["findings"] if f["claim_key"] == "strings.urls"][0]
        self.assertEqual((urls["claim"], urls["statement"]), ("The input contains a URL.", "URL strings in the input"))
        self.assertEqual(report.claims.statement("capability.ransomware"), "No claim rule")

    def test_no_supported_findings(self):
        text = report.to_markdown(analysis("unsupported"))
        self.assertIn("No finding was supported by the evidence.", text)

    def test_m3c_markdown_has_full_readable_derived_details_and_exact_json_values(self):
        original = code_analysis()
        text = report.to_markdown(original)
        supported, derived = text.split("## Derived by analysis tools (not verified against the bytes)")
        self.assertNotIn("MOV rax", supported)
        for marker in ("### Assembly (derived)", "### References (derived)", "### Referenced strings (derived)",
                       "| File offset | Length | Instruction |", "| `10` | `3` | `MOV rax, [message]` |",
                       "`message`", "`hello`", "`ascii`", "`0x1000`", "`0x2000`"):
            self.assertIn(marker, derived)
        self.assertIn("Truncated: `true`", derived)
        parsed = json.loads(report.to_json(original))
        self.assertEqual([f["value"] for f in parsed["results"][0]["findings"]],
                         [f.value for f in original.results[0].findings])

    def test_code_detail_addresses_are_hex_but_file_offsets_and_lengths_stay_decimal(self):
        text = report.to_markdown(code_analysis())
        self.assertIn("#### Function at `0x1000`", text)
        self.assertIn("| `0x1000` | `read` | `0x2000` | `message` |", text)
        self.assertIn('| `0x2000` | `ascii` | `hello` | `false` | `["0x1000"]` |', text)
        self.assertIn("| `10` | `3` | `MOV rax, [message]` |", text)

    def test_generic_m3c_values_format_only_addresses_without_mutating_json(self):
        original = code_analysis(instruction="MOV rax, 4096", name="8192", text="4096")
        before = report.to_json(original)
        generic = report.to_markdown(original).split("### Assembly (derived)")[0]
        expected = (
            {"entry": "0x1000", "instructions": [[2, 3, "MOV rax, 4096"]], "truncated": True},
            [["0x1000", "read", "0x2000", "8192"]],
            [{"address": "0x2000", "encoding": "ascii", "text": "4096", "truncated": False, "from": ["0x1000"]}],
        )
        for value in expected:
            self.assertIn(report._cell(value), generic)
        self.assertEqual(report.to_json(original), before)
        values = [f["value"] for f in json.loads(before)["results"][0]["findings"]]
        self.assertEqual(values[0]["entry"], 4096)
        self.assertEqual(values[1][0][2], 8192)
        self.assertEqual(values[2][0]["from"], [4096])

    def test_legacy_code_values_use_lowercase_hex_including_zero_and_uint64(self):
        original = code_analysis()
        result, = original.results
        values = (
            ("code.functions", ["4096"]),
            ("code.calls", [[0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, "8192"]]),
            ("code.pseudocode", {"entry": 0, "text": "return 4096;", "truncated": False}),
        )
        findings = tuple(make_finding("code", "Tool reading.", key, value, [result.evidence[0].id], "inferred")
                         for key, value in values)
        changed = Analysis(original.input, original.tools,
                           (AnalysisResult(result.task_id, "code", "ok", result.evidence, findings),),
                           tuple(ReviewVerdict(f.id, "derived", ("Tool reading; not verified.",)) for f in findings))
        before = report.to_json(changed)
        text = report.to_markdown(changed)
        for value in (["4096"], [["0xffffffffffffffff", "8192"]],
                      {"entry": "0x0", "text": "return 4096;", "truncated": False}):
            self.assertIn(report._cell(value), text)
        self.assertEqual(report.to_json(changed), before)
        parsed = json.loads(before)["results"][0]["findings"]
        self.assertEqual(parsed[1]["value"], [[18446744073709551615, "8192"]])
        self.assertEqual(parsed[2]["value"]["entry"], 0)

    def test_m3c_detail_cells_keep_hostile_text_inert(self):
        text = report.to_markdown(code_analysis(instruction="`<img src=x>|\nRET", name="[x](https://evil.invalid)",
                                               text="![p](x)`|"))
        import re
        count = 0
        for line in text.splitlines():
            if not line.startswith("|"):
                continue
            for cell in re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", line)[1:-1]:
                cell = cell.strip()
                if any(marker in cell for marker in ("<img", "](", "RET")):
                    count += 1
                    self.assertTrue(cell.startswith("`") and cell.endswith("`") and "`" not in cell[1:-1], cell)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(count, 3)

    def test_rejected_or_unreviewed_code_never_gets_derived_detail_tables(self):
        for status in ("unsupported", "unreviewed"):
            original = code_analysis(status="unsupported")
            if status == "unreviewed":
                original = Analysis(original.input, original.tools, original.results, ())
            text = report.to_markdown(original)
            self.assertNotIn("### Assembly", text)
            self.assertNotIn("### References", text)
            self.assertNotIn("### Referenced strings", text)

    def test_assembly_offsets_resolve_only_its_own_result_evidence(self):
        original = code_analysis()
        result, = original.results
        isolated = AnalysisResult(result.task_id, result.role, result.status, (), result.findings)
        foreign = AnalysisResult("tk-fedcba9876543210", "code", "ok", result.evidence, ())
        changed = Analysis(original.input, original.tools, (isolated, foreign), original.verdicts)
        text = report.to_markdown(changed)
        self.assertNotIn("| `10` | `3` |", text)

    def test_query_instruction_page_is_complete_paged_hex_and_inert_without_json_mutation(self):
        original = code_analysis()
        result, = original.results
        value = {"entry": 0x1000, "start": 64, "total": 100,
                 "rows": [[16, 1, "RET`|<img src=x>"], [17, 2, "CALL [4096]"]], "truncated": True}
        finding = make_finding("code", "Tool reading.", "code.instructions", value, [result.evidence[0].id], "inferred")
        current = Analysis(original.input, original.tools,
                           (AnalysisResult(result.task_id, "code", "ok", result.evidence, (finding,)),),
                           (ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "derived", ("Tool reading.",)),), (),
                           {"name": "procedure_assembly", "args": {"entry": 0x1000, "start": 64}})
        before = report.to_json(current)
        text = report.to_markdown(current)
        for marker in ('"entry":"0x1000"', "rows 64..65 of 100", "Next start: 66", "Truncated: `true`",
                       "| 64 | `0x1010` | `1` | `RET'\\|<img src=x>` |", "| 65 | `0x1011` | `2` | `CALL [4096]` |"):
            self.assertIn(marker, text)
        self.assertEqual(report.to_json(current), before)
        parsed = json.loads(before)
        self.assertEqual(parsed["query"]["args"]["entry"], 4096)
        self.assertEqual(parsed["results"][0]["findings"][0]["value"], value)

    def test_complete_query_page_has_no_next_start_and_addresses_are_hex(self):
        original = code_analysis()
        result, = original.results
        value = {"start": 9, "total": 10, "rows": [["<img src=x>|`", 0x2000, "func", "global", True]]}
        finding = make_finding("structural", "Reading.", "symbols.list", value, [result.evidence[0].id])
        current = Analysis(original.input, original.tools,
                           (AnalysisResult(result.task_id, "structural", "ok", result.evidence, (finding,)),),
                           (ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "supported", ()),), (), {"name": "list_names", "args": {"query": "x"}})
        text = report.to_markdown(current)
        self.assertIn("rows 9..9 of 10", text)
        self.assertNotIn("Next start:", text)
        self.assertIn("| 9 | `<img src=x>\\|'` | `0x2000` | `func` | `global` | `true` |", text)

    def test_android_evidence_names_its_member_and_child_offset(self):
        analysis = android_query("inspect_android_package", {})
        text = report.to_markdown(analysis)
        self.assertIn("apk.inventory @ ", text)  # central directory entries are in the input itself
        self.assertIn("apk.manifest in `AndroidManifest.xml` @ 0x", text)
        evidence = report.to_dict(analysis)["results"][0]["evidence"]
        manifest = [e for e in evidence if e["operation"] == "apk.manifest"]
        self.assertEqual({e["artifact"]["member"] for e in manifest}, {"AndroidManifest.xml"})
        self.assertIn(f"apk.manifest in `AndroidManifest.xml` @ {hex(manifest[0]['location']['offset'])}+20", text)
        self.assertTrue(all("artifact" not in e for e in evidence if e["operation"] == "apk.inventory"))

    def test_android_pages_are_readable_and_json_keeps_raw_values(self):
        analysis = android_query("inspect_android_package", {})

        self.assertRegex(text, r"\| 2 \| `classes2.dex` \| `stored` \|")

        self.assertRegex(text, r"\| 1 \| `classes2.dex` \| `Lorg/reverseai/fixture/Worker;` \| `run` \| `\(\)V` \| "
                               r"`0x[0-9a-f]+` \| `method` \| `Lorg/reverseai/fixture/Helper;->compute\(II\)I` \| `false` \|")
```

`tests/test_review.py`:

```py
import re
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from reverseai.analysts import structural
from reverseai.contract import (
    AnalysisResult, Evidence, InputRef, Location, Observation, ReviewVerdict, ToolRef, evidence_id, make_evidence, make_finding,
    sha256_hex,
)
from reverseai import review as review_module
from reverseai.review import review
from reverseai.tools import structure
from tests.fixtures_structure import elf, structure_evidence

TOOLS = {"structure": structure.TOOL}
REASON = re.compile(r"(ev-[0-9a-f]{16}: [a-zA-Z ]+|finding cites no evidence|finding does not match its ID"
                    r"|finding ID reused for different content|no claim rule for this claim_key"
                    r"|[a-z_.]+ may only cite [a-z_.]+(, [a-z_.]+)* evidence|[a-z_.]+ must be (observed|inferred)|cited evidence does not yield the claimed value"
                    r"|another finding gives [a-z_.]+ a different value)\Z")


def forged(evidence, **changes):
    """Evidence with altered fields and a matching ID, as a tampered result would carry it."""
    fields = {"input_sha256": evidence.input_sha256, "tool": evidence.tool, "operation": evidence.operation,
              "location": evidence.location, "excerpt_sha256": evidence.excerpt_sha256, "observation": evidence.observation}
    fields.update(changes)
    return Evidence(id=evidence_id(**fields), **fields)


class ReviewTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.data, _ = elf()
        self.input = InputRef(sha256=sha256_hex(self.data), size=len(self.data), name="sample")
        self.task = structural.plan(self.input)
        self.evidence = structure_evidence(self.data, self.task)
        self.identify = self.evidence[0]

    def result(self, findings, evidence=None, task_id=None):
        return AnalysisResult(task_id or self.task.id, "structural", "ok", tuple(self.evidence if evidence is None else evidence),
                              tuple(findings))

    def finding(self, value="elf", evidence_ids=None, claim_key="format.container"):
        ids = [self.identify.id] if evidence_ids is None else evidence_ids
        return make_finding("structural", "The input format.", claim_key, value, ids)

    def verdict(self, finding, evidence=None, data=None):
        verdicts = review(self.data if data is None else data, self.input, [self.result([finding], evidence)], TOOLS)
        self.assertEqual(len(verdicts), 1)
        for reason in verdicts[0].reasons:
            self.assertRegex(reason, REASON)  # short, names evidence IDs only
        return verdicts[0]

    def test_the_analyst_findings_are_supported(self):
        findings = structural.conclude(self.task, self.evidence)
        verdicts = review(self.data, self.input, [self.result(findings)], TOOLS)
        self.assertEqual(verdicts, tuple(ReviewVerdict(f.id, "supported") for f in sorted(findings, key=lambda f: f.id)))

    def test_missing_evidence(self):
        finding = self.finding(evidence_ids=["ev-0000000000000000"])
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding), ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", ("ev-0000000000000000: evidence missing",)))

    def test_tampered_excerpt(self):
        tampered = forged(self.identify, excerpt_sha256=sha256_hex(b"MZ\x90\x00"))
        finding = self.finding(evidence_ids=[tampered.id])
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding, [tampered]),
                         ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (f"{tampered.id}: excerpt hash mismatch",)))

    def test_wrong_tool_version(self):
        newer = make_evidence(self.data, ToolRef("structure", "0.1.1"), "structure.identify",
                              structure.identify(self.data, {})[0])
        finding = self.finding(evidence_ids=[newer.id])
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding, [newer]),
                         ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (f"{newer.id}: tool name or version not registered",)))
        unregistered = review(self.data, self.input, [self.result([self.finding()])], {})
        self.assertEqual(unregistered[0].reasons, (f"{self.identify.id}: tool name or version not registered",))

    def test_out_of_range_location(self):
        outside = forged(self.identify, location=Location(len(self.data) - 2, 4))
        finding = self.finding(evidence_ids=[outside.id])
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding, [outside]),
                         ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (f"{outside.id}: location outside the input",)))

    def test_no_evidence_cited(self):
        finding = self.finding(evidence_ids=[])
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding), ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", ("finding cites no evidence",)))

    def identify_as(self, kind, length=4):
        """Intact identify evidence over the input's first bytes that says `kind`: two tools that disagree."""
        return make_evidence(self.data, structure.REF, "structure.identify",
                             Observation(Location(0, length), {"format": kind, "magic": self.data[:length].hex()}))

    def test_contradiction_by_claim_key(self):
        pe_evidence = self.identify_as("pe")
        elf_finding, pe_finding = self.finding("elf"), self.finding("pe", [pe_evidence.id])
        verdicts = review(self.data, self.input, [self.result([elf_finding]), self.result([pe_finding], [pe_evidence])], TOOLS)
        reason = ("another finding gives format.container a different value",)
        self.assertEqual(verdicts, tuple(sorted((ReviewVerdict(elf_finding.id, "contradicted", reason),
                                                 ReviewVerdict(pe_finding.id, "contradicted", reason)), key=lambda v: v.finding_id)))

    def test_an_unsupported_finding_never_contradicts_a_verified_one(self):
        verified = self.finding("elf")
        for label, bogus, reason in (
                ("missing evidence", self.finding("pe", evidence_ids=["ev-0000000000000000"]), "ev-0000000000000000: evidence missing"),
                ("no evidence", self.finding("pe", evidence_ids=[]), "finding cites no evidence")):
            with self.subTest(label):
                verdicts = review(self.data, self.input, [self.result([verified]), self.result([bogus])], TOOLS)
                self.assertEqual(verdicts, tuple(sorted((ReviewVerdict(verified.id, "supported"),
                                                         ReviewVerdict(bogus.id, "unsupported", (reason,))),
                                                        key=lambda v: v.finding_id)))

    def test_two_verified_findings_that_agree_are_contradicted_by_a_third_that_differs(self):
        elf_again, pe_evidence = self.identify_as("elf", length=2), self.identify_as("pe")
        first, second, other = self.finding("elf"), self.finding("elf", [elf_again.id]), self.finding("pe", [pe_evidence.id])
        self.assertEqual(len({first.id, second.id, other.id}), 3)
        evidence = [*self.evidence, elf_again, pe_evidence]
        verdicts = review(self.data, self.input, [self.result([first, second, other], evidence)], TOOLS)
        reason = ("another finding gives format.container a different value",)
        self.assertEqual(verdicts, tuple(ReviewVerdict(finding_id, "contradicted", reason)
                                         for finding_id in sorted((first.id, second.id, other.id))))

    def test_citations_resolve_only_inside_the_findings_own_result(self):
        finding = self.finding("elf")
        elsewhere = self.result([], task_id="tk-0000000000000001")
        verdicts = review(self.data, self.input, [self.result([finding], evidence=[]), elsewhere], TOOLS)
        self.assertEqual(verdicts, (ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (f"{self.identify.id}: evidence missing",)),))

    def test_a_mutating_analyst_cannot_get_altered_evidence_or_values_supported(self):
        evidence = make_evidence(self.data, structure.REF, "structure.identify", structure.identify(self.data, {})[0])
        finding = self.finding("elf", [evidence.id])
        evidence.observation["format"] = "pe"  # an analyst edits the record it was handed
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding, [evidence]),
                         ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (f"{evidence.id}: record does not match its ID",)))
        sections = [item for item in self.evidence if item.operation == "structure.sections" and item.observation["name"] == ".rwx"]
        listed = make_finding("structural", "Writable and executable.", "sections.writable_executable", [".rwx"], [sections[0].id])
        listed.value.append(".text")  # a mutable value changed after the ID was bound
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(listed), ReviewVerdict(listed.id, "unsupported", ("finding does not match its ID",)))

    def test_one_finding_id_with_different_content_is_unsupported(self):
        original = self.finding("elf")
        changed = self.finding("elf")
        object.__setattr__(changed, "claim", "A different claim.")  # as a 64-bit ID collision would look
        with patch.object(review_module, "finding_intact", return_value=True):
            verdicts = review(self.data, self.input, [self.result([original]), self.result([changed])], TOOLS)
        self.assertEqual(verdicts, (ReviewVerdict(original.id, "unsupported", ("finding ID reused for different content",)),))

    def test_evidence_from_an_unregistered_operation(self):
        bogus = make_evidence(self.data, structure.REF, "structure.bogus", structure.identify(self.data, {})[0])
        finding = self.finding(evidence_ids=[bogus.id])
        self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding, [bogus]),
                         ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (f"{bogus.id}: operation not registered",)))

    def test_the_input_reference_must_describe_the_bytes(self):
        finding = self.finding("elf")
        for label, other, reason in (("size", InputRef(self.input.sha256, self.input.size + 1, "sample"), "input size mismatch"),
                                     ("hash", InputRef("0" * 64, self.input.size, "sample"), "input hash mismatch")):
            with self.subTest(label):
                verdicts = review(self.data, other, [self.result([finding])], TOOLS)
                self.assertEqual(verdicts, (ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (f"{self.identify.id}: {reason}",)),))

    def test_a_claim_must_follow_from_the_evidence_it_cites(self):
        headers = [item for item in self.evidence if item.operation == "structure.headers"][0]
        cases = (
            (self.finding("pe"), "cited evidence does not yield the claimed value"),
            (self.finding("elf", [headers.id]), "format.container may only cite lief.headers, structure.identify evidence"),
            (self.finding("elf", claim_key="format.colour"), "no claim rule for this claim_key"),
        )
        for finding, reason in cases:
            with self.subTest(reason=reason):
                self.assertEqual(self.verdict(finding), ReviewVerdict(finding.id, "unsupported", (reason,)))

    def test_changed_input_bytes_fail_every_item(self):
        changed = b"\x00" + self.data[1:]
        verdict = self.verdict(self.finding(), data=changed)
        self.assertEqual(verdict.status, "unsupported")
        self.assertEqual(verdict.reasons, (f"{self.identify.id}: input hash mismatch", f"{self.identify.id}: excerpt hash mismatch"))

    def test_one_verdict_per_finding_in_a_deterministic_order(self):
        findings = structural.conclude(self.task, self.evidence)
        twice = [self.result(findings), self.result(findings, task_id="tk-0000000000000001")]
        verdicts = review(self.data, self.input, twice, TOOLS)
        self.assertEqual([v.finding_id for v in verdicts], sorted(f.id for f in findings))
        self.assertEqual(verdicts, review(self.data, self.input, list(reversed(twice)), TOOLS))
        self.assertEqual(review(self.data, self.input, [], TOOLS), ())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`tests/test_review_guards.py`:

```py
"""Isolated reviewer guards for package-pointer bounds and permission page metadata."""

import unittest

from reverseai.contract import (
    AnalysisResult, InputRef, Location, Observation, OperationSpec, ToolRef, ToolSpec, content_id, make_evidence,
    make_finding, sha256_hex,
)
from reverseai.review import review

DATA = bytes(range(256)) * 4
INPUT = InputRef(sha256_hex(DATA), len(DATA), "fixture.bin")


def verdict(tool, operation, observation, key, value):
    ref = ToolRef(tool, "0.1.0")
    tools = {tool: ToolSpec(ref, {operation: OperationSpec(operation, {}, lambda d, a: [])})}
    item = make_evidence(DATA, ref, operation, Observation(Location(0, 8), observation))
    finding = make_finding("structural", "Rows.", key, value, [item.id], "observed")
    result = AnalysisResult(content_id("tk", {"k": key}), "structural", "ok", (item,), (finding,))
    return review(DATA, INPUT, [result], tools)[0].status


class ReviewerGuardTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_package_pointer_longer_than_255_characters_is_refused(self):
        for path, expected in (("/" + "p" * 254, "supported"), ("/" + "p" * 255, "unsupported")):
            row = {"file": "package.json", "path": path, "value": "x", "truncated": False}
            page = {"start": 0, "total": 1, "rows": [["package.json", path, "x", False]]}
            self.assertEqual(verdict("js", "js.package", {"kind": "package_field", "index": 0, "total": 1, **row},
                                     "javascript.package", page), expected, len(path))

    def test_permission_index_and_total_must_be_integers_not_booleans(self):
        def attribute(index, total):
            return {"kind": "manifest_attribute", "index": index, "total": total, "element_index": 1,
                    "element": "uses-permission", "attribute": "android:name", "type": "string", "value": "p.A"}
        self.assertEqual(verdict("apk", "apk.manifest", attribute(0, 1), "android.permissions", ["p.A"]), "supported")
        for index, total in ((False, 1), (0, True), (True, 2)):
            self.assertEqual(verdict("apk", "apk.manifest", attribute(index, total), "android.permissions", ["p.A"]),
                             "unsupported", (index, total))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

`tests/test_revise_ghidra_image.py`:

```py
"""Offline image revision protocol tests. All Docker interactions are inert fakes."""

import contextlib
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from tests.test_build_ghidra_image import FakeDocker, build


PARENT = "sha256:ac77fda75da8580e0479087580f83b6e5495fb16df97b9696a2bdf3ae100f452"
FILES = {"worker.py", "project_cache.py", "ghidra_scripts/ReverseAIOptions.java",
         "ghidra_scripts/ReverseAIQuery.java", "ghidra_scripts/ReverseAIPrepare.java"}
ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES = {key: "" for key in ("DOCKER_HOST", "DOCKER_CONTEXT", "DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY", "DOCKER_CERT_PATH", "BUILDX_BUILDER")}


class RevisionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(temporary.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(temporary.name)
        self.source = self.root / "source"
        shutil.copytree(build.SOURCE, self.source)
        for name in FILES:
            (self.source / name).write_bytes(("reviewed " + name + "\n").encode())
        self.lock = self.root / "image.lock.json"
        self.docker = FakeDocker()

    def revise(self, route="B", *extra):
        with patch.object(build, "SOURCE", self.source), patch.object(build, "docker", self.docker), \
                patch.dict(os.environ, ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES), contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), \
                patch.object(build, "fetch", side_effect=AssertionError("offline route downloaded")):
            return build.main(["revise", "--route", route, "--lock", str(self.lock), *extra])

    def assert_clean(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.containers, {})
        created = [args[args.index("--name") + 1] for args in self.docker.calls if args[0] == "create"]
        removed = [args[2] for args in self.docker.calls if args[0] == "rm"]
        self.assertCountEqual(created, removed)
        self.assertFalse(any(args[0] in ("start", "run", "exec", "pull") for args in self.docker.calls))

    def test_B_never_starts_or_builds_and_copies_only_the_reviewed_files(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.revise(), 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls[0], ("image", "inspect", PARENT))
        creates = [args for args in self.docker.calls if args[0] == "create"]
        self.assertEqual(len(creates), 2)
        for args, image_id in zip(creates, (PARENT, self.docker.image_id)):
            self.assertEqual(args[:6], ("create", "--pull=never", "--platform", "linux/arm64", "--network=none", "--name"))
            self.assertEqual(args[7:], (image_id,))
        uploads = [args for args in self.docker.calls if args[0] == "cp" and ":/opt/" not in args[1]]
        self.assertEqual({args[2].split(":/opt/reverseai/")[1] for args in uploads}, FILES)
        self.assertEqual(len(uploads), 5)
        self.assertEqual([args[0] for args in self.docker.calls].count("commit"), 1)
        self.assertFalse(any(args[0] in ("build", "info", "context") for args in self.docker.calls))
        lock = json.loads(self.lock.read_text())
        self.assertEqual(set(lock), {"adapter_version", "base_digest", "ghidra_sha256", "jdk_sha256", "parent_image_id",
                                     "bundle_sha256", "cache_format", "image_id", "platform"})
        self.assertEqual((lock["parent_image_id"], lock["adapter_version"], lock["cache_format"]), (PARENT, "12.1.4-r7", 1))
        self.assertEqual(lock["ghidra_sha256"], "ddac49f903da9d5bac833e5cc79395098b9c33cfd3279be5f31bd00387d2d4db")
        self.assertEqual(lock["jdk_sha256"], "23e37e026f12f3e706f18938ff611db3032d075b09d0879a25d06718c773e223")
        self.assert_clean()

    def test_A_uses_only_the_closed_context_and_forces_local_legacy_resolution(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.revise("A"), 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls[0], ("image", "inspect", PARENT))
        built, = [args for args in self.docker.calls if args[0] == "build"]
        self.assertEqual(built[:5], ("build", "--platform", "linux/arm64", "--pull=false", "--network=none"))
        self.assertEqual(built[5:9], ("--iidfile", built[6], "--tag", "reverseai-ghidra:12.1.4-r7"))
        self.assertEqual(len(built), 10)
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.legacy_calls, [built])
        self.assertEqual(set(self.docker.context), {"Dockerfile", "ghidra_scripts", *FILES})
        self.assertFalse(any(args[0] == "commit" for args in self.docker.calls))
        self.assert_clean()

    def test_legacy_subprocess_explicitly_overrides_ambient_buildkit(self):
        completed = subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0, stdout="ok\n")
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"DOCKER_BUILDKIT": "1"}), patch.object(build.subprocess, "run", return_value=completed) as run:
            self.assertEqual(build.docker("build", "context", capture=True, legacy=True), "ok")
        self.assertEqual(run.call_args.args[0], ["docker", "build", "context"])
        self.assertEqual(run.call_args.kwargs["env"]["DOCKER_BUILDKIT"], "0")
        self.assertTrue(run.call_args.kwargs["check"])

    def test_missing_or_aliased_parent_fails_before_any_other_docker_command(self):
        for route in ("A", "B"):
            with self.subTest(route=route, reason="missing"):
                self.docker = FakeDocker()
                self.docker.failure = lambda args: args[:2] == ("image", "inspect")
                with self.assertRaises(subprocess.CalledProcessError):
                    self.revise(route)
                self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls, [("image", "inspect", PARENT)])
            with self.subTest(route=route, reason="wrong identity"):
                self.docker = FakeDocker()
                self.docker.info_changes[PARENT] = {"Id": "sha256:" + "b" * 64}
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "image ID differs"):
                    self.revise(route)
                self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls, [("image", "inspect", PARENT)])
        self.assertFalse(self.lock.exists())

    def test_unknown_remote_or_containerd_A_backend_refuses_before_create_or_build(self):
        for key, value in (("Driver", "btrfs"), ("Driver", "overlayfs"), ("ServerVersion", "29.0.0"), ("ServerVersion", "28.5.1-vendor"),
                           ("OSType", "windows"), ("Architecture", "amd64"),
                           ("DriverStatus", [["driver-type", "io.containerd.snapshotter.v1"]])):
            with self.subTest(key=key, value=value):
                self.docker = FakeDocker()
                self.docker.server[key] = value
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "recognized local legacy Engine"):
                    self.revise("A")
                self.assertFalse(any(args[0] in ("create", "build") for args in self.docker.calls))
        self.docker = FakeDocker()
        self.docker.endpoint = "tcp://docker.example:2375"
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "recognized local legacy Engine"):
            self.revise("A")
        self.assertFalse(self.lock.exists())

    def test_A_endpoint_or_driver_environment_override_is_refused(self):
        for key in ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES:
            with self.subTest(key=key), patch.dict(os.environ, dict(ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES, **{key: "override"})), \
                    patch.object(build, "docker", self.docker):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "endpoint or builder overrides"):
                    build.preflight_legacy_builder()
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls, [])

    def test_unreviewed_revision_instructions_are_refused_before_creation(self):
        path = self.source / "Dockerfile.revise"
        original = path.read_text()
        mutations = [original + line + "\n" for line in ("RUN true", "ADD https://example.invalid/a /a",
                     "FROM busybox", "COPY --from=other /a /a", "ARG PARENT", "ENV PATH=/attacker", "USER root")]
        mutations += ["# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1\n" + original,
                      original.replace("COPY worker.py /opt/reverseai/worker.py", "COPY . /opt/reverseai/"),
                      original.replace("COPY worker.py", "CO\\\nPY worker.py").replace("USER 65534:65534", "RUN --network=none true\nUSER 65534:65534"),
                      original.replace(PARENT, "reverseai-ghidra:12.1.4-r6")]
        for index, text in enumerate(mutations):
            with self.subTest(index=index):
                self.docker = FakeDocker()
                path.write_text(text)
                with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                    self.revise()
                self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls, [("image", "inspect", PARENT)])
        self.assertFalse(self.lock.exists())

    def test_extra_script_or_symlink_bundle_is_refused_before_docker(self):
        extra = self.source / "ghidra_scripts/Evil.java"
        extra.write_bytes(b"unreviewed")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "script file set"):
            self.revise()
        extra.unlink()
        helper = self.source / "project_cache.py"
        helper.unlink()
        helper.symlink_to("worker.py")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "regular files"):
            self.revise()
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls, [])

    def test_staged_revision_dockerfile_is_rechecked_after_a_concurrent_source_change(self):
        original_copy = shutil.copy2

        def replace_during_copy(source, target, *args, **kwargs):
            result = original_copy(source, target, *args, **kwargs)
            if Path(source).name == "Dockerfile.revise":
                with Path(target).open("a") as stream:
                    stream.write("RUN true\n")
            return result

        with patch.object(build.shutil, "copy2", side_effect=replace_during_copy):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(SystemExit, "revision Dockerfile"):
                self.revise()
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls, [("image", "inspect", PARENT)])
        self.assertFalse(self.lock.exists())

    def test_runtime_tree_hashes_symlink_targets_without_following_them(self):
        folder = self.root / "runtime"
        folder.mkdir()
        outside = self.root / "outside"
        outside.mkdir()
        (outside / "secret").write_bytes(b"never hashed through the link")
        (folder / "linked").symlink_to(outside, target_is_directory=True)
        with patch.object(build, "file_sha256", side_effect=AssertionError("followed a symlink")):
            before = build.tree_hashes(folder)
            (folder / "linked").unlink()
            (folder / "linked").symlink_to(self.root, target_is_directory=True)
            after = build.tree_hashes(folder)
        self.assertEqual(set(before), {"linked"})
        self.assertEqual(before["linked"][0], "link")
        self.assertNotEqual(before, after)

    def test_parent_layer_or_runtime_configuration_drift_never_publishes(self):
        baseline = self.docker.image(self.docker.image_id)
        cases = [{"RootFS": {"Type": "layers", "Layers": ["sha256:" + "f" * 64]}}]
        for field, value in (("User", "0"), ("Entrypoint", ["sh"]), ("Env", ["PATH=/evil"]), ("Cmd", ["sh"]),
                             ("WorkingDir", "/evil"), ("Volumes", {"/samples": {}}), ("OnBuild", ["RUN touch /evil"]),
                             ("Healthcheck", {"Test": ["CMD", "sh"]})):
            config = dict(baseline["Config"], **{field: value})
            cases.append({"Config": config})
        for index, changed in enumerate(cases):
            with self.subTest(index=index):
                self.docker = FakeDocker()
                self.docker.info_changes[self.docker.image_id] = changed
                with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                    self.revise()
                self.assert_clean()
                self.assertFalse(self.lock.exists())

    def test_runtime_byte_mode_and_bundle_drift_are_detected_from_stopped_snapshots(self):
        changes = [{("jdk", "bin/java"): (b"changed JDK", 0o755)},
                   {("ghidra", "support/analyzeHeadless"): (b"changed Ghidra", 0o755)},
                   {("ghidra", "support/analyzeHeadless"): (b"fixed headless bytes", 0o644)},
                   {("reverseai", "worker.py"): (b"unreviewed worker", 0o644)},
                   {("reverseai", "project_cache.py"): ((self.source / "project_cache.py").read_bytes(), 0o600)},
                   {("reverseai", "ghidra_scripts/Unexpected.java"): (b"extra script", 0o644)}]
        for route in ("A", "B"):
            for changed in changes:
                with self.subTest(route=route, changed=list(changed)):
                    self.docker = FakeDocker()
                    self.docker.result_changes = changed
                    with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                        self.revise(route)
                    self.assert_clean()
                    self.assertFalse(self.lock.exists())

    def test_create_copy_commit_build_or_verification_failures_always_remove_stopped_containers(self):
        cases = [("B", lambda args: args[0] == "create"),
                 ("B", lambda args: args[:2] == ("container", "inspect")),
                 ("B", lambda args: args[0] == "cp" and ":/opt/" in args[1]),
                 ("B", lambda args: args[0] == "cp" and ":/opt/" not in args[1]),
                 ("B", lambda args: args[0] == "commit"),
                 ("A", lambda args: args[0] == "build"),
                 ("B", lambda args: args[:2] == ("image", "inspect") and args[2] != PARENT)]
        self.lock.write_bytes(b"existing approved lock\n")
        for route, failure in cases:
            with self.subTest(route=route, failure=failure):
                self.docker = FakeDocker()
                self.docker.failure = failure
                with self.assertRaises(subprocess.CalledProcessError):
                    self.revise(route)
                self.assert_clean()
                self.assertEqual(self.lock.read_bytes(), b"existing approved lock\n")
                self.assertEqual(sorted(path.name for path in self.root.glob("image.lock.json.*")), [])

    def test_bundle_identity_covers_every_file_and_is_independent_of_map_order(self):
        hashes = {name: hashlib.sha256((self.source / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for name in FILES}
        canonical = json.dumps(hashes, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("ascii")
        expected = hashlib.sha256(canonical).hexdigest()
        self.assertEqual(build.bundle_digest(dict(reversed(list(hashes.items())))), expected)
        self.revise()
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.lock.read_text())["bundle_sha256"], expected)
        for name in FILES:
            path = self.source / name
            body = path.read_bytes()
            path.write_bytes(body + b"changed\n")
            self.docker = FakeDocker()
            self.revise()
            self.assertNotEqual(json.loads(self.lock.read_text())["bundle_sha256"], expected)
            path.write_bytes(body)

    def test_revision_download_flags_are_rejected_even_if_assets_were_present(self):
        for extra in (("--download",), ("--download-dir", str(self.root))):
            with self.subTest(extra=extra), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
                with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                    self.revise("B", *extra)
        self.assertEqual(self.docker.calls, [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

```py
import unittest

from reverseai.contract import MAX_EXCERPT_BYTES, ContractError, ToolRef
from reverseai.tools.strings import TOOL
from tests.fixtures_strings import clean_control, known_strings


def observe(operation, data, **args):
    spec = TOOL.operations["strings." + operation]
    return spec.handler(data, spec.validate_args(args))


def records(observations):
    return [(item.location.offset, item.location.length, item.value) for item in observations]


class StringsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_tool_identity_and_argument_defaults(self):
        self.assertEqual(TOOL.ref, ToolRef("strings", "0.1.0"))
        self.assertEqual(TOOL.operations["strings.extract"].validate_args({}), {
            "encoding": "ascii", "max_strings": 1024, "min_length": 6,
        })
        self.assertEqual(TOOL.operations["strings.indicators"].validate_args({}), {"ruleset": "default"})

    def test_exact_ascii_extraction_at_declared_offsets(self):
        data, expected, _ = known_strings()
        self.assertEqual(records(observe("extract", data)), expected["ascii"])

    def test_exact_utf16le_extraction_at_declared_offsets(self):
        data, expected, _ = known_strings()
        self.assertEqual(records(observe("extract", data, encoding="utf16le")), expected["utf16le"])

    def test_exact_indicator_rules_matches_and_byte_ranges(self):
        data, _, expected = known_strings()
        actual = records(observe("indicators", data))
        self.assertEqual(actual, expected)
        self.assertEqual(len(actual), 16)

    def test_wide_strings_can_start_at_odd_byte_offsets(self):
        text = "VirtualAllocEx https://odd.example.invalid"
        data = b"\xff" + text.encode("utf-16le") + b"\xff"
        extracted = records(observe("extract", data, encoding="utf16le"))
        self.assertEqual(extracted, [(1, len(text) * 2, {
            "text": text, "encoding": "utf16le", "truncated": False,
        })])
        actual = records(observe("indicators", data))
        self.assertEqual(actual[0], (1, 28, {
            "rule": "virtual_alloc_ex", "category": "process_injection", "match": "VirtualAllocEx",
        }))
        self.assertEqual(actual[1][0], 31)

    def test_minimum_length_and_maximum_count(self):
        data = b"four\x00short\x00sixsix\x00seventh\x00"
        self.assertEqual([o.value["text"] for o in observe("extract", data)], ["sixsix", "seventh"])
        self.assertEqual([o.value["text"] for o in observe("extract", data, min_length=4, max_strings=2)], ["four", "short"])

    def test_long_ascii_and_wide_strings_have_bounded_text_and_excerpt(self):
        for encoding, codec in (("ascii", "ascii"), ("utf16le", "utf-16le")):
            with self.subTest(encoding=encoding):
                data = b"\xff" + ("a" * 5000).encode(codec) + b"\xff"
                observations = observe("extract", data, encoding=encoding)
                self.assertEqual(len(observations), 1)
                self.assertEqual(records(observations), [(1, MAX_EXCERPT_BYTES, {
                    "text": "a" * 256, "encoding": encoding, "truncated": True,
                })])

    def test_exact_text_limit_is_not_marked_truncated(self):
        self.assertEqual(observe("extract", b"a" * 256)[0].value["truncated"], False)
        self.assertEqual(observe("extract", b"a" * 257)[0].value["truncated"], True)

    def test_clean_control_has_strings_and_no_indicators(self):
        self.assertTrue(observe("extract", clean_control()))
        self.assertEqual(observe("indicators", clean_control()), [])

    def test_empty_short_and_non_printable_inputs(self):
        for data in (b"", b"abc", bytes(range(32)), b"\xff\x80\x00"):
            with self.subTest(data=data):
                self.assertEqual(observe("extract", data), [])
                self.assertEqual(observe("extract", data, encoding="utf16le"), [])
                self.assertEqual(observe("indicators", data), [])

    def test_unknown_or_out_of_bounds_arguments_refused(self):
        for args in ({"min_length": 3}, {"min_length": 65}, {"min_length": True},
                     {"max_strings": 0}, {"max_strings": 4097}, {"encoding": "utf8"},
                     {"path": "/tmp/x"}):
            with self.subTest(args=args), self.assertRaises(ContractError):
                observe("extract", b"inert", **args)
        with self.assertRaises(ContractError):
            observe("indicators", b"inert", ruleset="download")

    def test_api_boundaries_and_invalid_ipv4_control(self):
        data = (b"ReOpenProcess CreateRemoteThreaded sockets reconnect "
                b"256.1.2.3 1.2.3.999 01.2.3.4 x1.2.3.4 1.2.3.4.5")
        self.assertEqual(observe("indicators", data), [])

    def test_valid_ipv4_edges(self):
        data = b"0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255"
        self.assertEqual(records(observe("indicators", data)), [
            (0, 7, {"rule": "ipv4", "category": "network", "match": "0.0.0.0"}),
            (8, 15, {"rule": "ipv4", "category": "network", "match": "255.255.255.255"}),
        ])

    def test_remaining_rule_table_positive_controls(self):
        cases = (
            ("NtMapViewOfSection", "nt_map_view_of_section", "process_injection"),
            ("QueueUserAPC", "queue_user_apc", "process_injection"),
            (r"Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce", "registry_run_once", "persistence"),
            ("CreateServiceW", "create_service", "persistence"),
            ("InternetOpenA", "internet_open", "network"),
            ("socket", "socket", "network"),
            ("connect", "connect", "network"),
            ("CryptAcquireContextW", "crypt_acquire_context", "crypto"),
            ("NtQueryInformationProcess", "nt_query_information_process", "anti_debug"),
        )
        for text, rule, category in cases:
            for encoding, width in (("ascii", 1), ("utf-16le", 2)):
                with self.subTest(rule=rule, encoding=encoding):
                    self.assertEqual(records(observe("indicators", text.encode(encoding))), [
                        (0, len(text) * width, {"rule": rule, "category": category, "match": text}),
                    ])

    def test_case_insensitive_match_keeps_exact_input_spelling(self):
        self.assertEqual(records(observe("indicators", b"virtualallocex")), [
            (0, 14, {"rule": "virtual_alloc_ex", "category": "process_injection", "match": "virtualallocex"}),
        ])

    def test_chunk_boundary_matches_once_with_exact_byte_offsets(self):
        for text in ("VirtualAllocEx", "https://boundary.example.invalid/path", "203.0.113.7"):
            for codec, width in (("ascii", 1), ("utf-16le", 2)):
                with self.subTest(text=text, codec=codec):
                    source = " " * 4091 + text + " " * 4100
                    actual = observe("indicators", source.encode(codec))
                    self.assertEqual(len(actual), 1)
                    self.assertEqual(actual[0].location.offset, 4091 * width)
                    self.assertEqual(actual[0].location.length, len(text) * width)
                    self.assertEqual(actual[0].value["match"], text)

    def test_chunk_boundary_does_not_create_false_word_boundary(self):
        source = b"x" * 4096 + b"OpenProcess" + b"x" * 4096
        self.assertEqual(observe("indicators", source), [])

    def test_long_runs_are_joined_across_bounded_scanner_blocks(self):
        for codec, label, width in (("ascii", "ascii", 1), ("utf-16le", "utf16le", 2)):
            with self.subTest(codec=codec):
                text = "x" * 20_000 + " VirtualAllocEx"
                data = b"\xff" + text.encode(codec) + b"\xff"
                self.assertEqual(len(observe("extract", data, encoding=label)), 1)
                self.assertEqual(records(observe("indicators", data)), [
                    (1 + 20_001 * width, 14 * width, {
                        "rule": "virtual_alloc_ex", "category": "process_injection", "match": "VirtualAllocEx",
                    }),
                ])

    def test_indicator_flood_has_bounded_handler_output_and_sentinel(self):
        observations = observe("indicators", b"OpenProcess " * 10_000)
        self.assertEqual(len(observations), 4097)
        self.assertEqual(TOOL.operations["strings.indicators"].max_observations, 4096)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```
