```py
def wheel_sha256():
    """The one hash pinned in requirements.txt."""
    pinned = re.findall(r"--hash=sha256:([0-9a-f]{64})", (SOURCE / "requirements.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if len(pinned) != 1:
        raise SystemExit("requirements.txt must pin exactly one SHA-256")
    return pinned[0]


def logical_instructions(text):
    """Logical instructions as BuildKit reads them: a line ending in exactly one backslash (then only spaces or tabs)
    continues on the next one, comment and empty lines inside a continuation are skipped, and nothing is inserted at
    the join (A\\ then DD is ADD). A run of two or more trailing backslashes ends its instruction: measured natively
    with buildx v0.37.2 for runs of 1 to 5. Lines are split on LF only: the caller has refused every other
    control byte."""
    joined, current = [], None
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if current is None:
            line = line.lstrip(" \t")
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            current = ""
        elif not line.strip(" \t") or line.lstrip(" \t").startswith("#"):
            continue
        end = re.search(r"(\\+)[ \t]*$", line)
        if end and len(end.group(1)) == 1:
            current += line[:end.end(1) - 1]
        else:
            joined.append(current + line)
            current = None
    if current is not None:
        joined.append(current)
    return [words for words in (line.split() for line in joined) if words]


def check_dockerfile(path):
    """The lock records BASE_DIGEST, so the Dockerfile must build from exactly BASE and nothing else: ASCII without
    control bytes (a BOM or a form feed would hide a directive or an instruction), one FROM line, no ADD (remote URLs, Git), no COPY --from or RUN --mount ...from= (another
    image or stage), no parser directive (# syntax=, # escape=) and exactly one line USER 65534:65534. Instructions
    are counted case-insensitively and continuations are joined first, so neither hides one."""
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    if not raw.isascii() or re.search(rb"[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]|\r(?!\n)", raw):
        raise SystemExit("Dockerfile must be ASCII without control bytes (tab, LF and CRLF only)")
    text = raw.decode("ascii").replace("\r\n", "\n")
    lines = [line.strip(" \t") for line in text.split("\n") if line.strip(" \t")]
    instructions = logical_instructions(text)
    if [words for words in instructions if words[0].upper() == "FROM"] != [["FROM", BASE]]:
        raise SystemExit("Dockerfile FROM differs from the pinned base " + BASE)
    if any(re.match(r"#\s*\w+\s*=", line) for line in lines):
        raise SystemExit("Dockerfile parser directives are refused")
    if any(words[0].upper() == "ADD" for words in instructions):
        raise SystemExit("Dockerfile ADD is refused")
    flags = [word.lower() for words in instructions for word in words if word.startswith("--")]
    if any(flag.startswith("--from") or (flag.startswith("--mount") and "from=" in flag) for flag in flags):
        raise SystemExit("Dockerfile reads from another image or stage")
    if [words for words in instructions if words[0].upper() == "USER"] != [["USER", "65534:65534"]]:
        raise SystemExit("Dockerfile must have exactly one USER 65534:65534")


def file_sha256(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


class RefuseRedirects(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        raise SystemExit("the wheel URL redirected; refusing to follow it")


def fetch_wheel(target, expected):
    # The one fixed HTTPS URL on PyPI's file host; any redirect is refused, so no other URL or host is ever requested.
    if not WHEEL_URL.startswith(WHEEL_HOST) or not WHEEL_URL.endswith("/" + WHEEL):
        raise SystemExit("the wheel URL is not the pinned PyPI file")
    with urllib.request.build_opener(RefuseRedirects).open(WHEEL_URL, timeout=60) as response:
        data = response.read(WHEEL_BYTES_LIMIT + 1)
    if len(data) > WHEEL_BYTES_LIMIT or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != expected:
        raise SystemExit("downloaded wheel does not match the pinned SHA-256")
    target.write_bytes(data)


def docker(*args, capture=False):
    result = subprocess.run(["docker", *args], check=True, text=True, capture_output=capture)
    return result.stdout.strip() if capture else None


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--wheel-dir", type=Path, required=True, help="Private directory holding the pinned YARA-X wheel")
    parser.add_argument("--download", action="store_true", help="Fetch the pinned wheel into --wheel-dir if it is missing")
    parser.add_argument("--tag", default="reverseai-yarax:" + ADAPTER_VERSION)
    parser.add_argument("--lock", type=Path, default=SOURCE / "image.lock.json")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    check_dockerfile(SOURCE / "Dockerfile")
    expected = wheel_sha256()
    wheel = args.wheel_dir / WHEEL
    if not wheel.is_file():
        if not args.download:
            raise SystemExit(f"missing {WHEEL} in --wheel-dir (or pass --download)")
        args.wheel_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fetch_wheel(wheel, expected)
    if file_sha256(wheel) != expected:
        raise SystemExit("wheel does not match the pinned SHA-256")

    try:
        docker("image", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Id}}", BASE, capture=True)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        raise SystemExit("the pinned base " + BASE + " is not present locally; this tool never pulls") from None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reverseai-yarax-build-") as temporary:
        context = Path(temporary)
        for name in ("Dockerfile", "requirements.txt", "worker.py", RULESET):
            shutil.copy2(SOURCE / name, context / name)
        ruleset_sha256 = file_sha256(context / RULESET)  # the bytes the image copies
        (context / "wheels").mkdir()
        shutil.copy2(wheel, context / "wheels" / WHEEL)
        iidfile = context / "image.id"
        docker("build", "--platform", PLATFORM, "--network", "none", "--pull=false", "--iidfile", str(iidfile),
               "--tag", args.tag, str(context))
        image_id = iidfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    if not re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", image_id):
        raise SystemExit("docker build returned no image ID")
    lock = {"image_id": image_id, "platform": PLATFORM, "base_digest": BASE_DIGEST, "wheel_sha256": expected,
            "ruleset_sha256": ruleset_sha256, "adapter_version": ADAPTER_VERSION}
    text = json.dumps(lock, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
    args.lock.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(text, end="")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/hive_check.py`:

```py
"""Deterministic citation check for an AI analyst team's claims.

Agents in the hive (see docs/HIVE.md) cite the findings that ReverseAI returned
to them over MCP. This checker trusts none of the agents' transcripts: it runs
every cited question again through ReverseAI itself, with the same mapping the
MCP server uses, and keeps a claim only when each of its citations names a
finding that the fresh report contains with a `supported` or `derived` verdict.
Finding IDs are content-bound, so a citation can only resolve if the same file,
tool, operation and result produce it again.

It checks citations, not prose: whether the claim's sentence follows from the
cited findings is the council's judgement. It never executes the input.

    python tools/hive_check.py --inputs DIR --claims claims.json --out NEW_DIR [--with-ghidra] [--jobs 2]

claims.json:

    {"file": "program",
     "claims": [{"id": "main-usage",
                 "text": "Without arguments the program prints its usage line and exits 1.",
                 "citations": [{"tool": "search_strings", "args": {"query": "usage"},
                                "id": "fi-0123456789abcdef"}]}]}

`file` is the relative name inside DIR (a citation may override it with its own
`file`); `args` are the MCP tool arguments. The output directory receives
verdicts.json and one folder per distinct question. Exit status: 0 when every
claim is confirmed, 1 when any claim is rejected, 2 on a usage error.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from reverseai import mcp_tools  # noqa: E402

TOOLS = ("lief", "yarax", "ghidra", "jadx", "jsparser")
ID = re.compile(r"(fi|ev)-[0-9a-f]{16}\Z")
CLAIM_ID = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}\Z")
KEPT = ("supported", "derived")
MAX_CLAIMS = 5000
MAX_CITATIONS = 32
MAX_QUESTIONS = 1000
QUESTION_TIMEOUT = 1500


class UsageError(ValueError):
    pass


def _require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise UsageError(message)


def load_claims(path):
    try:
        data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise UsageError(f"cannot read claims: {error}") from None
    _require(isinstance(data, dict), "claims file must be a JSON object")
    default_file = data.get("file")
    _require(default_file is None or isinstance(default_file, str), "'file' must be a string")
    claims = data.get("claims")
    _require(isinstance(claims, list) and 0 < len(claims) <= MAX_CLAIMS,
             f"'claims' must be a list of 1..{MAX_CLAIMS} claims")
    seen = set()
    for claim in claims:
        _require(isinstance(claim, dict), "each claim must be an object")
        _require(isinstance(claim.get("id"), str) and CLAIM_ID.match(claim["id"]),
                 "each claim needs an 'id' of letters, digits and ._:- (at most 128)")
        _require(claim["id"] not in seen, f"duplicate claim id {claim['id']}")
        seen.add(claim["id"])
        _require(isinstance(claim.get("text"), str), f"claim {claim['id']}: 'text' must be a string")
        citations = claim.get("citations")
        _require(isinstance(citations, list) and len(citations) <= MAX_CITATIONS,
                 f"claim {claim['id']}: 'citations' must be a list of at most {MAX_CITATIONS}")
        for citation in citations:
            _require(isinstance(citation, dict), f"claim {claim['id']}: each citation must be an object")
            _require(isinstance(citation.get("tool"), str), f"claim {claim['id']}: citation needs 'tool'")
            _require(isinstance(citation.get("args", {}), dict), f"claim {claim['id']}: 'args' must be an object")
            _require(isinstance(citation.get("id"), str) and ID.match(citation["id"]),
                     f"claim {claim['id']}: citation 'id' must be a fi-/ev- ID")
            file = citation.get("file", citation.get("args", {}).get("file", default_file))
            _require(isinstance(file, str), f"claim {claim['id']}: no input file for a citation")
    return default_file, claims


def question_key(citation, default_file):
    args = dict(citation.get("args", {}))
    args["file"] = citation.get("file", args.get("file", default_file))
    return json.dumps({"tool": citation["tool"], "args": args}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def run_question(key, number, *, inputs, out, enabled, runner, timeout):
    question = json.loads(key)
    folder = out / "questions" / f"{number:04d}"
    try:
        argv = mcp_tools.command(question["tool"], question["args"], root=str(inputs),
                                 out=str(folder), enabled=enabled)
    except Exception as error:  # the MCP layer's own refusals: unknown tool, bad arguments, refused path
        return {"status": "refused", "detail": type(error).__name__ + (f": {error}" if str(error) else "")}
    folder.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    try:
        completed = runner(argv, timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"status": "failed", "detail": f"no answer within {timeout} s"}
    report = folder / "report.json"
    if completed.returncode != 0 or not report.is_file():
        tail = (completed.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()[-1:] or [""]
        return {"status": "failed", "detail": f"exit {completed.returncode}: {tail[0][:300]}"}
    data = json.loads(report.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    findings, evidence = {}, {}
    for result in data.get("results", []):
        for finding in result.get("findings", []):
            findings[finding["id"]] = finding["verdict"]
            for evidence_id in finding.get("evidence_ids", []):
                if finding["verdict"] in KEPT or evidence_id not in evidence:
                    evidence[evidence_id] = finding["verdict"]
        for item in result.get("evidence", []):
            evidence.setdefault(item["id"], "unreviewed")
    return {"status": "ok", "input_sha256": data["input"]["sha256"], "folder": str(folder.relative_to(out)),
            "findings": findings, "evidence": evidence}


def default_runner(argv, timeout):
    command = [sys.executable, "-B", "-m", "reverseai", *argv]
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(ROOT) + (os.pathsep + env["PYTHONPATH"] if env.get("PYTHONPATH") else "")
    return subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=env, check=False)


def judge(claims, default_file, answers):
    verdicts = []
    for claim in claims:
        reasons, kinds = [], []
        if not claim["citations"]:
            reasons.append("no citation")
        for citation in claim["citations"]:
            answer = answers[question_key(citation, default_file)]
            label = f"{citation['tool']} {citation['id']}"
            if answer["status"] != "ok":
                reasons.append(f"{label}: question {answer['status']} ({answer['detail']})")
                continue
            table = answer["findings"] if citation["id"].startswith("fi-") else answer["evidence"]
            verdict = table.get(citation["id"])
            if verdict is None:
                reasons.append(f"{label}: not in the fresh report")
            elif verdict not in KEPT:
                reasons.append(f"{label}: {verdict}")
            else:
                kinds.append(verdict)
        verdicts.append({
            "id": claim["id"],
            "verdict": "rejected" if reasons else "confirmed",
            "basis": None if reasons else ("supported" if all(k == "supported" for k in kinds) else "derived"),
            "reasons": reasons,
        })
    return verdicts


def check(inputs, claims_path, out, *, enabled=frozenset(), jobs=2, runner=default_runner, timeout=QUESTION_TIMEOUT):
    inputs, out = Path(inputs), Path(out)
    _require(inputs.is_dir(), "--inputs must be an existing directory")
    _require(not out.exists() or (out.is_dir() and not any(out.iterdir())), "--out must be new or empty")
    default_file, claims = load_claims(claims_path)
    keys = sorted({question_key(c, default_file) for claim in claims for c in claim["citations"]})
    _require(len(keys) <= MAX_QUESTIONS, f"at most {MAX_QUESTIONS} distinct questions per check")
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    answers = {}
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, jobs)) as pool:
        futures = {pool.submit(run_question, key, number, inputs=inputs, out=out, enabled=enabled,
                               runner=runner, timeout=timeout): key for number, key in enumerate(keys, 1)}
        for future in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures):
            answers[futures[future]] = future.result()
    hashes = {a["input_sha256"] for a in answers.values() if a["status"] == "ok"}
    verdicts = judge(claims, default_file, answers)
    summary = {"claims": len(verdicts), "confirmed": sum(v["verdict"] == "confirmed" for v in verdicts),
               "rejected": sum(v["verdict"] == "rejected" for v in verdicts), "questions": len(keys),
               "input_sha256": sorted(hashes)}
    questions = [{"question": json.loads(key), **{k: v for k, v in answers[key].items()
                                                   if k not in ("findings", "evidence")}} for key in keys]
    (out / "verdicts.json").write_text(json.dumps({"summary": summary, "claims": verdicts, "questions": questions},
                                                  indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return summary, verdicts


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Re-run every cited ReverseAI question and keep only claims "
                                                 "whose citations resolve in the fresh reports.")
    parser.add_argument("--inputs", required=True, help="Directory of approved inputs (as given to reverseai mcp)")
    parser.add_argument("--claims", required=True, help="Claims JSON written by the team")
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="New or empty directory for verdicts.json and the reports")
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=2, help="Questions run at the same time (default 2)")
    for tool in TOOLS:
        parser.add_argument("--with-" + tool, action="store_true", help=f"Enable the contained {tool} tool")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    enabled = frozenset(tool for tool in TOOLS if getattr(args, "with_" + tool))
    try:
        summary, verdicts = check(args.inputs, args.claims, args.out, enabled=enabled, jobs=args.jobs)
    except UsageError as error:
        print(f"hive_check: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    for verdict in verdicts:
        if verdict["verdict"] == "rejected":
            print(f"REJECTED {verdict['id']}: " + "; ".join(verdict["reasons"]))
    print(f"{summary['confirmed']}/{summary['claims']} claims confirmed from {summary['questions']} fresh questions")
    if len(summary["input_sha256"]) > 1:
        print("warning: citations resolved against more than one input", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0 if summary["rejected"] == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/host_proof.py`:

```py
"""Prove the current checkout on this host: the whole suite, then its wheel built, installed offline and run.

Usage (from the repository root, also the manual CI's only step):
    python -B tools/host_proof.py --receipt NEW_FILE

Nothing is downloaded and no sample is run. steps() is the one implementation of the proof steps; the Linux
container proof (tools/linux_proof.py --inside) calls it too. In a scratch directory: the whole suite on the
checkout, pip wheel --no-index --no-deps from a copy (no sdist), a fresh venv (bin/ or Scripts\\) with the wheel
installed --no-index, then the installed reverseai answers --version, its import path, doctor --json, analyze and
query --out of one code-built ELF; on Windows also tests.test_windows_output. The receipt names the commit
(git rev-parse HEAD), Python, platform, machine and every step's exit and output tail; it is written to a new file,
printed on one line after the marker REVERSEAI-HOST-PROOF and appended to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when that is set.
POSIX passes when every step exits 0 and the whole suite runs clean; Windows when the install, version, doctor,
fixture, analyze, query and Windows report tests pass, the whole suite's counts being recorded without gating.
Every command is an argv list; nothing goes through a shell.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath, PureWindowsPath
import platform
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MARKER = "REVERSEAI-HOST-PROOF "
SUITE_SECONDS = 1200
STEP_SECONDS = 300
TAIL_LINES = 40
POSIX_STEPS = ("suite", "wheel", "venv", "install", "version", "imported_from", "doctor", "fixture", "analyze",
               "query")
WINDOWS_STEPS = POSIX_STEPS[1:] + ("windows_tests",)
# Writes the code-built ELF with imports (tests/fixtures_structure.py) to the path in argv[1]; inert bytes, never run.
FIXTURE = ("import sys\nfrom tests import fixtures_structure as F\n"
           "open(sys.argv[1], 'xb').write(F.elf_imports()[0])\n")
# Environment that could point Python or pip at other code or an index; the proof passes --no-index anyway.
DROPPED_ENV = ("PYTHONPATH", "PYTHONHOME", "PYTHONSTARTUP", "PIP_INDEX_URL", "PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL", "PIP_FIND_LINKS",
               "PIP_CONFIG_FILE")
PIP_ENV = {"PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR": "1", "PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK": "1", "PIP_NO_INPUT": "1",
           "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"}


def as_text(value):
    return value.decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(value, bytes) else (value or "")


def run(argv, *, timeout, cwd=None, env=None):
    """(exit code, stdout, stderr) of one argv, always as text; a timeout gives exit code None."""
    try:
        done = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, text=True,
                              errors="replace", timeout=timeout, shell=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as expired:
        # TimeoutExpired keeps the bytes read so far even with text=True.
        return None, as_text(expired.stdout), as_text(expired.stderr)
    return done.returncode, done.stdout, done.stderr


def tail(text, lines=TAIL_LINES):
    return as_text(text).splitlines()[-lines:]


def suite_counts(stderr):
    """Counts from unittest's closing lines: {"ran", "skipped", "failures", "errors", "ok"}, or None."""
    ran = re.findall(r"^Ran (\d+) tests? in ", stderr, re.M)
    last = stderr.rstrip().splitlines()[-1] if stderr.strip() else ""
    status = re.fullmatch(r"(OK|FAILED)(?: \(([^)]*)\))?", last)
    if not ran or status is None:
        return None
    counts = {"ran": int(ran[-1]), "skipped": 0, "failures": 0, "errors": 0, "expected_failures": 0,
              "unexpected_successes": 0}
    for item in filter(None, (status.group(2) or "").split(", ")):
        key, _, value = item.partition("=")
        key = key.replace(" ", "_")
        if key not in counts or not value.isdigit():
            return None
        counts[key] = int(value)
    counts["ok"] = status.group(1) == "OK"
    return counts


def clean(counts, *, at_least=1):
    return bool(counts and counts["ok"] and counts["ran"] >= at_least
                and counts["failures"] == counts["errors"] == counts["unexpected_successes"] == 0)


def venv_programs(venv, windows):
    scripts, suffix = (venv / "Scripts", ".exe") if windows else (venv / "bin", "")
    return scripts / ("python" + suffix), scripts / ("reverseai" + suffix)


def reports(folder):
    if not (folder / "report.json").is_file():
        return None
    document = json.loads((folder / "report.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return {"input_sha256": document["input"]["sha256"], "summary": document["summary"],
            "reports": sorted(path.name for path in folder.iterdir())}


def steps(runner, work, source, env, *, windows=False):
    """Run the proof steps in the empty directory work; return the facts (platform facts are the caller's)."""
    facts = {"steps": {}}
    record = facts["steps"]

    def step(name, argv, *, timeout=STEP_SECONDS, cwd=None):
        code, out, err = runner(argv, timeout=timeout, cwd=cwd, env=env)
        out, err = as_text(out), as_text(err)
        record[name] = {"exit": code, "timed_out": code is None, "stdout": tail(out), "stderr": tail(err)}
        return code, out, err

    _, _, err = step("suite", [sys.executable, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests", "-t", "."],
                     timeout=SUITE_SECONDS, cwd=source)
    facts["suite"] = suite_counts(err)
    record["suite"]["failed_tests"] = [line for line in err.splitlines() if line.startswith(("FAIL: ", "ERROR: "))][:50]
    build, dist, venv, scratch = work / "build", work / "dist", work / "venv", work / "run"
    facts["venv"] = str(venv)
    shutil.copytree(source, build, symlinks=True, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(".git", "__pycache__"))
    scratch.mkdir()
    code, _, _ = step("wheel", [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "wheel", "--no-index", "--no-deps", "--wheel-dir",
                                str(dist), str(build)])
    wheels = sorted(dist.glob("reverseai-*-py3-none-any.whl")) if code == 0 else []
    if len(wheels) != 1:
        facts["wheel"] = None
        return facts
    data = wheels[0].read_bytes()
    facts["wheel"] = {"name": wheels[0].name, "size": len(data), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}
    if step("venv", [sys.executable, "-m", "venv", str(venv)])[0] != 0:
        return facts
    python, reverseai = (str(path) for path in venv_programs(venv, windows))
    if step("install", [python, "-m", "pip", "install", "--no-index", "--no-deps", str(wheels[0])])[0] != 0:
        return facts
    code, out, _ = step("version", [reverseai, "--version"], cwd=scratch)
    facts["version"] = out.strip() if code == 0 else None
    code, out, _ = step("imported_from", [python, "-I", "-c", "import reverseai; print(reverseai.__file__)"],
                        cwd=scratch)
    facts["imported_from"] = out.strip() if code == 0 else None
    code, out, _ = step("doctor", [reverseai, "doctor", "--json"], cwd=scratch)
    try:
        facts["doctor"] = json.loads(out) if code == 0 else None
    except ValueError:
        facts["doctor"] = None
    sample = scratch / "input.elf"
    if step("fixture", [sys.executable, "-B", "-c", FIXTURE, str(sample)], cwd=source)[0] != 0:
        return facts
    step("analyze", [reverseai, "analyze", str(sample), "--out", str(scratch / "report")], cwd=scratch)
    facts["analyze"] = reports(scratch / "report")
    step("query", [reverseai, "query", str(sample), "--query", "list_segments", "--arg", "limit=16", "--out",
                   str(scratch / "query")], cwd=scratch)
    facts["query"] = reports(scratch / "query")
    if windows:
        _, _, err = step("windows_tests", [sys.executable, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_windows_output", "-v"],
                         cwd=source)
        facts["windows_tests"] = suite_counts(err)
    return facts


def inside_venv(path, venv, windows):
    pure = PureWindowsPath if windows else PurePosixPath
    return bool(path and venv) and pure(venv) in pure(path).parents


def passed(facts, version, *, windows=False):
    """POSIX: every step exit 0 and a clean whole suite; Windows: the install-to-query steps and the Windows tests,
    every one of them run (unittest's count includes skips, so a skip fails). Both need doctor's JSON object to say
    host_ok true for the expected version."""
    record = facts.get("steps") if isinstance(facts.get("steps"), dict) else {}
    required = WINDOWS_STEPS if windows else POSIX_STEPS
    both = ["report.json", "report.md"]
    doctor, windows_tests = facts.get("doctor"), facts.get("windows_tests")
    return bool(all((record.get(name) or {}).get("exit") == 0 for name in required)
                and (clean(windows_tests) and windows_tests["skipped"] == 0 if windows else clean(facts.get("suite")))
                and isinstance(doctor, dict) and doctor.get("host_ok") is True and doctor.get("reverseai") == version
                and facts.get("wheel") and facts.get("version") == "reverseai " + version
                and inside_venv(facts.get("imported_from"), facts.get("venv"), windows)
                and (facts.get("analyze") or {}).get("reports") == both
                and (facts.get("query") or {}).get("reports") == both)


def expected_version(source):
    found = re.search(r'^__version__ = "([^"]+)"$', (source / "reverseai/__init__.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                      re.M)
    if found is None:
        raise SystemExit("the checkout names no reverseai.__version__")
    return found.group(1)


def host_env():
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key not in DROPPED_ENV}
    env.update(PIP_ENV)
    return env


def prove(receipt, runner=run, *, source=ROOT, windows=None):
    """Run every step here, write the receipt, print the marker line; 0 only when the host's predicate passes."""
    windows = os.name == "nt" if windows is None else windows
    version = expected_version(source)
    code, out, _ = runner(["git", "-C", str(source), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], timeout=30)
    commit = out.strip() if code == 0 and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", out.strip()) else None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reverseai-host-proof-") as work:
        # Resolved, so the venv path matches the import path Python reports (macOS /var is /private/var).
        facts = steps(runner, Path(work).resolve(), source, host_env(), windows=windows)
    ok = commit is not None and passed(facts, version, windows=windows)
    document = {"commit": commit, "expected_version": version, "os": "windows" if windows else os.name,
                "python": platform.python_version(), "platform": platform.platform(), "machine": platform.machine(),
                "passed": ok, **facts}
    text = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True)
    with open(receipt, "x", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        stream.write(json.dumps(document, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print(MARKER + text)
    summary = os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY")
    if summary:
        with open(summary, "a", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            stream.write(f"### ReverseAI host proof: {'passed' if ok else 'FAILED'}\n\n```\n{MARKER}{text}\n```\n")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--receipt", type=Path, required=True, help="A new file for the JSON receipt")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.receipt.exists() or args.receipt.is_symlink():
        parser.error("--receipt must name a new file")
    return prove(args.receipt)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`tools/linux_proof.py`:

```py
"""Prove one commit on Linux arm64: the whole suite, then its wheel built, installed offline and run.

Usage (from the repository root, with docker-desktop reserved):
    python3 -B tools/linux_proof.py --commit REV --receipt NEW_FILE

Nothing is pulled or downloaded. The digest-pinned python:3.12-slim base must already be present locally. The
commit's Git-tracked files (git archive, no host mount) are added to a throwaway image FROM that base, with no RUN
step; the container runs as 65534:65534 with the network off, a read-only root, every capability dropped and a tmpfs
at /tmp. Inside, this file runs again with --inside from the archived copy and runs the steps of tools/host_proof.py (one implementation): the whole suite on
the read-only tree, then pip builds the wheel from a copy in /tmp (pip wheel --no-index, no sdist), a fresh venv
installs it with --no-index, and the installed reverseai answers --version, doctor --json, analyze and query of a
code-built ELF. The
inside run prints one marker line of JSON; the host writes the receipt (Python version, platform, commit, counts,
base digest) and removes its image and container whatever the outcome. Every command is an argv list; nothing goes
through a shell.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import importlib.util
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import re
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import uuid

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PLATFORM = "linux/arm64"
BASE_DIGEST = "sha256:16bf2b5c59a08523519d3c8589deca849285dee1d62a3653e124c3dba340f15e"
BASE = "python:3.12-slim@" + BASE_DIGEST
SOURCE = "/opt/src"
MARKER = "REVERSEAI-LINUX-PROOF "
DOCKERFILE = (f"FROM {BASE}\n"
              "ADD source.tar /opt/\n"
              "USER 65534:65534\n"
              f"WORKDIR {SOURCE}\n"
              f'ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "-B", "{SOURCE}/tools/linux_proof.py", "--inside"]\n')
DOCKER_SECONDS = 120
RUN_SECONDS = 1800


def _host_proof():
    """tools/host_proof.py, the one implementation of the proof steps, loaded by path from this file's folder."""
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("reverseai_host_proof", Path(__file__).with_name("host_proof.py"))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


H = _host_proof()
as_text, run, tail, suite_counts = H.as_text, H.run, H.tail, H.suite_counts
REQUIRED_STEPS = H.POSIX_STEPS


# --- inside the container -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def inside(runner=run, work=Path("/tmp"), source=Path(SOURCE)):
    """Run the shared steps inside the container with a fixed environment; add the container's own facts."""
    env = {"PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin", "HOME": str(work / "home"), "LANG": "C.UTF-8", **H.PIP_ENV}
    (work / "home").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    facts = {"python": platform.python_version(), "platform": platform.platform(), "machine": platform.machine(),
             "uid": os.getuid()}
    facts.update(H.steps(runner, work, source, env))
    return facts


# --- on the host ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_argv(context, iidfile, tag):
    return ["docker", "build", "--platform", PLATFORM, "--pull=false", "--network=none", "--iidfile", str(iidfile),
            "--tag", tag, str(context)]


def run_argv(image_id, name):
    return ["docker", "run", "--rm", "--init", "--pull", "never", "--name", name, "--platform", PLATFORM,
            "--network", "none", "--read-only", "--cap-drop", "ALL", "--security-opt", "no-new-privileges",
            "--user", "65534:65534", "--pids-limit", "1024", "--memory", "4g", "--memory-swap", "4g",
            "--tmpfs", "/tmp:rw,exec,nosuid,nodev,size=2g", image_id]


def remove_argv(image_id):
    return ["docker", "image", "rm", "--no-prune", image_id]


def marker_facts(stdout):
    lines = [line for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith(MARKER)]
    if len(lines) != 1:
        raise ValueError("the container printed no single proof marker")
    facts = json.loads(lines[0][len(MARKER):])
    if not isinstance(facts, dict):
        raise ValueError("the proof marker is not an object")
    return facts


def passed(facts, version):
    """The host predicate, on Linux aarch64, Python 3.12, uid 65534, with every packaged lock loading from the venv."""
    doctor = facts.get("doctor")
    return bool(facts.get("machine") == "aarch64" and str(facts.get("platform", "")).startswith("Linux-")
                and str(facts.get("python", "")).startswith("3.12.") and facts.get("uid") == 65534
                and H.passed(facts, version)
                and doctor and doctor.get("host_ok") is True and doctor.get("reverseai") == version
                and len(doctor.get("tools", ())) == 5
                and all(tool["lock_loads"] and tool["lock"].startswith("/tmp/venv/") for tool in doctor["tools"]))


def utc():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def absent(runner, kind, ref):
    """True only when Docker answers that this container or image does not exist; silence is not absence."""
    code, out, err = runner(["docker", kind, "inspect", "--format", "{{.Id}}", ref], timeout=30)
    return code not in (0, None) and "no such" in (as_text(out) + as_text(err)).lower()


def remove_container(runner, name, *, attempts=10, pause=1.0):
    """Force-remove the owned, generated container name (--rm may still be removing it); never another name."""
    for _ in range(attempts):
        runner(["docker", "rm", "--force", name], timeout=30)
        if absent(runner, "container", name):
            return True
        time.sleep(pause)
    return False


def prove(commit, receipt, runner=run, *, pause=1.0):
    """Build, run and remove the throwaway image; write the receipt; return 0 only when every step passed.

    After the base check every outcome writes a receipt, and every exit, interrupts included, first removes the
    owned container (once its run started) and any image the build named, then checks that Docker no longer knows
    them."""
    code, out, _ = runner(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "rev-parse", "--verify", commit + "^{commit}"], timeout=30)
    if code != 0 or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", out.strip()):
        raise SystemExit("the commit does not resolve in this repository")
    commit = out.strip()
    if runner(["docker", "image", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Id}}", BASE], timeout=30)[0] != 0:
        raise SystemExit("the pinned base " + BASE + " is not present locally; this tool never pulls")
    started, image_id, facts, error, version, docker_exit = utc(), None, None, None, None, None
    name = "reverseai-linux-proof-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]
    run_started = False
    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reverseai-linux-proof-") as temporary:
            context = Path(temporary)
            archive = context / "source.tar"
            code, out, _ = runner(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "show", commit + ":reverseai/__init__.py"], timeout=30)
            found = re.search(r'^__version__ = "([^"]+)"$', out, re.M) if code == 0 else None
            version = found.group(1) if found else None
            if version is None:
                error = "the commit names no reverseai.__version__"
            elif runner(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "archive", "--format=tar", "--prefix=src/", "-o", str(archive),
                         commit], timeout=120)[0] != 0:
                error = "git archive failed"
            else:
                (context / "Dockerfile").write_text(DOCKERFILE, encoding="ascii")
                iidfile = context / "image.id"
                code, _, err = runner(build_argv(context, iidfile, "reverseai-linux-proof:" + commit[:12]),
                                      timeout=DOCKER_SECONDS)
                # An image the build named is ours to remove even when the client then failed.
                named = iidfile.read_text(encoding="ascii").strip() if iidfile.exists() else ""
                image_id = named if re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", named) else None
                if code != 0 or image_id is None:
                    error = f"docker build failed (exit {code}): " + " | ".join(tail(err, 5))
        if error is None:
            run_started = True
            docker_exit, out, err = runner(run_argv(image_id, name), timeout=RUN_SECONDS)
            try:
                facts = marker_facts(out)
            except ValueError as problem:
                error = str(problem)
            if docker_exit is None:
                error = "the container did not finish within the time limit"
            elif docker_exit != 0:
                error = f"docker run exited {docker_exit}: " + " | ".join(tail(err, 5))
    finally:
        container_removed = not run_started or remove_container(runner, name, pause=pause)
        if image_id is not None:
            runner(remove_argv(image_id), timeout=DOCKER_SECONDS)
        image_removed = image_id is None or absent(runner, "image", image_id)
    ok = (error is None and docker_exit == 0 and facts is not None and passed(facts, version)
          and container_removed and image_removed)
    document = {"commit": commit, "platform": PLATFORM, "base": BASE, "base_digest": BASE_DIGEST,
                "expected_version": version, "image_id": image_id, "image_removed": image_removed,
                "container": name, "container_removed": container_removed, "docker_exit": docker_exit,
                "started": started, "ended": utc(), "passed": ok, "error": error, "inside": facts}
    with open(receipt, "x", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        stream.write(json.dumps(document, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    suite = (facts or {}).get("suite") or {}
    print(f"{'passed' if ok else 'FAILED'}: {commit[:12]} on {PLATFORM}, Python {(facts or {}).get('python')}, "
          f"{suite.get('ran')} tests ({suite.get('skipped')} skipped), container removed: {container_removed}, "
          f"image removed: {image_removed}" + (f"; {error}" if error else ""))
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--inside", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    parser.add_argument("--commit", help="The candidate commit or tag")
    parser.add_argument("--receipt", type=Path, help="A new file for the JSON receipt")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.inside:
        print(MARKER + json.dumps(inside(), sort_keys=True))
        return 0
    if not args.commit or args.receipt is None:
        parser.error("--commit and --receipt are required")
    if args.receipt.exists() or args.receipt.is_symlink():
        parser.error("--receipt must name a new file")
    return prove(args.commit, args.receipt)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`tools/reverseai_build.py`:

```py
"""Dependency-free PEP 517 backend; also: python tools/reverseai_build.py wheel|sdist."""

import argparse
import ast
import base64
import csv
import gzip
import hashlib
import io
from pathlib import Path
import stat
import subprocess
import tarfile
import tomllib
import zipfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TOOLS = ("lief", "yarax", "ghidra", "jadx", "jsparser")
SOURCE_DIRS = ("reverseai", "tools", "containers", "docs", "tests", "media")
LICENSE_FILES = ("LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md")
SOURCE_FILES = ("README.md", *LICENSE_FILES, "pyproject.toml")


def _version():
    tree = ast.parse((ROOT / "reverseai/__init__.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for node in tree.body:
        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and any(
                isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == "__version__" for target in node.targets):
            return ast.literal_eval(node.value)
    raise ValueError("Missing ReverseAI version")


def _metadata():
    project = tomllib.loads((ROOT / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["project"]
    version = _version()
    if project["name"] != "reverseai" or project["version"] != version:
        raise ValueError("Inconsistent ReverseAI project identity")
    if project.get("license") != "MIT" or project.get("license-files") != list(LICENSE_FILES):
        raise ValueError("Unsupported project license declaration")
    headers = ("Metadata-Version: 2.4", "Name: reverseai", f"Version: {version}",
               f"Summary: {project['description']}", f"Requires-Python: {project['requires-python']}",
               "Description-Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=UTF-8", "License-Expression: MIT",
               *(f"License-File: {name}" for name in LICENSE_FILES))
    return ("\n".join(headers) + "\n\n").encode("utf-8") + (ROOT / project["readme"]).read_bytes()


def _read(path):
    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"Expected a regular source file: {path.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return path.read_bytes()


def _wheel_files(*, editable=False):
    if editable:
        files = {"reverseai_editable.pth": (str(ROOT.resolve()) + "\n").encode("utf-8")}
    else:
        files = {path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(): _read(path)
                 for path in (ROOT / "reverseai").rglob("*.py") if "__pycache__" not in path.parts}
        for tool in TOOLS:
            files[f"reverseai/_locks/{tool}.json"] = _read(ROOT / "containers" / tool / "image.lock.json")
        files["reverseai/_locks/m2_fixture_v1.json"] = _read(ROOT / "containers/yarax/m2_fixture_v1.json")
    info = f"reverseai-{_version()}.dist-info"
    files[f"{info}/METADATA"] = _metadata()
    files[f"{info}/WHEEL"] = ("Wheel-Version: 1.0\nGenerator: reverseai_build\n"
                             "Root-Is-Purelib: true\nTag: py3-none-any\n").encode("ascii")
    files[f"{info}/entry_points.txt"] = b"[console_scripts]\nreverseai = reverseai.cli:main\n"
    for name in LICENSE_FILES:
        files[f"{info}/licenses/{name}"] = _read(ROOT / name)
    record = f"{info}/RECORD"
    rows = [(name, "sha256=" + base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(data).digest()).rstrip(b"=").decode("ascii"),
             str(len(data))) for name, data in files.items()]
    rows.append((record, "", ""))
    stream = io.StringIO(newline="")
    csv.writer(stream, lineterminator="\n").writerows(sorted(rows))
    files[record] = stream.getvalue().encode("utf-8")
    return files


def _write_wheel(wheel_directory, files):
    filename = f"reverseai-{_version()}-py3-none-any.whl"
    destination = Path(wheel_directory)
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(destination / filename, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=9) as archive:
        for name, data in sorted(files.items()):
            info = zipfile.ZipInfo(name, date_time=(1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0))
            info.create_system = 3
            info.external_attr = (stat.S_IFREG | 0o644) << 16
            info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
            archive.writestr(info, data, compresslevel=9)
    return filename


def build_wheel(wheel_directory, config_settings=None, metadata_directory=None):
    """Build the universal wheel without importing the application or any input."""
    return _write_wheel(wheel_directory, _wheel_files())


def build_editable(wheel_directory, config_settings=None, metadata_directory=None):
    """Expose this trusted checkout through a .pth, retaining the normal metadata."""
    return _write_wheel(wheel_directory, _wheel_files(editable=True))


def _source_files():
    # Only this checkout's index selects files; never consult a parent repository.
    if (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "ls-files", "--stage", "-z"],
                                check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
        entries = []
        for row in result.stdout.split(b"\0"):
            if not row:
                continue
            attributes, raw_name = row.split(b"\t", 1)
            mode, _, stage = attributes.split()
            name = raw_name.decode("utf-8")
            if name not in SOURCE_FILES and name.split("/", 1)[0] not in SOURCE_DIRS:
                continue
            if stage != b"0" or mode not in (b"100644", b"100755"):
                raise ValueError("Source distribution requires regular, resolved Git entries")
            entries.append((name, int(mode, 8) & 0o777))
        return sorted(entries)
    if not (ROOT / "PKG-INFO").is_file():
        raise ValueError("Build the source distribution from a Git checkout or an unpacked sdist")
    paths = [ROOT / name for name in SOURCE_FILES]
    paths += [path for name in SOURCE_DIRS for path in (ROOT / name).rglob("*")
              if path.is_file() and "__pycache__" not in path.parts]
    return sorted((path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(), 0o755 if path.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else 0o644)
                  for path in paths)


def build_sdist(sdist_directory, config_settings=None):
    """Use Git's file list and modes, with deterministic tar and gzip metadata."""
    root = f"reverseai-{_version()}"
    filename = root + ".tar.gz"
    destination = Path(sdist_directory)
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    files = {name: (_read(ROOT / name), mode) for name, mode in _source_files()}
    files["PKG-INFO"] = (_metadata(), 0o644)
    with (destination / filename).open("wb") as output:
        with gzip.GzipFile(filename="", mode="wb", fileobj=output, mtime=0, compresslevel=9) as compressed:
            with tarfile.open(fileobj=compressed, mode="w|", format=tarfile.PAX_FORMAT) as archive:
                for name, (data, mode) in sorted(files.items()):
                    info = tarfile.TarInfo(root + "/" + name)
                    info.size = len(data)
                    info.mode = mode
                    info.mtime = info.uid = info.gid = 0
                    info.uname = info.gname = ""
                    archive.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))
    return filename


def get_requires_for_build_wheel(config_settings=None):
    return []


def get_requires_for_build_sdist(config_settings=None):
    return []


def get_requires_for_build_editable(config_settings=None):
    return []


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("kind", choices=("wheel", "sdist"))
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("dist"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print((build_wheel if args.kind == "wheel" else build_sdist)(args.out))
```
